artigo.texto: Plataformas Broadcast Soluções de Dados e Conteúdos Soluções de Tecnologia A SINEXCEL (300693.SZ) concluiu o envio de todos os sistemas de conversão de energia (PCS) StellaON 1250K para o projeto de armazenamento de energia em baterias de 100 MW/400 MWh 15 de outubro de 2026, às 22:43 VALLENAR, Chile, 15 de outubro de 2026 /PRNewswire/ — A SINEXCEL (300693.SZ) concluiu o envio de todos os sistemas de conversão de energia (PCS) StellaON 1250K para o projeto de armazenamento de energia em baterias de 100 MW/400 MWh da RelyEZ Energy Storage Technology Co., Ltd., no Chile. O sistema de armazenamento de energia de quatro horas, localizado em Atacama, será carregado nos períodos de menor demanda e descarregado nos horários de pico, contribuindo para aumentar a flexibilidade da rede elétrica e melhorar a rentabilidade do projeto. A entrega dentro do prazo apoia a execução do projeto. Em projetos de grande escala no exterior, os cronogramas de produção, inspeção e envio precisam estar rigorosamente alinhados ao andamento das obras no local. A SINEXCEL concluiu o fornecimento de todo o lote de PCS dentro do prazo, ajudando a RelyEZ Energy a manter o cronograma de transporte, instalação, comissionamento e conexão à rede elétrica. Em um projeto dessa escala, atrasos na entrega de um único lote podem comprometer o cronograma de construção. A entrega coordenada reduz as incertezas e ajuda as equipes locais a planejar as próximas etapas do projeto. PCS StellaON 1250K projetado para as condições extremas do Atacama Os equipamentos de energia instalados no Atacama precisam operar em condições ambientais adversas, que podem incluir altas temperaturas, poeira e areia. O PCS StellaON 1250K apresenta eficiência máxima de 99% e eficiência de 98,5% na potência nominal. O equipamento opera em temperaturas de ?40 °C a 60 °C, mantém a potência máxima a 55 °C e conta com grau de proteção IP65. Manter a potência nominal em altas temperaturas ajuda a minimizar a redução de potência e a necessidade de capacidade adicional. A maior eficiência de conversão também reduz as perdas de energia ao longo de ciclos sucessivos de carga e descarga, contribuindo para a estabilidade operacional e a rentabilidade a longo prazo. Expansão da capacidade de atendimento local nas Américas Após o envio, o projeto avançará para as etapas de instalação e comissionamento no local. A SINEXCEL conta com uma equipe dedicada ao atendimento pós-venda na América Latina e sete centros de serviço distribuídos pelas Américas. As solicitações técnicas podem ser respondidas em até 30 minutos. A empresa também oferece suporte 24 horas por dia e garante o fornecimento de peças de reposição em até sete dias. A SINEXCEL já forneceu equipamentos para mais de 17 GW de capacidade de armazenamento de energia, distribuídos por mais de 5.000 projetos, e mantém parcerias com mais de 600 empresas em mais de 60 países e regiões. Após o embarque, o projeto chileno avança para a fase de entrega e implementação no local. A SINEXCEL continuará ampliando sua presença local na América Latina e prestando suporte aos clientes ao longo de todo o ciclo de vida dos projetos. Sobre a SINEXCEL Fundada em 2007, a SINEXCEL é pioneira em armazenamento de energia, carregamento de veículos elétricos e soluções de qualidade de energia. Com 17 GW de capacidade instalada de armazenamento, 200.000 carregadores CC para veículos elétricos e quase 20 milhões de amperes de filtros harmônicos ativos instalados, a SINEXCEL estabelece parcerias com líderes do setor para promover a liberdade energética. artigo.texto: A forklift hums across a massive distribution center floor, powered by a battery pack that doesn't quit when the shift ends. This is the world Electrovaya (ELVA +3.88%) occupies. The company designs and manufactures proprietary lithium-ion energy storage systems for mission-critical industrial applications like material handling, robotics, and defense. Shares trade at $5.02 as of Oct 14, 2026, and are down 31% over the past year. Our proprietary Hidden Gems scoring system assigns Electrovaya an overall Superscore of 71 out of 100, placing it in the Above Average category. The Superscore is an AI-powered score that evaluates a company's overall strength by combining financial performance, product market position, technological capabilities, leadership quality, and relative valuation. It represents the unification of all our scores into a single score for public companies, with five rating bands: Exceptional (90-100), Strong (75-89), Above Average (60-74), Average (40-59), and Cautious (0-39). This score places the company in the top ~28% of every company we score, ahead of roughly 71 out of every 100 firms in our database. The Superscore serves as a data-driven starting point for your research, and this piece breaks down the core strengths and persistent risks that define the current investment thesis. ELVA Electrovaya NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 10/15/26 Why ELVA Has a 71 Superscore - Commercial scaling success: Revenue surged 43% year over year in fiscal 2025, proving the company can successfully transition from R&D-heavy development to high-volume manufacturing. - Operational profitability: Management delivered $3.4 million in net income during fiscal 2025, marking a definitive pivot from the consistent losses that characterized its earlier development phase. - Technology differentiation: Proprietary ceramic-separator battery designs allow for higher safety profiles and longer cycle lives, creating a tangible competitive advantage in mission-critical industrial markets. - Manufacturing expansion: The ongoing ramp-up of the Jamestown, NY gigafactory provides the necessary capacity to fulfill significant repeat orders from Fortune 100 and 500 customers. - Strategic market positioning: The launch of the ElvaPulse 1500 platform targets the rapidly growing demand for data center energy storage, diversifying revenue beyond traditional material handling. Why Is ELVA's Superscore Not Higher? - Stretched valuation multiples: The stock trades at a forward P/E of 58, a valuation level that leaves little margin for error if growth guidance slips or product timing shifts. - Capital intensity risks: Aggressive spending on facility expansion resulted in -$3.6 million in free cash flow on a trailing 12-month basis, necessitating continued reliance on debt and equity financing. - Execution timing sensitivity: The recent move of approximately $5 million in high-voltage system deliveries into fiscal 2027 illustrates how supply chain or project delays can impact quarterly results. - Market saturation hurdles: The company faces intense competition in the energy storage space from entrenched, larger global incumbents who possess significantly more established manufacturing and distribution networks. The company maintains a high return on net tangible assets, which ranks in the top 12% of our database. This means it generates outsize profits on a relatively small base of physical machinery and equipment, a level of efficiency that can turn growth into compounded value for shareholders even when valuation multiples appear elevated. Hidden Gems Database Scores at a Glance Is ELVA Right For Your Portfolio? This stock warrants a closer look if... - You are seeking exposure to high-growth industrial stocks benefiting from the shift toward industrial electrification and robotics. - You value proprietary technology moats, such as specialized battery ceramic separators, that differentiate a company in mission-critical segments. You may want to keep researching before buying if... - You are uncomfortable with the stock market volatility and liquidity risks often inherent in small-cap industrial technology companies. - You prefer companies that generate consistent positive free cash flow rather than those in heavy capital-expenditure phases. The Superscore provides a quantitative baseline, but it is just one signal that must be weighed against your own financial goals and tolerance for the inherent risks of small-cap growth investing. My 5-year prediction for ELVA stock The stock can outperform and deliver high returns over the next five years, given demand for its proprietary battery technology. Power is in short supply, which provides Electrovaya a big tailwind to fuel growth and shareholder returns. The company has achieved six consecutive quarters of positive earnings after years of losses. Management attributes this to its ceramic separator -- a key differentiator over competitors. This separator extends the cycle life of the batteries, particularly in heavy industrial use. Importantly, the improvement in profitability over the past year shows that continued increases in scale can translate into higher margins and earnings. The company's order pipeline is expanding into other markets, such as robotics and stationary energy storage. There are risks. Electrovaya is a very small player going up against large companies developing battery and fuel cell technologies. Executing and winning deals with large Fortune 500 companies will be key to unlocking long-term shareholder returns. The stock trades at a high forward P/E of 58, which prices in a lot of growth. If it can deliver on analysts' expectations for 55% annualized earnings growth, the stock could outperform through 2031. Overview: Climb Global Solutions is a value added IT distributor and solutions provider that helps enterprises source servers, storage, software and related data center infrastructure. Operations: Climb Global Solutions generates about $687 million from Distribution and $25 million from Solutions, largely from U.S., U.K., Canadian and European customers. Market Cap: $607 million Climb Global Solutions is involved in the AI data center buildout from the plumbing side, supplying the hardware, software and services that keep expanding workloads running reliably. Climb’s continued expansion across Europe, the U.K. and Sub Saharan Africa, together with management’s stated aim to complete about US$100 million of acquisitions each year and match its North American scale overseas, increases its addressable market and provides more scope to leverage shared back office resources, which can support higher gross billings and operating leverage over time. The key issue for Climb Global Solutions is how that scaling plan interacts with one unseen pressure that could reshape future margins. If that pressure is on your radar, read the full narrative for Climb Global Solutions to see how Climb Global Solutions could be affected and where the upside might still be hiding. Overview: Littelfuse builds protection, control and power components that sit inside data center, grid and transportation hardware, tying it directly into AI infrastructure demand. Operations: Littelfuse generates about US$1.5b from Electronics, US$688 million from Transportation and US$455 million from Industrial, serving customers globally. Market Cap: US$10.2b For AI investors, Littelfuse matters because its high voltage protection hardware sits in the background of data center buildouts that power the theme. Expanding adoption of high voltage architectures in data centers, grid and transportation applications is expected to increase Littelfuse content per system, with management targeting a 25 to 30% data center revenue CAGR over five years and citing 2 to 4 times higher content in future high voltage systems, which can support revenue growth and earnings. The interesting twist is how one shift in customer buying patterns could reshape the earnings payoff investors expect from that extra content. Overview: Super Micro Computer builds high performance, modular servers and storage that power AI data centers and hyperscale cloud deployments worldwide. Market Cap: US$23.5b Super Micro Computer is one of the clearest pure plays on the AI infrastructure buildout because its racks, servers and cooling solutions are designed specifically for dense, GPU heavy data centers that hyperscalers are racing to deploy. "The company's launch and rapid expansion of its Data Center Building Block Solution allows customers to deploy turnkey, energy efficient and customized AI data centers faster than traditional solutions." artigo.texto: Mercado global de sensores de umidade por condutividade térmica: Tamanho, Tendências e Previsão até 2035 - Relatório completo em PDF · pacote de dados Excel · documento Word · apresentação executiva - Entrega por e-mail 24/7, inclusive fins de semana e feriados - Copiar e colar habilitado · formato pronto para impressão - Rodadas ilimitadas de esclarecimentos após a entrega Previsão do mercado de sensores de umidade por condutividade térmica até 2035, impulsionado pela demanda de data centers e da indústria Resumo De acordo com o mais recente relatório da IndexBox sobre o mercado global de sensores de umidade por condutividade térmica, o mercado entra em 2026 com fundamentos de demanda mais amplos, comportamento de compra mais disciplinado e uma arquitetura de oferta mais diversificada regionalmente. O mercado global de sensores de umidade por condutividade térmica entra em uma fase de expansão sustentada, apoiada pela crescente demanda por medição de umidade precisa e durável em data centers, automação industrial, sistemas de climatização automotiva e equipamentos médicos. Diferentemente dos sensores capacitivos de polymer, os sensores de condutividade térmica oferecem medição direta da umidade absoluta, com histerese mínima e desempenho robusto em ambientes agressivos, o que os torna indispensáveis na fabricação de semiconductor, na produção farmacêutica e no controle avançado de HVAC. À medida que a digitalização e as exigências de eficiência energética se intensificam até 2035, espera-se que o mercado cresça a uma taxa composta anual estável, com o índice de mercado subindo de 100 em 2025 para um patamar significativamente mais alto em 2035. Este relatório oferece uma perspectiva baseada em dados sobre tamanho de mercado, segmentação, dinâmica da cadeia de suprimentos e estratégias competitivas, ajudando fabricantes, distribuidores e investidores a navegar por um cenário em evolução. Entre os principais fatores de crescimento estão a expansão de data centers de hiperescala, que exigem controle preciso de umidade para evitar condensação e descargas eletrostáticas, a adoção de regulamentações mais rigorosas de qualidade do ar interior e a integração de sensores de umidade em sistemas de gestão predial conectados à IoT. O ambiente competitivo é moldado por fabricantes de sensores consolidados e empresas de tecnologia especializadas, com foco em miniaturização, saída digital e redução de custos para adoção em massa. O cenário-base para o mercado de sensores de umidade por condutividade térmica entre 2026 e 2035 projeta crescimento robusto, com taxa composta de crescimento anual (CAGR) de 5,8% e índice de mercado atingindo 176 em 2035 (2025 = 100). Essa perspectiva se apoia na adoção acelerada de tecnologias de edificações inteligentes, nas quais os sensores de umidade são essenciais para otimizar o consumo de energia em HVAC e manter o conforto dos ocupantes. No ambiente industrial, o avanço da Indústria 4.0 e da manutenção preditiva impulsiona a demanda por sensores confiáveis e de longa vida útil, capazes de operar em condições extremas. O setor automotivo, em especial a fabricação de veículos elétricos, desponta como aplicação de alto crescimento para sensores de umidade no gerenciamento de baterias e no controle climático da cabine. Regionalmente, a Ásia-Pacífico deve permanecer como o maior e mais dinâmico mercado, sustentada pela fabricação de eletrônicos e pelo desenvolvimento de infraestrutura na China, no Japão e na Coreia do Sul. América do Norte e Europa registrarão demanda constante de reposição e modernização de sistemas existentes, enquanto América Latina e Oriente Médio e África oferecem oportunidades incrementais em monitoramento industrial e agrícola. Restrições na cadeia de suprimentos de componentes especializados e serviços de calibração podem representar desafios temporários, mas, no geral, o mercado está preparado para uma expansão consistente até 2035. artigo.texto: - Gotion Power Morocco plans to begin commissioning its battery-production equipment during the week of 20 October. - The first phase of the Kenitra project represents approximately $1.3 billion in investment. - The factory will manufacture batteries for electric vehicles and energy storage, targeting African and international markets. - A separate partnership with Volkswagen’s PowerCo will produce battery materials in Morocco. Gotion Power Morocco announced on 12 October that equipment commissioning and startup would begin during the week of 20 October at its plant in Kenitra’s Atlantic Free Zone. The company says construction of the cell plant’s buildings and infrastructure is complete. The first phase is designed for 20 gigawatt-hours of annual production capacity, a planned figure rather than current output. The facility will manufacture lithium iron phosphate batteries, commonly known as LFP batteries, for customers in Morocco and elsewhere in Africa, alongside Europe, the Middle East and the United States. According to TelQuel, which reported the company’s statement issued on 12 October, commissioning will open the way to industrial cell production. Gotion Power Morocco chairman Khalid Qalam had previously indicated that sales of assembled batteries were expected before the end of the year. From investment plans to factory operations The announcement gives a more precise timetable for a project whose first production line had already been expected to start in October. Commissioning involves bringing equipment into operation and testing its performance before production can expand. It should not be confused with the factory immediately reaching its full annual capacity. Gotion’s own project information puts first-phase investment at approximately $1.3 billion and identifies a planned capacity of 20 GWh. The next commercial milestones will be consistent production, customer deliveries and the gradual increase in output. Volkswagen adds a European connection The factory’s progress comes as Gotion deepens its partnership with Volkswagen and the German carmaker’s battery subsidiary, PowerCo. On 28 September, the companies announced plans for joint ventures in Spain, Slovakia and Morocco to expand production of LFP battery cells and cathode materials. The proposed Kenitra joint venture will manufacture cathode material, a key battery component. Gotion will hold 51% and PowerCo 49%, with the partners managing the venture together. That materials project is separate from the cell-production equipment scheduled for commissioning this month. Volkswagen’s announcement did not establish an October startup date for the cathode facility. Morocco is attracting investment in both finished battery cells and the materials needed to manufacture them. Why Morocco matters to the supply chain Volkswagen says its partnership with Gotion is intended to diversify supplies and strengthen Europe’s battery industry. LFP technology offers relatively competitive costs, a long service life and durability, making it attractive for more affordable electric vehicles and energy-storage systems. The companies see expanding European demand as an opportunity for their production network. For Morocco, the investment provides an opportunity to move further into battery manufacturing while serving markets beyond its borders. The project has also attracted African development financing. The African Development Bank announced approval of a loan in July to support an integrated battery-manufacturing facility in Kenitra. Its financing documents describe an initial 10 GWh project, whereas Gotion’s broader first-phase description puts capacity at 20 GWh.

artigo.texto: Mercado global de criptografia por hardware: Tamanho, Tendências e Previsão até 2035 - Relatório completo em PDF · pacote de dados Excel · documento Word · apresentação executiva - Entrega por e-mail 24/7, inclusive fins de semana e feriados - Copiar e colar habilitado · formato pronto para impressão - Rodadas ilimitadas de esclarecimentos após a entrega Projeção do Mercado de Criptografia por Hardware até 2035: Crescimento Impulsionado pela Demanda de Data Centers e pela Conformidade Regulatória Resumo Segundo o mais recente relatório da IndexBox sobre o mercado global de Criptografia por Hardware, o mercado inicia 2026 com fundamentos de demanda mais amplos, comportamento de compra mais disciplinado e uma arquitetura de oferta mais diversificada regionalmente. O mercado global de criptografia por hardware entra em uma fase de expansão sustentada, com horizonte de projeção até 2035. A criptografia por hardware, que se baseia em componentes físicos dedicados para executar funções criptográficas, oferece desempenho superior, menor latência e maior resistência à violação em comparação com alternativas baseadas em software. À medida que os volumes de dados aumentam e as ameaças cibernéticas se tornam mais sofisticadas, organizações de diversos setores priorizam uma proteção de dados robusta. Exigências regulatórias como GDPR, HIPAA e CCPA impulsionam a adoção, enquanto a proliferação da computação em nuvem e de borda cria novos vetores de demanda. O mercado abrange unidades de disco com autocrifragem, módulos de segurança de hardware, chips TPM, pen drives criptografados e outros hardwares especializados. Os principais setores de uso final incluem data centers, TI corporativa, governo, serviços financeiros e saúde. O cenário competitivo reúne fornecedores consolidados de semicondutores e armazenamento, além de empresas especializadas em segurança. Esta análise oferece uma visão orientada por dados da dinâmica de mercado, dos fatores de demanda e das considerações estratégicas para os participantes até 2035. O cenário-base para o mercado de criptografia por hardware prevê crescimento constante entre 2026 e 2035, sustentado por fatores estruturais de demanda. A frequência e a gravidade crescentes das violações de dados levam as organizações a adotar a criptografia baseada em hardware como camada fundamental de segurança. Os marcos regulatórios em todo o mundo estão mais rígidos, exigindo criptografia para dados sensíveis em repouso e em trânsito, o que impulsiona diretamente a demanda por soluções de hardware em conformidade. A expansão de data centers e da infraestrutura de nuvem, impulsionada pela transformação digital e por cargas de trabalho de IA, exige criptografia de alto desempenho que somente o hardware é capaz de oferecer. No segmento corporativo, a migração para arquiteturas de confiança zero e a necessidade de proteger ambientes de trabalho remoto são catalisadores adicionais. A adoção de dispositivos de armazenamento criptografados pelos consumidores também cresce, ainda que a partir de uma base menor. Entre os entraves estão os custos iniciais elevados, a complexidade de integração e a escassez de mão de obra qualificada. No entanto, a inovação contínua, como a integração da criptografia aos processadores principais e o desenvolvimento de criptografia pós-quântica, deve atenuar esses desafios. O índice de mercado deve alcançar 185 até 2035, refletindo uma trajetória robusta de expansão. Fatores de Demanda e Restrições Principais Fatores de Demanda - Violações de dados e ameaças cibernéticas crescentes impulsionam a demanda por criptografia de hardware resistente à violação - Exigências regulatórias rigorosas (GDPR, HIPAA, CCPA) que requerem criptografia para dados sensíveis - Proliferação de data centers e infraestrutura de nuvem que exige criptografia de alto desempenho - Adoção de arquiteturas de segurança de confiança zero e tendências de trabalho remoto - Crescimento da eletrônica de consumo com recursos de criptografia integrados - Avanços em algoritmos de criptografia e integração com arquiteturas de computação emergentes Possíveis Restrições ao Crescimento - Custos iniciais elevados e complexidade de integração de soluções de criptografia por hardware - Escassez de mão de obra qualificada para implantação e gestão - Problemas de compatibilidade com sistemas legados e ambientes de TI diversificados - Concorrência de soluções de criptografia baseadas em software em segmentos sensíveis a custos Estrutura de Demanda por Setor de Uso Final Armazenamento em Data Centers (participação estimada: 30%) Os data centers são o maior setor de uso final da criptografia por hardware, impulsionados pelo crescimento exponencial das necessidades de armazenamento de dados e pela demanda por criptografia de alto desempenho e baixa latência. À medida que provedores de serviços em nuvem e empresas ampliam sua infraestrutura de armazenamento, cresce a implantação de unidades de disco com autocrifragem (SEDs) e módulos de segurança de hardware (HSMs) para garantir a proteção dos dados sem comprometer o desempenho. A migração para interfaces NVMe e PCIe acelera ainda mais a demanda por criptografia por hardware, pois essas tecnologias exigem offload criptográfico eficiente. A conformidade regulatória, como o GDPR e exigências específicas do setor, obriga os operadores de data centers a implementar criptografia para dados em repouso. Até 2035, espera-se que a adoção de SEDs se torne padrão no armazenamento corporativo, enquanto os HSMs terão demanda crescente para gestão de chaves e aceleração criptográfica. O avanço da computação de borda e do 5G também criará novos nós distribuídos de data centers que exigirão criptografia. Entre os indicadores do lado da demanda estão a capacidade de armazenamento embarcada, os gastos com infraestrutura de nuvem e o ritmo de construção de data centers. artigo.texto: Fortescue has delivered its first-ever large-scale Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) to North Star Junction (NSJ), marking a major milestone in the company’s mission to decarbonise its Pilbara iron ore operations. This installation is the first in a planned 4-5GWh rollout of large-scale storage systems that will be required to decarbonise Fortescue’s energy supply over the coming years. Powered by BYD’s advanced Blade Battery technology, the NSJ BESS will store renewable energy generated during the day and supply green power to Fortescue’s Pilbara Energy Connect (PEC) network at night. The installation comprises 48 energy storage containers, providing a total capacity of 250MWh and capable of delivering up to 50MW of power for five hours. Designed to provide critical grid stability, the BESS is a major step toward replacing fossil fuelled generation with renewable energy. Fortescue Metals and Operations Chief Executive Officer, Dino Otranto said: “This is a big moment for Fortescue – we’re fundamentally changing the way we power our mines. These systems let us store solar power and use it when we need it most, helping us cut diesel and gas and run our sites on renewable energy.” BYD’s Blade Batteries are engineered for high safety, reliability, and performance, featuring liquid cooling systems designed to operate efficiently in Pilbara temperatures and conditions. Ms Yin Xueqin, General Manager of BYD Energy Storage and New Battery Application, said: “Fortescue is leading one of the most ambitious mining decarbonisation programs in the world, and BYD is proud to support this transformation. “The NSJ BESS is an important milestone for our partnership, and we will continue working closely with Fortescue to deliver the large-scale storage needed to power a green Pilbara.” Fortescue’s next BESS installation will be at Eliwana, with a 120MWh system scheduled for delivery and installation in early 2026. The company is also progressing construction of its 190MW Cloudbreak Solar Farm, which is now almost halfway complete, and has built more than 460 km of transmission lines as part of the PEC project.

artigo.texto: Date: 2026-10-14 04:30:17 Hong Kong, Oct 14, 2026 - (ACN Newswire) - As artificial intelligence (AI) and cloud services grow rapidly, uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems are becoming increasingly important in keeping data centers running reliably. GP Energy Tech Limited (âGP Energy Techâ or theâCompanyâ), a subsidiary of Gold Peak Technology Group Limited (âGold Peakâ) (SEHK: 40), is showcasing its Nickel-Zinc (NiZn) battery system at the Hong Kong Electronics Fair (Autumn Edition), held at the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Center from October 13 to 16. With Manufacturing Twins and Speed to Scale at the core of its approach, the Company is advancing the development and scalable supply of backup power solutions for AI and cloud data centers, as well as other critical infrastructure. As part of its product development efforts, the Company is embracing the promising application of NiZn batteries in UPS systems and battery backup units (BBUs) and is also exploring opportunities to provide backup power for emerging 800-volt direct current (800 VDC) architectures. Speed to Scale: accelerating commercialization through smart manufacturing Drawing on Gold Peak's more than 60 years of experience in battery design, manufacturing and sales, GP Energy Tech is leveraging the Group's expertise in electro-chemistry and high-volume Nickel-based battery manufacturing to advance its NiZn battery systems. Through smart automation and replicable production processes, the Company is accelerating the transition from technology development to commercial application. While maintaining consistent quality and reliable delivery, it flexibly expands manufacturing capacity in line with customer demand, supporting the delivery of NiZn battery solutions at scale to meet growing demand for next-generation backup power. Alan Lo, Executive Vice Chairman of GP Energy Tech said:âThe value of NiZn technology lies in its ability to meet the industry's requirements for safety, power and sustainability simultaneously. By combining this technology with Gold Peak's more than 60 years of manufacturing experience, smart automation and Manufacturing Twins strategy, we are building scalable supply capacity. This is what sets GP Energy Tech apart. The rapid growth of AI and cloud services is creating new requirements for backup power in data centers and other critical infrastructure. We believe solutions that combine safety, high-power density and recyclability will play an important role in data centers. We look forward to working with customers and partners worldwide to advance the adoption of NiZn battery technology in these applications.â Alan Lo (left), Executive Vice Chairman of GP Energy Tech, and Brian Li (right), Vice Chairman and Executive Vice President of Gold Peak, introduce the NiZn battery technology to visitors and explain how it can meet the evolving backup power needs of AI and cloud data centers. Kevin Choi (left), Permanent Secretary for Innovation, Technology and Industry of the Hong Kong SAR Government, visits the GP Energy Tech booth to learn about the company's NiZn battery technology for backup power applications across the entire AI value chain and in cloud data centers. Sophia Chong (left), Executive Director of the Hong Kong Trade Development Council (HKTDC), joins GP Energy Tech's management team for discussion on the development of the innovation and technology industry. Combining safety, high-power density and sustainability Combining non-flammable chemistry, high-power density, a compact footprint, and over 90% recyclability, GP Energy Tech's NiZn battery solution is designed primarily for AI and cloud data centers and is also suitable for other critical infrastructure. It offers operators a backup power option for use with UPS systems. Its water-based, non-flammable electrolyte avoids thermal runaway risk in high-density computing environments, while its high-power density supports more efficient use of space, requiring 74% less floor space per MW than lead-acid systems. Its recyclability also supports resource circularity, enabling operators to balance performance and sustainability when deploying backup power. From cell to cabinet: supporting flexible deployment GP Energy Tech's NiZn battery solution features a modular design built around cells in cylindrical Sub-C format. Each pack contains 128 cells, with nine packs forming a module and ten modules integrated into a cabinet containing 11,520 cells. This architecture allows customers to deploy the solution flexibly according to their UPS system configurations, meeting the backup power requirements of different applications. Exploring applications in UPS systems, BBUs, and emerging 800 VDC architectures To address the power requirements of different applications, GP Energy Tech is further assessing NiZn battery solutions for UPS systems and BBUs, considering power density, system footprint and backup runtime to inform its product development direction. The Company is also actively exploring battery backup opportunities in emerging 800 VDC power architectures as the power infrastructure needs of AI and cloud data centers evolve. Suitability will be further assessed through system-level testing and validation. Advancing commercialization through Manufacturing Twins strategy and industry collaboration GP Energy Tech's Manufacturing Twins strategy brings together manufacturing facilities in China and Malaysia to enhance flexibility in capacity allocation and strengthen supply resilience, providing reliable supply support for customers in different markets. The Company's first NiZn manufacturing facility in Dongguan, China, commenced operations in January 2026 and entered full mass production in mid-June. The first commercial order was delivered in August 2026. The Malaysian facility, part of the Manufacturing Twins strategy, is targeted to open in the third quarter of 2027. artigo.texto: Trina Storage, the energy storage division of Trinasolar, has secured a contract to supply a 50 MW/196 MWh battery energy storage system (BESS) for the AEJ Nozu project in Oita Prefecture, Japan, strengthening its presence in the country’s expanding utility-scale energy storage market. The project, located in Nishihata, Nozu Town, Usuki City, was awarded under Japan’s FY2023 Long-Term Decarbonization Auction and is scheduled for completion in the third quarter of 2028. Under the agreement, Trina Storage will deploy its Elementa 2 Pro 5 MWh battery energy storage solution to support the project’s energy storage requirements. The AEJ Nozu project represents another addition to Trina Storage’s growing portfolio in Japan, where demand for grid-scale battery storage is increasing alongside renewable energy deployment. The company has been expanding its local operational capabilities to support project development, system configuration, technical consultation, delivery coordination and after-sales services. Through its Japan-based team, Trina Storage works with customers and project partners to address local technical specifications and project requirements throughout the development and operational lifecycle. These capabilities are supported by the company’s global expertise in battery cell technology, system integration and utility-scale energy storage solutions. Commenting on the development, Dr. Leo Zhao, Head of Energy Storage (APAC) at Trina Storage, said the company was pleased to contribute to Japan’s expanding renewable energy portfolio through the AEJ Nozu project. He highlighted the opportunities emerging from Japan’s evolving energy requirements and emphasized the importance of combining advanced storage technology with strong local support capabilities. In addition to the Nozu project, Trina Storage is supplying a 160 MWh utility-scale battery energy storage project in Japan’s Kyushu region, further expanding its presence in the market. The company also signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with AMP-lify in September for approximately 1 GWh of grid-connected battery energy storage projects across Japan. The proposed projects will feature Trina Storage’s latest Elementa 3 series energy storage technology. These developments reflect Trina Storage’s continued expansion in Japan’s energy storage sector as the country increases investment in grid flexibility, renewable energy integration and long-duration energy storage infrastructure. With the addition of the AEJ Nozu project and its expanding pipeline of storage developments, Trina Storage is positioning itself to support Japan’s transition toward a more flexible and decarbonized electricity system. artigo.texto: The Lino Lakes City Council continues to have discussions around data centers. At the council’s most recent work session, Community Development Director Michael Grochala reviewed the city’s current land use regulations and provided an overview of data centers. “We’re hearing a lot more about them now,” Grochala said. “They’ve been around for years … but we’re seeing a lot more locally within the Twin Cities Metro Area and as a whole nationally.” What data centers do A data center is a facility that houses computer servers and related equipment used to process, store and distribute digital information. Grochala said data centers support cloud computing, artificial intelligence, data storage, online applications and other digital services. Unlike a typical office or commercial building, a data center is designed primarily to operate computer equipment. These facilities generally run continuously and require reliable electrical power, cooling systems, network connectivity and backup power, Grochala said. “The city’s zoning ordinance defines a data center as an establishment primarily involved in compiling, storing and maintaining information in digital form using a mainframe computer,” Grochala said. “The definition specifically excludes general business offices, computer-related sales establishments and business or personal service establishments.” Types and sizing considerations Data centers vary in size, ownership and function. Common types include enterprise, colocation and hyperscale facilities (see sidebar for more information). Grochala said the hyperscale data centers are driving concerns and interest. “These are much bigger facilities. These are over 200,000 square feet, some of them getting into the million-square-foot size,” he explained. “… These places are really pushing a lot of data, storing a lot of data and now computing, as AI is expanding.” Because these facilities differ in size, design and operating requirements, the appropriate location depends on the data center’s type and scale, available site infrastructure, surrounding land uses and local regulations. Potential sites may include industrial districts, technology or business parks, areas with existing or planned electrical and high-capacity fiber infrastructure, and locations with adequate water and wastewater infrastructure when water-based cooling is proposed. Under the city’s current zoning code, a data center is a permitted use in the Light Industrial (LI), General Industrial (GI) and Business Campus (BC) zoning districts. The LI district includes high-tech businesses and professional services. The GI district allows general industrial uses and services, including more intensive activities. The BC district supports employment-oriented development, including offices, services, research and development, data centers and light industrial uses. A data center proposed in one of these districts would not require rezoning, Grochala explained. However, the development would still need to comply with all applicable city building and development requirements. The city’s 2040 Comprehensive Plan provides the broader land-use framework for determining whether a proposed data center aligns with the city’s planned development pattern. Each proposal would be evaluated according to its location, design and development characteristics. Data centers may also be subject to state and regional regulations and approvals. Minnesota’s Business First Stop offers a coordinated resource for businesses and project proposers navigating state requirements. Depending on the project, those requirements may address environmental review, water appropriation and use, stormwater and wastewater, air emissions, electric generation or storage, utility interconnection, and building and plumbing standards. The city’s land use review and any applicable state or regional reviews are separate processes. A project must satisfy the requirements of each reviewing authority before the corresponding approvals or permits can be issued. Grochala said Lino Lakes’ location within the metropolitan area, access to major transportation corridors and established business campus and industrial areas may create opportunities for technology-oriented development. The city also participates in the Minnesota Technology Corridor, a regional economic development collaboration among six cities. The corridor encompasses development areas along I-35E and I-35W and identifies more than 1,500 acres of future development potential. According to the city staff report, supporting infrastructure includes proximity to I-35E, a fiber-optic backbone and two electric transmission lines. Council members share feedback, thoughts Council Member Julia Nelson clarified that no company has approached the city about building a data center. “I would be for anything that gives us the most power and control over this,” she added. Council Member Randy Rennaker, who brought this forward for discussion to the council in July, said he wants to make certain the city is protected and has the control of what type of facilities are built in the city. “I have friends and family who live in the city that can’t water their yard on a Monday or a Wednesday,” he added. “Some of these data centers are using exorbitant amounts of water. That’s just not right.” Council Member Chris Lyden asked Grochala if it would be possible to ban data centers in the specific zoning districts. Grochala said staff have not gone down the path of exploring prohibition, but the city could establish standards. There was no formal action taken by the council. It was discussion only.

artigo.texto: O Nordeste estará no centro do debate energético nacional pelos próximos 10 anos e pode atrair quase 30% dos novos investimentos em data centers de grande porte, além de ampliar a produção eólica, fotovoltaica e de gás natural. As perspectivas constam no Plano Decenal de Expansão de Energia (PDE 2036), elaborado pela Empresa de Pesquisa Energética (EPE), sob diretrizes do Ministério de Minas e Energia (MME). Divulgado no último dia 8 para consulta pública, o PDE atribui a atratividade do Nordeste aos data centers à presença de pontos de chegada de cabos internacionais de fibra óptica, à elevada disponibilidade de geração renovável e ao potencial de desenvolvimento econômico regional. Apesar dessas vantagens, o subsistema Sudeste/Centro-Oeste deverá receber a maior parcela dos novos investimentos em grandes data centers, estimada em mais de 65%, enquanto o Sul ficará com os 5% restantes. >> Faça parte do canal do Movimento Econômico no WhatsApp No cenário nacional, os centros de dados ganham importância com a digitalização da economia, a expansão dos serviços de armazenamento e processamento de informações e a disseminação da inteligência artificial. O PDE projeta que o consumo de eletricidade dos data centers no Brasil alcance aproximadamente 30 terawatts-hora (TWh) em 2036. Pelo porte dos novos empreendimentos, a tendência apontada é de busca por conexão direta à rede básica de transmissão. Demanda elétrica do Nordeste cresce acima da média nacional A expansão das atividades de comércio e serviços deverá impulsionar o crescimento da carga elétrica no subsistema Nordeste. O PDE estima avanço médio de 3,7% ao ano entre 2026 e 2036, a maior taxa entre os subsistemas e superior aos 3,3% previstos para o Sistema Interligado Nacional (SIN). Segundo o relatório, a carga global nordestina deverá passar de 14.209 megawatts médios (MW médios) em 2026 para 20.462 MW médios em 2036. Esse indicador reúne o consumo final de eletricidade e as perdas verificadas entre a geração e o atendimento aos consumidores. Com isso, segundo o PDE, os data centers passam a exercer influência crescente sobre o perfil de demanda da classe comercial. Nacionalmente, a participação dessa classe no consumo de eletricidade deverá aumentar de 19% para 24% no período, enquanto a residencial recuará de 32% para 28%. Além dos centros de dados, o planejamento considera novas demandas associadas à produção de hidrogênio por eletrólise, que tendem a ocorrer apenas no segundo quinquênio, devido ao prazo mais longo de maturação dos investimentos, ainda em escala reduzida no horizonte analisado. Transmissão precisa atender novos consumidores e escoar renováveis A instalação de grandes consumidores, como data centers e plantas de hidrogênio, exigirá reforços na transmissão, segundo avaliação da Empresa de Pesquisa Energética. O PDE destaca um estudo para inserção dessas cargas no Nordeste e recomenda o Bipolo Nordeste II, que ampliará a capacidade de exportação de eletricidade da região para Sudeste e Sul. O empreendimento e as obras associadas deverão permitir a conexão de novos projetos de geração, consumo e armazenamento, além de fortalecer a estabilidade da rede e reduzir cortes de geração por restrições de confiabilidade. A redução mais ampla desses cortes, conhecidos como curtailment, também dependerá de armazenamento, resposta da demanda e maior flexibilidade das usinas. Nas simulações do plano, os cortes permanecem em patamar absoluto semelhante ao de 2026 ao longo do horizonte analisado. Trata-se de uma projeção sistêmica, sem previsão específica para regiões ou empreendimentos. Já sobre novos parques eólicos, solares e linhas de transmissão no Nordeste, o estudo indica que será necessário maior atenção aos impactos cumulativos sobre vegetação, fauna, paisagem e acesso das comunidades aos recursos naturais. O relatório também aponta riscos de conflitos pelo uso da água nas termelétricas e de pressão sobre comunidades, infraestrutura e ambientes marinhos nas atividades de petróleo e gás. Projetos de gás somam R$ 7,5 bilhões em infraestrutura As bacias de Sergipe-Alagoas, Parnaíba e Potiguar estão entre as principais contribuições à expansão da produção bruta nacional de gás natural, com uma projeção de atingir 308 milhões de metros cúbicos por dia em 2036. A produção líquida, descontados reinjeção, perdas, queimas e consumo próprio, deverá chegar a 135 milhões de metros cúbicos por dia, com destaque para o Sergipe Águas Profundas (SEAP) e os campos da Bacia do Parnaíba, no Maranhão. No Nordeste, três projetos de infraestrutura reúnem estimativas de aproximadamente R$ 7,5 bilhões. A maior parcela corresponde ao escoamento do SEAP, com R$ 6,8 bilhões, capacidade de 18 milhões de metros cúbicos por dia e operação prevista a partir de 2030. O projeto prevê processamento no ambiente marítimo e injeção direta na malha de transporte, por um gasoduto de 134 quilômetros. Na Bahia, a UPGN Miranga, da PetroReconcavo, tem investimento estimado em R$ 360 milhões e entrada prevista para 2028. A capacidade de processamento será de 950 mil metros cúbicos por dia, expansível a 1,5 milhão. Em Pernambuco, o terminal de regaseificação de GNL de Suape aparece com R$ 350 milhões, capacidade de 14 milhões de metros cúbicos por dia e operação considerada para 2027. Segundo o PDE, a ampliação da oferta de gás pode fortalecer o abastecimento industrial e a flexibilidade do sistema elétrico. Esses benefícios dependem da competitividade do combustível, da execução dos investimentos e das condições regulatórias. artigo.texto: Amwins Global Risks (AGR) is expanding its specialist commercial and industrial (C&I) insurance facility to cover battery energy storage systems (BESS) and electric vehicle charging infrastructure. The facility groups distributed assets under a single program, with deductibles scaled to individual site characteristics rather than to utility-scale norms. The structure is designed for portfolios that sit between the two ends of the existing insurance market: too small for utility-scale terms, too numerous to place site by site. Amwins has offered BESS cover through NARDAC, its specialist energy MGA, since March 2024, with capacity of up to $50 million per location backed by eight Lloyd’s syndicates. The C&I facility does not introduce new BESS cover so much as a new structure for it: a portfolio approach that groups multiple distributed sites under a single programme, with deductibles calibrated to individual asset scale rather than applied uniformly across the portfolio. The BESS insurance market has been expanding, but unevenly. A number of insurers have restricted or withdrawn capacity following battery fires in the UK and overseas, a trend documented by market participants including Allianz UK, which expanded its own BESS underwriting capability in July 2026 partly in response to gaps left by capacity withdrawals. That means brokers face a market where appetite and expertise are not evenly distributed. Allianz UK expanded its own BESS underwriting capability in July 2026, with its head of construction, engineering and energy insurance noting that early engagement with experienced underwriters is increasingly valuable given how quickly the risk landscape is developing. For C&I assets specifically, the challenge is structural as much as technical. Individual sites can be relatively small in value, but developers are assembling portfolios of dozens of them across multiple locations. Applying terms designed for a large utility-scale installation to a single C&I site can produce deductibles that are disproportionate to the asset’s value, making the insurance economically unworkable. The Amwins facility is designed to resolve that by underwriting at portfolio level while still assessing accumulated natural catastrophe exposure across individual locations. “Individual sites can be relatively small, but developers are increasingly building portfolios comprising numerous assets across multiple locations," said Tom Harries, director at Amwins Global Risks and partner at NARDAC. "Bringing those assets together allows us to underwrite them efficiently at portfolio scale, while still recognising the individual risk characteristics of each site.” The facility covers both construction and operational phases, including delay in start-up and business interruption cover. The EV charging component is primarily directed at the US market, where commercial charging infrastructure is being deployed at scale. Amwins Global Risks operates from London and places through the London market, giving US-based developers and their brokers access to London capacity for risks that the domestic US market has been slower to accommodate in structured form. Harries said the addition of BESS and EV charging reflects the increasing convergence of distributed energy technologies, and that the facility is designed to adapt as portfolios grow. “It allows us to focus on monitoring how the portfolio’s natural catastrophe exposure changes as new projects are added and gives developers the freedom to concentrate on building out their portfolios, knowing their insurance program can adapt and grow alongside them.” The C&I expansion follows AGR’s renewal and enlargement of a separate natural catastrophe facility for renewable energy projects in July 2026, which increased available capacity to $50 million per placement from $20 million and broadened cover to all major natural catastrophe perils globally. The two moves extend AGR’s distributed and renewable energy proposition across construction, operation and catastrophe layers within a matter of months.

artigo.texto: Deriva Energy, a Brookfield portfolio company and independent power producer, has closed $280 million in financing for its 302 MW Frontier Energy Storage project in Kay County, Oklahoma. Announced on October 12, 2026, the standalone battery energy storage system is expected to become the largest in the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) region upon completion in late 2027. Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce (CIBC) and KeyBanc Capital Markets served as coordinating lead arrangers and joint bookrunners, with CIBC also acting as administrative agent. Deriva plans to reinvest transaction proceeds into its late-stage renewable energy development pipeline. The project's energy capacity in MWh, storage duration and specific grid services have not been disclosed. artigo.texto: Plataformas Broadcast Soluções de Dados e Conteúdos Soluções de Tecnologia 14 de outubro de 2026, às 12:27 Seja para as equipes criarem redes e infraestruturas corporativas no setor de varejo, saúde, serviços financeiros ou implementarem um data center de IA com velocidade e escala gigantescas, a configuração, a observabilidade e a automação dependem de um registro confiável de qual infraestrutura deve existir e como ela deve operar. Esse registro é o NetBox, disse Kris Beevers, CEO e cofundador da NetBox Labs. O NetBox é usado por empresas como Arm, CoreWeave, Kaiser Permanente e J.P. Morgan Chase para criar, operar e expandir suas redes e infraestruturas. Estamos observando um crescimento enorme, com mais de 90% das principais neonuvens usando o NetBox para projetar e escalar seus datacenters de IA, e esperamos que o NetBox alimente mais de 100 GW de capacidade de datacenters de IA até 2030. O NetBox se torna nativo do NVIDIA DSX OS A NVIDIA fez uma parceria com a NetBox Labs para tornar o NetBox uma fonte nativa de referência para o NVCM, de modo que a configuração de rede no DSX OS venha diretamente do sistema de registro que as equipes de infraestrutura de IA já usam. Isso coloca o NetBox no centro do design, do provisionamento e da operação das implementações de IA em grande escala da atualidade. O NetBox fornece os dados centrais que impulsionam a automação da configuração em todas as malhas de cluster nativas da NVIDIA. Leia mais sobre a Parceria NetBox Labs NVIDIA aqui. Contexto do NetBox em todos os dashboards da Grafana Labs A infraestrutura está produzindo cada vez mais telemetria. Mas a telemetria só mostra o que a infraestrutura está fazendo, não o que ela é: a qual dispositivo uma interface pertence, onde ela está localizada, qual função ela desempenha, quem é o proprietário dela e se ela deveria existir. Atualmente as equipes preenchem essa lacuna manualmente, com scripts ou suposições frágeis. Com a nova parceria da NetBox Labs com a Grafana Labs, o NetBox registra como a infraestrutura deve ser e a Grafana mostra o que ela está realmente fazendo. O plugin gratuito e de código aberto do NetBox, desenvolvido em colaboração com a Grafana Labs e publicado no catálogo da Grafana, transfere o contexto do NetBox em tempo real (local, função, tenant, rack, proprietário, ciclo de vida) para os dashboards e alertas da Grafana. Ele não exige alterações no pipeline, evita rótulos desatualizados e não adiciona nenhum custo de métrica. Separadamente, a plataforma Orb de código aberto da NetBox Labs agora oferece aos usuários da Grafana Cloud uma nova fonte de fluxo de rede e telemetria de pacotes. A observabilidade das redes e da infraestrutura são casos de uso populares em toda a comunidade da Grafana, e o contexto é o que separa uma parede de métricas das respostas e ações, disse Ash Mazhari, VP de Desenvolvimento Corporativo da Grafana Labs. O NetBox é o sistema de registro em que as equipes já confiam. Com a fonte de dados do NetBox em nosso catálogo e a Orb fornecendo telemetria de rede para a Grafana Cloud, nossos usuários passam a ter um entendimento mais profundo da sua infraestrutura e dos dados de rede. Leia mais sobre a Parceria entre a NetBox Labs e a Grafana Labs aqui. Novos recursos da plataforma NetBox Labs para pessoas e agentes de IA Além das parcerias, a NetBox Labs também anunciou várias novas adições à plataforma de Inteligência de Infraestrutura da NetBox Labs. Leia mais sobre Anúncios da Plataforma de Inteligência de Infraestrutura da NetBox Labs aqui. Somente a NetBox Labs oferece uma plataforma abrangente de inteligência de infraestrutura que aborda todas as etapas do ciclo de vida da infraestrutura, com neutralidade de fornecedores, proteções claras para agentes e a confiança dos ambientes mais exigentes do mundo, afirmou o CEO e cofundador Kris Beevers. Os anúncios de hoje sobre o produto da NetBox Labs e as parcerias com a NVIDIA e a Grafana Labs possibilitam às equipes, em qualquer estágio da sua jornada de modernização da infraestrutura, trabalhar com a confiança de quem conta com o apoio da plataforma de inteligência de infraestrutura mais potente do mundo. Estamos muito animados com o que essas parcerias e anúncios de produtos significam para nossos clientes e nossos negócios. Sobre a NetBox Labs A NetBox Labs simplifica todo o ciclo de vida da infraestrutura para os ambientes técnicos mais exigentes do mundo. Ela é a administradora comercial do NetBox, o sistema de registro de infraestrutura de código aberto no qual mais de 10 mil organizações confiam há mais de uma década. A NetBox Labs simplifica a aquisição, a modelagem, a implementação e o gerenciamento de infraestruturas tanto para pessoas quanto para agentes. Sua plataforma de inteligência de infraestrutura é a base de sistemas de missão crítica em empresas como Arm, CoreWeave, J.P. Morgan, Kaiser Permanente e Riot Games. Com sede em Nova York, a NetBox Labs é apoiada pela NGP, Notable Capital, Flybridge, IBM, Salesforce e Two Sigma. Visite https://netboxlabs.com para mais informações. artigo.texto: BYD's Dual Track: A 1,008-Kilometer Flagship at Home, a Nine-Minute Charge for Europe Published on 10/16/2026 at 03:31 | Editorial boerse-global.de Goldman Sachs is keeping its faith in BYD ahead of the company's third-quarter 2026 earnings release, maintaining a buy rating on the H-shares with a target price of 134 Hong Kong dollars. The investment bank expects revenue of 242.936 billion renminbi for the period and net profit of 11.5 billion renminbi. The quarterly report is due on October 29. The stock traded at EUR 8.34 on European exchanges, a modest gain of 0.7% on the day. Since the start of the year, however, the shares are down 22%. They closed the previous session at EUR 8.35, which puts the price 4.0% above the 52-week low. A Flagship Sedan and a Battery Lead Away from the balance sheet, BYD introduced its new flagship sedan, the Da Han, in China on Tuesday. The all-electric model arrives in three variants priced between 235,900 and 275,900 yuan. The longest-range version, a rear-wheel-drive configuration, delivers up to 1,008 kilometers on China's CLTC test cycle. The company also strengthened its hand in the supply business. According to data from China's automotive battery industry association, BYD's battery installations in China climbed to 18.29 gigawatt-hours in September, giving it a 21.09% market share — a slight increase over the previous month — and keeping it in second place behind CATL, the sector leader. Hybrid Exports in Brussels' Crosshairs Trade policy has emerged as a complicating factor. Reuters reported on October 9 that the European Union and China reached a common understanding aimed at moderating the flow of Chinese hybrid and plug-in hybrid vehicles into the bloc. The arrangement could cut imports by several million cars over a four-year span, though negotiators have yet to disclose the details. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying BYD? For BYD, the issue touches a key growth engine, since the group leans heavily on partially electrified powertrains in its international business. The political understanding underscores the pressure on Chinese manufacturers to rethink their European distribution strategies, with local production and pure battery-electric vehicles moving to the fore. Technology is also being deployed to address customer concerns about range and charging times. That strategy was on display at the Paris Motor Show, where BYD unveiled the fully electric ATTO 8. The vehicle uses a flash-charging system that, according to the manufacturer, can take the battery from 10% to 97% in nine minutes. European sales are slated to begin in the first quarter of 2027. Local Assembly, Global Ambitions Alongside the model offensive, BYD is building out overseas manufacturing. Its subsidiary BYD Malaysia signed a letter of intent with Inokom Corporation, which is to handle the assembly of partially disassembled vehicles. The companies did not disclose which models are planned or when production will start. Operationally, volumes remain substantial despite the trade discussions. In September 2026, the group sold 463,561 vehicles with alternative drivetrains. Mixed Signals Ahead of the Numbers Market sentiment has been pulled in different directions. On September 29, JPMorgan downgraded the stock from "overweight" to "neutral" and cut its target price from 124 to 88 Hong Kong dollars, citing weaker domestic demand, rising procurement costs and trade-policy uncertainty. Media reports on Tuesday also weighed on the mood, pointing to discussions about European restrictions on hybrid imports and planned Chinese cuts to export tax rebates. Two dates now anchor the coming weeks. On October 20, BYD plans to begin sales of the second-generation Seagull, for which pre-orders opened just over a week ago. Nine days later, on October 29, investors get their look at the books for the third quarter. Ad BYD Stock: New Analysis - 16 October Fresh BYD information released. What's the impact for investors? Our latest independent report examines recent figures and market trends.

The global market for Battery Electrode Dry Coating Materials is entering a decisive commercialization phase as cell manufacturers scale solvent-free electrode production to cut gigafactory operating costs and meet tightening VOC regulations. Dry coating eliminates solvent recovery systems, reduces energy consumption, and simplifies line footprint, but adoption is gated by a dual qualification burden: electrode performance validation and industrial-scale powder process validation. This creates first-mover advantages for integrated cell makers and specialized material formulators. The supply chain for consistent dry polymer binder powders and tailored conductive additive blends is a critical bottleneck, with scaling of formulated inputs more constrained than active material supply. Pricing power is shifting from per-kilogram material sales to solution-based models bundling formulation, process parameters, and technical support. The economic case strengthens for thick electrodes targeting high-energy-density cells and for solid-state designs where solvent incompatibility makes dry processing a technical necessity. Geographic adoption will mirror gigafactory clusters, while material supply concentrates in specialty chemical hubs, creating new trade dependencies. Under this scenario, the market grows at a 18.5% CAGR from 2025 to 2035, reaching a market index of 545 (2025=100). Dry coating eliminates solvent recovery systems, cutting factory OPEX and floor space, which is critical for high-volume EV battery plants. Currently, dry coating is being piloted for NMC and LFP electrodes, with early adoption by Tesla and other integrated manufacturers. The shift to dry processing is also supported by automakers' sustainability goals, as it reduces VOC emissions and energy use. artigo.texto: The Custer County Board of Supervisors met for less than an hour on Tuesday morning inside the Custer County Courthouse. Following a public hearing late last month which saw no members of the public coming forward, the Board of Supervisors voted unanimously today to adopt the data center regulations recommended to them by the planning commission. Ahead of last week’s public hearing, Zoning Administrator Darci Tibbs explained the process that led to the regulations being drafted. “The purpose of these regulations is to not encourage or attract data centers, but to make sure that if one is proposed in Custer County, we have appropriate standards and safeguards in place to protect the health, safety, and welfare of our citizens, and to protect the ag and rural character of the county,” said Tibbs.” View the full data center regulation document here: Custer County Data Center Regulations The board also voted unanimously to put a 12 month moratorium in place regarding battery energy storage systems. This time period was stated to be so that more time could be given to researching them and to work toward regulations, much like the months long process ahead of the adoption of data center regulations. In board of equalization matters, tax corrections for the years 2023 through 2025 were made to change a stick built home to a mobile home resulting in over $2,000 back to the property owner. A motor vehicle exemption for Custer Care was also approved, at a loss to the county of $16 and change. Levy allocation requests for the upcoming fiscal year were approved unanimously for all subdivisions. View the levy allocations here: 2026-2027 Levies Custer County Sub-divisions County Assessor Elise Taylor came before the board regarding her department’s copier machine, stating that it is starting to show signs of failing. The current copier has been in use since around 2017 or 2018 and is owned, however repairs had become more frequent with parts being harder to find. Taylor said options of a $143 per month lease or purchase over $7,000 were available. Following a discussion about what budget the copier would have to come from and the fact that budgets were just passed and the copiers health was not a concern presented, discussions about its replacement fizzled out. A contract between Central Plains Valuations and the county’s assessor’s office was approved, capped at $8,000. The contract was stated to be the same as it had been since 2021. Supervisor Anne Gibbons was the lone vote of no. With no applications to cross right-of-way received, the meeting was adjourned at 9:52 AM.

artigo.texto: Sodium-Ion Batteries and Storage Flexibility: Why Batteries are not a Bottleneck for a Fully Renewable Energy System Battery technology is frequently framed around a material bottleneck, but a recent study from LUT University researchers suggests that concern may be overstated. According to pv magazine, the analysis examines sodium-ion batteries as a promising alternative to lithium-ion batteries and finds that raw material availability need not constrain the scale of storage required for a fully renewable energy system. The study notes that sodium-ion batteries rely on abundant raw materials beyond the cathode, with hard carbon replacing natural graphite in anodes and aluminum substituting for copper as the anode current collector. Previous energy system simulations pointed to stationary battery demand approaching 75 TWh of capacity by 2050, while mobile batteries were estimated to dominate at up to almost 275 TWh of capacity by mid-century. A ratio of roughly 0.8 kWh of capacity per kW of installed solar PV capacity was identified for a cost-optimized, flexible global energy system run entirely on renewable energy. Including electronics and other applications, total battery demand could exceed 350 TWh of capacity by 2050. A bottom-up assessment spanning cell-level to system-level costs found sodium-ion batteries already close to cost parity with lithium counterparts. System-level costs were estimated at about EUR120 per kWh of capacity in 2025, and applying different learning rates could bring costs down to a range of EUR28.5 to EUR51.9 per kWh of capacity by 2050. The authors conclude that batteries are ruled out as a bottleneck on both raw material and cost grounds. They also note that sodium-ion batteries can serve as a drop-in technology produced on existing lithium-ion production lines. For solar PV prosumers who both produce and consume electricity, batteries are not strictly necessary for a secure supply. A grid connection allows surplus rooftop generation to be fed into the grid and reimbursed, with electricity drawn back during periods of low or no solar yield. Rising grid electricity prices and falling battery costs may nonetheless make adding a battery economically beneficial for optimizing overall energy supply costs. An initial cost-optimization study found that PV-battery systems are widely beneficial for prosumers in terms of total energy supply cost, with electrification of heat via heating rods or heat pumps identified as key. Residential rooftop PV yields about 18% less electricity than ground-mounted systems, yet very low-cost solar PV is not a limitation. Combining with stationary battery storage enables high demand and heat cover ratios globally, and battery capacity optimization depends on whether electric vehicles are included. High benefits were found for cars capable of supplying electricity to the system through vehicle-to-home arrangements. A follow-up study examined whether seasonal hydrogen storage benefits residential PV prosumer systems. Long-term storage was found to play only a niche role for Nordic countries in an off-grid scenario, even with significant cost reduction potential. The updated optimization model showed most regions reaching grid parity by 2035, with more than half having already reached parity in 2020. Batteries were confirmed to play an important role. For on-grid cases, a maximum battery-to-PV ratio of 1.6 to 1.8 kWh of capacity per kW was found, rising to 3 to 4 kWh of capacity per kW in off-grid cases. The electric vehicle fleet is growing quickly worldwide, already accumulating battery capacity on the terawatt-hour scale and driving solar PV capacity demand. Using this capacity for power system balancing is seen as a promising solution for systems with a growing share of variable renewable generation. Smart charging alone provides flexibility by raising electricity consumption during renewable generation peaks and reducing it during deficits. Vehicle-to-grid goes further, turning electric vehicles into distributed battery storage on wheels that can supply electricity to the grid during deficit periods. A study analyzing smart charging and vehicle-to-grid confirmed substantial system benefits. These technologies allow installed utility-scale battery storage capacity to be reduced by about 50%, indirectly lowering critical material use in batteries and reducing the need for other energy storage technologies. Enabling them alone may cut total annual system costs by about 4%. Vehicle-to-grid cannot be free for the system, however. Electric vehicle owners must be incentivized to participate and compensated for battery wear. The role and impact of vehicle-to-grid will depend strongly on the cost of this service, but even at EUR50 to EUR100 per MWh it still provides system benefits. The main challenge is the public infrastructure needed for electric vehicles to charge or feed high-quality AC power into the grid whenever parked, especially during the midday PV generation peak when additional storage capacity is most valuable. Flexibility is needed to mitigate the variability of renewable energy sources arising from their weather-dependent nature. Battery energy storage systems have gained widespread attention as a potential leading technology for this role, with advantages including high energy density, rapid response, reliable power delivery, sustained discharge capability, and geographical independence. Continued reductions in battery manufacturing costs have strengthened the role of battery storage in facilitating renewable energy integration, particularly for solar PV. A comprehensive review of flexibility options across more than 1000 research articles found that compared with other storage technologies, including pumped hydro energy storage, thermal energy storage, and e-hydrogen storage, battery technologies currently offer an attractive combination of rapid response, modularity, efficiency, and technological maturity. artigo.texto: Mercado global de sistemas de armazenamento de energia por ar comprimido (CAES): Tamanho, Tendências e Previsão até 2035 - Relatório completo em PDF · pacote de dados Excel · documento Word · apresentação executiva - Entrega por e-mail 24/7, inclusive fins de semana e feriados - Copiar e colar habilitado · formato pronto para impressão - Rodadas ilimitadas de esclarecimentos após a entrega Previsão do Mercado de Armazenamento de Energia por Ar Comprimido (CAES) até 2035: Crescimento Acelera com a Demanda por Integração de Renováveis Resumo De acordo com o mais recente relatório da IndexBox sobre o mercado global de armazenamento de energia por ar comprimido (CAES), o mercado entra em 2026 com fundamentos de demanda mais amplos, comportamento de compra mais disciplinado e uma arquitetura de oferta mais diversificada regionalmente. O mercado global de armazenamento de energia por ar comprimido (CAES) entra em uma fase de transformação, à medida que os sistemas elétricos de todo o mundo avançam rumo à descarbonização profunda e lidam com a intermitência da capacidade eólica e solar em rápida expansão. Diferentemente do armazenamento em baterias de curta duração, o CAES oferece capacidade de descarga de várias horas a vários dias, o que o torna uma solução atraente para requisitos de armazenamento de energia de longa duração (LDES), cada vez mais críticos para a confiabilidade da rede. O panorama tecnológico vem se diversificando além dos tradicionais projetos diabáticos, com variantes adiabáticas avançadas (AA-CAES), isotérmicas e de armazenamento de energia por ar líquido (LAES) atraindo investimentos significativos em pesquisa e desenvolvimento. Esses sistemas de nova geração buscam eliminar a dependência de combustíveis fósseis, melhorar a eficiência de ida e volta e reduzir as restrições geográficas relacionadas ao armazenamento geológico. O apoio de políticas públicas, incluindo créditos fiscais de investimento e mecanismos de mercado de capacidade em regiões-chave, vem reforçando a viabilidade econômica dos projetos. O mercado também testemunha uma transição de projetos de demonstração isolados para implantações em escala comercial, sustentadas pela queda dos custos de componentes e pelo aumento da expertise em integração de sistemas. Este relatório oferece uma análise baseada em dados do mercado de CAES de 2026 a 2035, abrangendo segmentos tecnológicos, aplicações finais, dinâmicas regionais e estratégias competitivas. Trata-se de um recurso estratégico para concessionárias, fornecedores de tecnologia, investidores e formuladores de políticas que navegam pelo cenário em evolução do armazenamento de energia. O cenário-base para o mercado global de CAES de 2026 a 2035 prevê uma expansão robusta, sustentada pela aceleração da transição global para energias renováveis e pela necessidade correspondente de armazenamento de longa duração. À medida que fontes renováveis variáveis passam a responder por uma parcela crescente da geração de eletricidade, os operadores de rede enfrentam desafios cada vez maiores para equilibrar oferta e demanda, gerenciar o corte de geração e garantir a confiabilidade. O CAES, com sua capacidade de armazenar energia por longos períodos e fornecer inércia síncrona, está bem posicionado para enfrentar esses desafios. Espera-se que o mercado cresça a uma taxa composta de crescimento anual (CAGR) de 15,2% entre 2026 e 2035, alcançando um índice de mercado de 420 (2025=100) até 2035. Esse crescimento será impulsionado por uma onda de anúncios de novos projetos, especialmente em regiões com geologia favorável ao armazenamento subterrâneo e marcos regulatórios de apoio. Projeta-se que os sistemas CAES adiabáticos avançados e isotérmicos conquistem uma parcela crescente das novas adições de capacidade, por oferecerem maior eficiência e operação com zero emissões. No entanto, o mercado continuará enfrentando a concorrência do armazenamento em baterias de lithium-ion, que se beneficia de cadeias de suprimento consolidadas e custos em queda, bem como de outras tecnologias de LDES, como hidrelétricas reversíveis e hidrogênio. Ainda assim, espera-se que a combinação única de escala, duração e flexibilidade operacional do CAES garanta um nicho distinto no futuro mix energético. O período de previsão também verá uma ênfase crescente em sistemas híbridos que integram o CAES à geração renovável e a outros ativos de armazenamento para maximizar valor. Vetores e Restrições da Demanda Principais Vetores de Demanda - Rápida expansão da capacidade de energia renovável variável, especialmente eólica e solar, criando uma necessidade premente de armazenamento de longa duração para gerenciar a intermitência e o corte de geração. - Apoio crescente de políticas públicas e incentivos ao investimento em tecnologias de armazenamento de energia de longa duração (LDES) nos principais mercados, incluindo créditos fiscais e reformas do mercado de capacidade. - Avanços tecnológicos em sistemas adiabáticos, isotérmicos e de armazenamento de energia por ar líquido que melhoram a eficiência, reduzem custos e eliminam a dependência de combustíveis fósseis. - Requisitos crescentes de confiabilidade e resiliência da rede, à medida que eventos climáticos extremos e a infraestrutura envelhecida impulsionam a demanda por energia de reserva e serviços de estabilização da rede. - Queda dos custos de componentes-chave, como compressores, expansores e trocadores de calor, aliada a economias de escala decorrentes de implantações de projetos maiores. - Aumento da demanda corporativa e industrial por gestão de energia no local e soluções de descarbonização, especialmente em setores de uso intensivo de energia.
