artigo.texto: A presidente e diretora de operações da SpaceX, Gwynne Shotwell, apresentou a estratégia da companhia para desenvolver infraestrutura de data centers no espaço como solução direta para a escassez de terrenos, a morosidade no licenciamento ambiental e a saturação da matriz energética terrestre no ano de 2026. A decisão estratégica visa atender à demanda insaciável por capacidade computacional e processamento de inteligência artificial por meio da instalação de servidores em satélites em órbita baixa, alavancando a capacidade própria de lançamento e reduzindo os custos operacionais de resfriamento e geração de energia. Inflação imobiliária e gargalos de infraestrutura no setor terrestre O avanço acelerado do processamento de dados e dos modelos de inteligência artificial gerou uma pressão sem precedentes sobre a infraestrutura física em solo. A instalação de supercomputadores exige grandes extensões territoriais próximas a entroncamentos de fibra óptica e subestações de energia elétrica. Esse movimento desencadeou uma especulação imobiliária severa em hubs tecnológicos globais, onde o valor da terra registrou valorizações extremas. A especulação imobiliária representa apenas uma das barreiras para a expansão de infraestrutura em solo. A obtenção de licenças ambientais, autorizações municipais de zoneamento e alvarás de construção tem imposto prazos operacionais prolongados, atrasando a entrada em operação de novas unidades. Além disso, a conexão de novas cargas à rede elétrica terrestre enfrenta fila de espera acentuada, com operadoras estipulando prazos de até três anos para a instalação de geradores e subestações dedicadas. A saturação das matrizes energéticas locais força companhias de tecnologia a buscarem alternativas fora dos modelos tradicionais de redes públicas de distribuição. A escassez de energia contínua para suportar clusters de alta densidade computacional tornou-se o principal gargalo para a escala da infraestrutura de supercomputação em escala global. Arquitetura orbital e vantagens operacionais do processamento espacial A migração de cargas de trabalho computacionais para a órbita terrestre elimina a necessidade de aquisição de terrenos e contorna as limitações de infraestrutura local. A órbita baixa oferece espaço físico ilimitado para a disposição de ativos computacionais, eliminando completamente os custos imobiliários e os atritos regulatórios municipais associados à construção civil convencional. A eficiência do modelo espacial fundamenta-se na utilização de recursos naturais orbitais para resolver os dois maiores custos de operação de um data center: energia e resfriamento. A captação de energia solar em órbita ocorre de forma contínua, sem a atenuação provocada pela atmosfera terrestre ou pelas variações climáticas. Satélites posicionados em órbitas heliossíncronas mantêm exposição solar permanente, permitindo geração fotovoltaica ininterrupta para alimentar os processadores. Para sustentar o fornecimento de equipamentos para essa infraestrutura, a SpaceX iniciou a construção de uma fábrica dedicada à produção de painéis solares nas proximidades de Austin, no estado do Texas. A verticalização da produção de módulos fotovoltaicos busca garantir o suprimento direto para os novos satélites de processamento, alinhando a fabricação de hardware à capacidade interna de lançamento. - Autonomia energética orbital: Captação fotovoltaica contínua sem interferência atmosférica ou ciclos noite-dia em órbitas específicas. - Arrefecimento por radiação: Utilização do vácuo e do espaço profundo como sumidouro térmico de baixa temperatura, reduzindo a necessidade de insumos líquidos. - Verticalização do transporte: Redução drástica do frete logístico ao utilizar frotas próprias de lançamentos reutilizáveis. - Eliminação de PUE hídrico: Supressão do consumo de água potável para sistemas de resfriamento evaporativo terrestre. O resfriamento dos servidores orbitais é realizado via dissipação radiativa para o espaço profundo, cuja temperatura de fundo aproxima-se do zero absoluto. Ao direcionar radiadores térmicos para o vácuo espacial, o sistema elimina a necessidade de infraestruturas complexas de ar condicionado, chillers ou torres de resfriamento à água, fatores que oneram significativamente a pegada hídrica e energética dos data centers terrestres. Impactos na cadeia de suprimentos e competitividade no mercado de IA A implementação de data centers espaciais altera substancialmente a cadeia global de valor da tecnologia da informação e dos serviços de nuvem. Ao integrar a capacidade de lançamento com a fabricação de hardware solar e a operação de redes de satélites, estabelece-se um modelo de negócios verticalizado focado na oferta de capacidade de processamento de baixa latência e alta densidade. A redução nos custos de infraestrutura física e insumos energéticos permite a oferta de poder computacional a custos marginais reduzidos. Esse fator impacta diretamente empresas que desenvolvem e treinam grandes modelos de linguagem (LLMs), simulações científicas e processamento de dados em larga escala, que passam a contar com uma alternativa viável aos centros de dados continentais saturados. Sob a perspectiva regulatória, a transição para plataformas computacionais espaciais transfere os debates de licenciamento civil para a esfera do direito espacial internacional e da gestão de tráfego orbital. A coordenação de frequências de transmissão de dados e a prevenção de detritos espaciais passam a ser elementos centrais na conformidade operacional dos operadores de infraestrutura em nuvem. Cronograma de execução e projeções do setor computacional O desenvolvimento da infraestrutura de processamento no espaço segue um cronograma estruturado na expansão da capacidade de lançamento e na implantação da fábrica de painéis solares no Texas. artigo.texto: In the race for California’s 46th Congressional District, voters will choose between two candidates with differing perspectives on federal health insurance programs, data centers and more. Rep. Lou Correa, D-Santa Ana, said the rising number of uninsured Americans and the lack of affordable healthcare available to them is a result of President Donald Trump’s administration gutting the Affordable Care Act. Any structural reforms to Medicare and Medicaid can only happen once Congress reverses the cuts that were included in the Big Beautiful Bill budget package, which passed last year, said Correa, 68, who is seeking his sixth term in Congress to represent a district that covers parts of Anaheim, Fullerton and Santa Ana. “We must be more efficient in delivering healthcare services, better coordinated medical data, and more preventive care. We need to ensure that we have a cost-effective, healthy nation,” Correa said in response to a questionnaire from the Southern California New Group. His challenger is David Pan, 62, a Republican and professor of German at UC Irvine. To fix the healthcare programs, Pan said the federal government should look to privatize Medicare and Medicaid, so that private insurance companies approved by and contracted with the federal government would be the sole providers of Medicare and Medicaid benefits. But Pan’s proposal doesn’t stop there. It aligns with how he feels Congress should address rising affordability concerns: The federal government should phase out the country’s welfare and entitlement programs “and use this money to create a universal basic income of $16,000 per year for every individual 21 and older.” He called for monthly payments of $1,000 to all U.S. citizens who are at least 21 years old “and $4,000 per year could be paid into each person’s health savings account.” The savings created by privatizing Medicare and Medicaid would go toward creating this universal basic income, Pan said. “My plan would improve affordability by putting cash directly into people’s bank accounts, reduce fraud and waste in government, and still save over $1 trillion per year over the long term,” Pan said. “We would have a system that provides freedom and equal opportunity to everyone, and in which hard work leads to success.” This isn’t a new platform for Pan. He campaigned on universal basic income in his 2024 congressional bid, losing then to Correa. The two candidates for the 46th Congressional District don’t see eye-to-eye on what the top concern constituents are facing. For Correa, it’s immigration. The ramp-up of federal immigration enforcement since the beginning of 2025 has had a direct impact on the economy, especially in California, Correa said. “California today is the fourth-largest economy in the world. We lead the nation in agriculture and food production, as well as light manufacturing, biomedical, high tech, and high-tech startups, and venture capital. All these industries rely on an immigrant workforce,” Correa said. “Our economy needs immigrant workers to grow, these workers that are being deported.” As for specific policy, Correa said Congress should reform the timeline of when an immigrant can apply for a change in their legal status. Federal law allows for undocumented people to apply for a change to their citizenship if they were in the country before 1972. A bill in the House would change that date, from 1972 to seven years before that application to change citizenship is filed. (That bill, which has no Republican co-sponsors, has stalled in the House Judiciary Committee after it was introduced last year.) Correa would like to see that amendment go even further: “Let’s change the date again to 2019.” Pan, when asked what immigration policy should look like in five years, said the federal government should maintain a secure border. “In addition, we should have ways for people to immigrate legally if they go through proper procedures and are vetted,” he said. “We can establish a pathway to legal residence for law-abiding residents who contribute to our country.” Another area where Correa and Pan differ is their stance on offshore oil drilling and production in California, something the Trump administration has aggressively pushed since taking office last year. Correa, who was first elected in 2016, pointed to his record of opposing these efforts and co-sponsoring legislation to permanently ban offshore drilling off California’s coast. The West Coast Ocean Protection Act would permanently ban oil and gas exploration off the coasts of California, Oregon and Washington. The bill was introduced in April 2025 and referred to the House Committee on Natural Resources, where it has since stalled. While Congress needs to ensure people can afford to fill their gas tanks today, the country needs a “smart, balanced, long-term energy policy” that transitions to favor renewable energy sources, Correa said. “And we must be sure that the food we eat, including seafood, is not contaminated. Accordingly, we must protect our future food supply, and that includes our oceans,” he said. “The threat of offshore oil spills and the threat to our future food supply make offshore drilling unwise.” Conversely, Pan said he would support expanding offshore drilling here, so long as oil companies “think that it would be economically productive.” As long as oil is still comparably efficient with other energy resources, Pan said, “its production should not be suppressed.” But like Correa, Pan acknowledged that energy production must eventually transition to cleaner alternatives. “I support the expansion of all forms of energy that are economically efficient and can diversify our energy production,” he said. “Climate policy should instead focus on carbon taxes, which would generate government revenue and have a real environmental effect.” Correa has similar environmental concerns about data centers. artigo.texto: As of August 2026, Latin America and the Caribbean had approximately 3.4 GW of BESS systems in operation, more than double the 1.68 GW identified in 2025, according to the Latin American and Caribbean Energy Organization (OLACDE). Chile accounts for nearly two-thirds of the total. In line with this scenario, GoodWe presented a new architecture for the commercial and industrial (C&I) segment on October 14th, comprised of the ETR line of hybrid inverters from 50 to 125 kW and the BAT-C battery systems of 208.9 and 261.2 kWh . This initiative aims to expand the scale of projects and, at the same time, allow companies to incorporate energy storage gradually. And the movement won't end there. Andrés Azula , GoodWe 's Solutions Manager for South America—excluding Brazil—announced in an interview with Energía Estratégica that, before the end of 2026, the company will add two more generations of hybrid inverters for the residential and C&I segments. Energy storage already accounts for approximately 60% of GoodWe's sales in South America , and the company aims to increase its share to nearly 80% of revenue. Furthermore, it is currently developing projects with ETR and BAT-C in Colombia, Chile, and Argentina , ranging from around 500 kW to 2 MW of power, with some projects reaching 4 MW dedicated solely to storage . A progressive entry into storage One of ETR's key differentiators is its Battery-Ready architecture. A company can start with photovoltaic generation alone and add batteries later without replacing the inverter , thus reducing the initial investment. According to Azula, the configuration responds to a recurring situation among industrial clients: there is interest in storage, but the investment cannot always be made from the beginning. “Many times they want to install their photovoltaic solar plant and generate savings initially, but then they realize the different applications of storage, such as peak shaving or load shifting . They may initially not have the investment capacity for a system with BESS,” he explained. BAT-C, on the other hand, uses LFP technology and comes in nominal capacities of 208.9 and 261.2 kWh . The battery incorporates liquid cooling, 314 Ah cells, and a declared lifespan of up to 10,000 cycles under the conditions specified by the manufacturer. But one of the central points of the new proposal is the scale that the whole can reach. “We can have a system with a 125 kW inverter and a 261 kWh battery, but we can also have 15 units and four batteries per inverter. That gives us more than one MWh per inverter, and we can exceed 15 MWh in a plant ,” he explained. In C&I, storage is starting to be used not only as backup but also to increase self-consumption, reduce peak demand and shift solar energy produced during the day to nighttime hours . “There are companies that operate 24 hours a day. That solar generation that during the day could be lost due to clipping or sent to the grid, they can store and deliver at night to their loads,” the executive noted. Progress, however, remains contingent on the economic conditions of each market. Azula pointed to access to financing as one of the difficulties in Argentina and regulation as one of the outstanding challenges in Peru, while identifying Chile as one of the markets with the most favorable conditions. Continue reading A case that is already in its second stage GoodWe already has regional experience that allows us to observe this logic in operation. In Cerro Guido, near Torres del Paine, in Chilean Patagonia , the company participated in a project to supply a completely off-grid hotel using a microgrid that combines photovoltaics, batteries and diesel generation. The first phase added 100 kW of power and 200 kWh of storage . Before the installation, the hotel relied on a diesel generator 24 hours a day. Following the initial experience, the owner decided to move forward with an expansion that will bring the system to 200 kW of power and 400 kWh of storage . The case also serves as an example of the phased growth model that GoodWe intends to deepen with its new architecture: starting with a certain capacity and expanding the system according to the evolution of demand. The company is also monitoring two photovoltaic installations of more than 1 MW in Argentina , a ceramic brick factory in Resistencia, Chaco, and a cassava production plant in Misiones, whose owners are already evaluating incorporating storage into existing projects. Next up: ES G3 and ET G3 The presentation of ETR and BAT-C will not close GoodWe's release schedule for 2026. Azula told Energía Estratégica that during the fourth quarter the company will move forward with ES G3 , its new generation of residential hybrid inverters. Among its new features will be direct coupling with generators . It will initially be available in select South American countries while the company completes certification processes and meets protection requirements for other markets. ET G3 will also arrive, aimed at everything from small C&I applications to medium-scale projects, with power outputs from 20 to 50 kW . The new generation will also incorporate direct coupling with diesel generators and improvements in integration, efficiency, and performance. GoodWe anticipates general availability for the South American market during the last quarter of the year. In addition to the equipment upgrade , CEMS Plus 2.0 , GoodWe's new management and monitoring platform, began operating in August, replacing the previous version of CEMS and also integrating SolarGo functions. According to the Goodwe representative, the tool centralizes monitoring and commissioning in a single environment, incorporates greater data processing capacity, and allows for remote tasks that previously required on-site intervention. This enables installers and distributors to manage plants located in different parts of the region from their offices. Thus, the company seeks to cover different levels of a market

artigo.texto: Gasgoo Munich-— Greater Bay Technology has commissioned the industry's first gigawatt-hour-scale solid-state battery line. At an Oct. 13 ceremony at its Nansha headquarters, the company marked the completion of capacity upgrades for mass production. The line was retrofitted from existing capacity to produce cells classified under the national solid-state battery standard GB/T 48093.1-2026. This marks the world's first solid-state battery to roll off a mass-production line with certification from an authoritative third-party lab, according to Dong Yang, chairman of the China Automotive Power Battery Industry Innovation Alliance. Third-party tests showed the cells lost less than 0.5% of their mass after being punctured and continuously baked for six hours in a 120°C vacuum — meeting the national standard GB/T 48093.1-2026 issued in late August. That makes Greater Bay Technology the first company to clear testing under the new benchmark. The first solid-state cells roll off the line. (Image credit: Greater Bay Technology) The cells also passed every safety test under the upcoming GB 38031-2025 standard, which takes effect July 1, 2026. In a nail-penetration test, a steel needle pierced the fully charged cell without triggering a fire or explosion, and the structure remained intact. On the performance front, the batteries use a deep-eutectic-based composite solid electrolyte. Specific energy ranges from 260 to 480 Wh/kg, while cycle life matches conventional cells and supports stable fast charging. Drawing on state-backed R&D, Greater Bay Technology retrofitted and optimized portions of an existing 4 GWh liquid lithium battery line. By upgrading rather than building a heavy-asset plant from scratch, the company bridged the manufacturing gap from liquid to all-solid-state — while retaining the ability to flexibly switch between the two formats. After A-sample cells rolled off the line in April, the gigawatt-hour-scale line was upgraded and commissioned just six months later. At the ceremony, Greater Bay Technology also signed strategic pacts with the Shenzhen Vertical Take-Off and Landing Aircraft Innovation Center and Hubei Liming Lithium Industry. The deals aim to speed up the deployment of solid-state batteries across multiple applications — from electric vehicles and the low-altitude economy to embodied robots and premium energy storage.

artigo.texto: Mercado global de concentrados de eletrólito de ácido fosfórico: Tamanho, Tendências e Previsão até 2035 - Relatório completo em PDF · pacote de dados Excel · documento Word · apresentação executiva - Entrega por e-mail 24/7, inclusive fins de semana e feriados - Copiar e colar habilitado · formato pronto para impressão - Rodadas ilimitadas de esclarecimentos após a entrega Previsão do Mercado de Concentrados de Eletrólito de Ácido Fosfórico até 2035: Demanda por Energia de Backup em Data Centers Impulsiona o Crescimento Resumo De acordo com o mais recente relatório da IndexBox sobre o mercado global de concentrados de eletrólito de ácido fosfórico, o mercado entra em 2026 com fundamentos de demanda mais amplos, comportamento de compra mais disciplinado e uma arquitetura de oferta mais diversificada regionalmente. O mercado global de concentrados de eletrólito de ácido fosfórico entra em uma fase de expansão sustentada, com a demanda projetada para crescer a uma taxa anual composta de 6% a 9% entre 2026 e 2035. Essas formulações especializadas atuam como meio condutor em células a combustível de ácido fosfórico (PAFC), eletrolisadores e outros sistemas eletroquímicos, e seu desempenho é decisivo para a eficiência e a longevidade das unidades instaladas. O vetor de demanda mais poderoso é a implantação acelerada de sistemas PAFC para energia estacionária e backup em data centers e infraestrutura de telecomunicações, onde as exigências de confiabilidade são rigorosas e os ciclos de reposição geram demanda recorrente por concentrados. Os concentrados de alta pureza, que respondem por cerca de 70% a 80% do valor de mercado, alcançam um prêmio de preço de 25% a 40% sobre os graus industriais padrão, graças a limites de impurezas iônicas inferiores a 10 ppm. A oferta permanece concentrada em menos de uma dúzia de fabricantes especializados, com mais de 55% a 65% da capacidade produtiva localizada na América do Norte e na Europa Ocidental. A Ásia-Pacífico, excluindo Japão e Coreia do Sul, continua dependente de importações, embora a capacidade local de mistura e purificação esteja crescendo rapidamente. Ciclos de qualificação de 12 a 18 meses e padrões regulatórios divergentes aumentam a complexidade, mas o panorama geral aponta para um crescimento robusto até 2035. O cenário-base para o mercado de concentrados de eletrólito de ácido fosfórico prevê expansão constante entre 2026 e 2035, sustentada pelo uso consolidado e crescente de sistemas PAFC em aplicações de energia estacionária. Data centers, torres de telecomunicações, hospitais e edifícios comerciais adotam cada vez mais soluções de cogeração (CHP) e energia de backup baseadas em células a combustível para cumprir metas de descarbonização e garantir operações ininterruptas. Isso cria um duplo fluxo de demanda: os volumes de carga inicial para novas instalações e um mercado recorrente de reposição que já representa 30% a 40% das vendas de concentrados em volume. O segmento de reposição é particularmente resiliente, pois a degradação do eletrólito segue ciclos previsíveis, o que dá visibilidade aos fornecedores. Do lado da oferta, a capacidade está concentrada na América do Norte e na Europa Ocidental, mas novas unidades de mistura e purificação na China e na Coreia do Sul vêm reduzindo gradualmente a dependência de importações da Ásia-Pacífico. Espera-se que os preços se mantenham firmes para os graus de alta pureza, com as especificações premium sustentando uma vantagem de preço de 25% a 40% sobre os concentrados industriais padrão. A volatilidade das matérias-primas, ligada aos custos de rocha fosfática e energia, representa riscos de margem, mas contratos de longo prazo e barreiras de qualificação protegem os fornecedores já estabelecidos. A divergência regulatória, especialmente entre o REACH da União Europeia e as normas GB chinesas, pode retardar novos entrantes, mas não ameaça o crescimento geral do mercado. Até 2035, o índice de mercado deve alcançar 185 (2025=100), refletindo uma taxa anual composta de 6,8%. Vetores e Restrições da Demanda Principais Vetores de Demanda - Aumento da implantação de sistemas PAFC para energia de backup em data centers e telecomunicações, impulsionado pela necessidade de eletricidade confiável e de baixa emissão. - Adoção crescente da cogeração (CHP) em edifícios comerciais e hospitais, apoiada por incentivos governamentais e mandatos de descarbonização. - Demanda recorrente de reposição de concentrados de eletrólito, já que as pilhas PAFC instaladas exigem reabastecimento periódico, criando uma receita estável de pós-venda. - Expansão da infraestrutura de hidrogênio e das instalações de eletrolisadores, nas quais eletrólitos de ácido fosfórico são usados em certos processos eletroquímicos de alta temperatura. - Aumento do rigor das especificações de impurezas iônicas em membranas de células a combustível, favorecendo fornecedores de concentrados de alta pureza e elevando as barreiras de entrada. - Regionalização da fabricação de células a combustível na Ásia-Pacífico, sobretudo na China e na Coreia do Sul, impulsionando a capacidade local de mistura e purificação e reduzindo prazos de entrega. Possíveis Restrições ao Crescimento - Volatilidade dos preços do ácido fosfórico como matéria-prima, ligada aos custos globais de rocha fosfática e energia, gerando incerteza de margem e forçando renegociações de contratos. - Ciclos longos de qualificação de fornecedores, de 12 a 18 meses, que limitam o número de fontes viáveis e retardam a entrada de novos graus de concentrado no mercado. - Divergência regulatória entre os principais mercados, especialmente entre o REACH da União Europeia e as normas GB chinesas em evolução, elevando custos de conformidade e atrasando lançamentos de produtos. - Concorrência de químicas alternativas de baterias, como as de íons de lítio e as de fluxo, em algumas aplicações de energia de backup e armazenamento estacionário. - Altos requisitos de capital para manuseio em sala l

artigo.texto: Helios Energy, an international renewable energy and battery storage contractor, is rapidly strengthening its position across the Balkans and Central Europe and aims to establish a long-term presence in key European energy markets. With its own engineering and construction resources, Helios delivers large-scale solar, wind, battery energy storage (BESS), and hybrid projects, positioning itself as a multi-technology engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) partner for Europe’s energy transition. Established in Romania in 2022, Helios has since expanded into Hungary, Italy, Bulgaria, and the United Kingdom. Its Turkish sister company, Doğuhan Energy, which has been active in wind power construction since 1996, provides the technical and operational foundation behind Helios’ expansion across Europe. Doğuhan operates exclusively in Turkey, while Helios is focused on regional and European markets, explains Mehmet Selim Çelik, Commercial Project Manager at Helios Energy. While Romania remains one of its core markets, Helios intends to continue strengthening operations in the Balkans, accelerate growth in Italy, and progressively expand further into Central Europe and other strategic European markets, the company says. Building a long-term position in Italy Italy, in particular, is an important strategic growth market for Helios, where it plans to expand its presence significantly and build long-term relationships with developers, investors, and other energy sector partners. The Italian branch was established in 2024 and has started working on three solar projects this year, according to Çelik. Helios is working on BESS projects in the UK together with a Romanian client Earlier this year, Helios also launched construction on a wind power plant in Bulgaria and began work on BESS projects in the United Kingdom in cooperation with a Romanian client, Çelik said. However, the company’s objective is not simply to enter new countries on a project-by-project basis. Rather, it seeks to establish a sustainable, long-term presence in key European markets. Helios provides EPC, sub-EPC, and balance of plant services across the solar, wind, and BESS sectors. However, rather than focusing on a single technology or market, the company is developing into a multi-technology European energy contractor, capable of supporting increasingly complex renewable energy and BESS developments. The track record includes over 3,000 MW of renewable energy capacity The Group’s track record includes over 3,000 MW of installed capacity, about 1,000 wind turbines, and more than 85 renewable energy projects. The completed renewable energy portfolio currently includes 2,316 MWm of wind, 717 MWp of solar, and 266 MWh of BESS capacity. Focusing on energy storage projects Energy storage is a particularly important component of the company’s project pipeline, with 1,048 MWh of BESS under execution, alongside 261.4 MWm of wind and 270.9 MWp of solar PV projects. The company emphasizes that energy storage is expected to remain a key pillar of its future growth. More than 1 GWh of energy storage capacity is currently under construction Helios’ main BESS projects include Parau in Romania, with a capacity of 156 MWh, implemented in 2025 and 2026. Additionally, Helios is working on the 260.78 MWh Rateşti and 338.64 MWh Parau 2 battery energy storage systems, both in Romania, as well as on the 150 MWh Minety Stonehill BESS in the United Kingdom. In the solar segment, the biggest projects are located in Romania: Rateşti, with a capacity of 154 MWp, realized in 2022, and Parau 2, of 233.74 MWp, launched this year. The Group’s biggest wind projects are in Turkey, while Helios is also working on several large facilities in Southeast Europe, including the 117.6 MW Tuluceşti and 44.8 MW Folteşti wind farms, both in Romania. Combining EPC capabilities with hands-on construction experience Helios’ key distinction from other contractors is its hands-on construction capability. The company does not operate solely as a project manager or subcontractor – it maintains its own engineering and construction resources, specialized machinery, and equipment, giving it greater direct control over quality and overall project delivery, according to the statement. Helios offers comprehensive EPC and sub-EPC services, including the construction of substations, control buildings, and access roads, electrical works for substations and BESS, and the installation of steel mounting structures and solar modules. Helios designs solar and wind power plants and substations, and offers maintenance and support In addition to designing and building power generation facilities and batteries, the company also provides SCADA, CCTV surveillance, and communication systems, as well as preventive, corrective, and predictive maintenance and support to solar and wind power plants. Helios’ technical equipment includes its own fleet of specialized machinery, such as cranes, telehandlers, excavators, and ramming machines. Its capabilities also cover mechanical, electrical, and civil works testing, as well as operation and maintenance (O&M) tools and monitoring equipment such as thermal cameras and drones.

artigo.texto: A White House executive order covering several categories of Chinese-made grid equipment could have a greater impact on battery storage supply chains than on transformers, circuit breakers or inverters, according to a new analysis by Rystad Energy. Executive Order 14421, signed by President Donald Trump on 26 August 2026, covers substation transformers, grid-connected inverters, battery energy storage systems (BESS), high-voltage circuit breakers and generation turbines. However, Rystad Energy notes that US dependence on China in several of these categories has already fallen significantly. The greatest exposure is now in batteries: China supplied 50% of the value of US lithium-ion battery imports in the 12 months to June 2026. “The supply chain problem created by the order falls most squarely on battery storage,” said Geoffrey Hebertson, Senior Analyst, Renewables and Power at Rystad Energy. According to the analyst, transformer and breaker markets had already largely shifted away from Chinese supply before the order was issued, while the battery market has yet to undergo a comparable transition. Source: Rystad Energy Grid Equipment Analysis; Rystad Energy Solar Solution; Rystad Energy Energy Storage Solution China accounts for half of US battery imports Rystad Energy’s analysis shows a significant difference across technologies. China accounted for only around 3% of US transformer imports and less than 1% of high-voltage circuit breaker imports by value in the 12 months to June 2026. In these categories, South Korea, Mexico and Canada together account for 74% of breaker imports and 48% of transformer imports. US reliance on China has also declined in the inverter market. The reported value of Chinese inverter exports to the United States fell by 34% between 2022 and 2025, as the 45X advanced manufacturing production credit supported the relocation of inverter assembly to the US. Rystad Energy expects US inverter manufacturing capacity to reach 126 GW by 2028. The picture is different for battery storage. After China, the next-largest suppliers of lithium-ion batteries are South Korea, with 15% of US imports, and Japan, with 13%, with no single alternative market currently able to match China’s scale. Data centers and AI increase exposure The executive order explicitly links the new security measures to the rapid growth of data centers and artificial intelligence, which are increasing electricity demand and the need for critical power infrastructure. The measure also covers uninterruptible power supply systems (UPS) used to support critical infrastructure, potentially extending its reach to behind-the-meter battery systems deployed at data centers to ensure power resilience. For Rystad Energy, this makes battery storage particularly important under the new policy, as large technology companies require growing volumes of storage to support the expansion of their facilities. December rulemaking will be decisive The final impact of the order will depend on rulemaking due by 24 December 2026. One of the main open questions is how the US Department of Energy will define a Covered Foreign Entity. Rystad Energy warns that a broad interpretation could also affect suppliers assembling equipment in countries such as South Korea or Mexico if they rely on Chinese-controlled components, capital or ownership structures. In that scenario, some of the supply sources currently viewed as alternatives to China could themselves fall under the restrictions. “If ownership is drawn broadly enough to follow Chinese capital into South Korean or Mexican assembly plants, the supply chain the tech industry is currently relying on to keep AI infrastructure buildout on schedule becomes part of the problem,” Hebertson said. Rystad Energy therefore considers the December rulemaking the most consequential stage in determining the true scope of the order, particularly for energy storage and the power infrastructure needed to support the expansion of data centers and artificial intelligence.

artigo.texto: The Dominican Republic finally awarded 325.69 MW of renewable capacity with storage in its public tender EDES-LP-NGR-01-2025 , confirming a substantial reduction from the 600 MW initially planned, as Energía Estratégica anticipated days ago , due to network restrictions. The data also show a significant dispersion in prices , with awarded bids ranging from 0.106 USD/kWh to maximum admissible values of 0.131 USD/kWh , in addition to other blocks at 0.093 USD/kWh and 0.085 USD/kWh , reflecting a process conditioned by multiple variables. The awarded block consists of five projects , with a predominance of photovoltaic solar technology —in some cases combined with storage— and a specific participation of wind energy. Among the winning projects Parque Taíno I stands out, developed by Parque Taíno I, SRL , with 84.70 MW awarded and a price of 0.106000 USD/kWh , positioning itself as the most competitive offer in the process. Next is Parque Solar Botoncillo, from Galileo Energía, SRL , with 44.20 MW at a price of 0.106450 USD/kWh , remaining within the lowest range of offers. Likewise, Mella Solar Power 1 (MSP1), SRL awards 99.00 MW at 0.106998 USD/kWh , consolidating the main block of solar projects with battery storage. For its part, Empresa Generadora de Electricidad Haina (EGE Haina) obtained two awards , including the Esperanza II Solar Park with 48.29 MW at 0.108952 USD/kWh and the Esperanza Wind Park with 49.50 MW at a price of 0.118951 USD/kWh , the latter being the project with the highest price within the awarded block. This set confirms the predominance of solar power in the awarded matrix , although with a slight technological diversification from the inclusion of the wind power project. Continue reading From the preliminary scenario to the cut: how does it impact the market? The contrast with the preliminary results is stark. In April, the market was analyzing a scenario where up to 605.1 MW would be awarded across eight projects , with average prices close to USD 0.108/kWh and a highly competitive curve. That scheme included more than 1500 MW offered , showing a strong oversupply and high investor interest, with multiple developers competing in a tight price range. However, the final award reduces the volume to 325.69 MW , leaving out approximately 280 MW compared to the 605 MW scenario , reflecting a more selective process. In addition to the reduction in capacity, there is a greater dispersion in the awarded prices , which indicates that the selection criteria were not based exclusively on the economic variable. In this sense, the restrictions of the electrical grid emerge as the determining factor behind the result , conditioning the system's capacity to absorb new storage projects. This point is particularly relevant given that it contrasts with recent signals from the Government , which during FES Caribe had anticipated new tenders for more than 800 MWh and a projection of 2000 MW of storage in the medium term . Consequently, the current cut could be interpreted as a temporary technical adjustment , while the country moves forward with adapting its infrastructure for future larger-scale rounds.

artigo.texto: Project doubles capacity of Bocanova site in one of the country's fastest-growing electricity load centers HOUSTON and OAKLAND, Calif., Oct. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Nightpeak Energy announced today the successful financial close and commercial operation of its 150 MW, two-hour duration Bocanova 2 battery storage project in Southeast Texas. The project reached commercial operation on September 17, doubling the Bocanova site's capacity to 300 MW and adding significant flexibility to the ERCOT grid as data centers and other large loads drive rapid growth in electricity demand. Bocanova 2 is the second phase of Nightpeak's battery storage development in Brazoria County, near the Houston metropolitan area. The first 150 MW phase, Bocanova 1, began commercial operation in August 2025. Bocanova 2 uses Tesla's Megapack 2 XL battery storage systems. Operating under a long-term offtake agreement with an investment-grade counterparty, the project was financed through a tax equity bridge loan and construction-to-term loan with MUFG Bank. U.S. Bank provided traditional tax equity. Paris Hays, Co-founder and CEO/CDO, Nightpeak Energy, said, "We're seeing large loads come to the grid at a pace and scale that is fundamentally changing how the power sector plans for new demand. Texas is at the forefront of that growth, and meeting it will require significant new infrastructure as well as resources that can respond quickly as conditions change. With 300 MW now operating at Bocanova, we're putting that kind of flexibility to work in one of the most dynamic power markets in the country. We're grateful to the City of Alvin, Brazoria County, and the local community for their support in bringing Bocanova to life." Since its founding in 2022, Nightpeak has developed and acquired a portfolio of over 1 GW of operating and de-risked capacity spanning gas-fired generation, battery storage and powered land development, and continues to advance an additional pipeline of flexible generation and large-load projects to meet growing demand in the U.S. About Nightpeak Energy Nightpeak Energy develops, owns and operates flexible power generation and large-load enablement assets that help meet growing electricity and AI demand while supporting a reliable, lower-carbon electric grid. Applying a technology-agnostic approach across gas-fired generation, energy storage, renewables, and large-load project types, the company combines generation and load into integrated solutions for its customers. Nightpeak is a portfolio investment of Energy Spectrum Partners VIII, LP, which is an infrastructure-focused private equity fund based in Dallas, Texas. Media Contact Ellie Malone [email protected] SOURCE Nightpeak Energy

Set us as preferred - Proposition 45 would speed environmental review for certain essential projects, supporters say, while opponents warn it could weaken protections. - A central dispute is whether the measure’s provisions for broadband projects could include data centers — an unresolved question legal experts say may ultimately be decided in court. - In Imperial County, a proposed massive data center faced community opposition and legal challenges; some say Proposition 45 could make projects harder to stop once applications are filed. When a county judge put the brakes on what would be the largest data center in California, ruling the whole project needed extensive environmental review, Kristian Salgado was relieved. The community organizer lives in Imperial County, where the nearly 1-million-square-foot facility was proposed. The rural county near the Mexico border struggles with bad air pollution and has one of the state’s highest rates of asthma hospitalization for kids, according to the National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences. One of Salgado’s nephews lives right next to the site and struggles with the respiratory disease. “It just seemed very unusual that a project of this scale, with that many backup generators, could be permitted without requiring any further [analysis] of what that would mean for residents,” she said. Now, Salgado and others who share her concern believe Proposition 45 on the November ballot could roll back their wins. The initiative changes the California Environmental Quality Act, or CEQA, a law intended to inform decision makers and the public about a project’s possible environmental impacts — and mitigate them to the extent possible. Supporters say Proposition 45 will speed up environmental review for essential housing, transportation, water, health, education and other projects, cutting costly delays and passing the savings on to consumers. Opponents say it not only weakens environmental protections for many developments, but will cover potentially polluting ones — including data centers. The Yes on 45 campaign forcefully rejects the data center claim, but independent legal experts are divided. At the heart of the debate is the definition of one of the categories covered by Proposition 45: “broadband internet access projects” or “mass-market retail service … that provides the capability to transmit data to, and receive data from, all or substantially all internet endpoints.” Prop 45 seeks to overhaul the law often blamed for delaying construction and driving up its cost: the California Environmental Quality Act. Dan Dunmoyer, president and chief executive of the California Building Industry Assn., which supports the proposition, was adamant: “We specifically excluded data centers” when crafting the measure. Yet the proposition expressly names certain excluded projects: nuclear energy, high-speed rail, jails and Delta conveyance facilities. Data centers aren’t among them. Dunmoyer maintains that even if they’re not explicitly listed, data centers just don’t fit the measure’s definition. In a Daily Journal op-ed, Rachelle Chong, a former Federal Communications Commission member, similarly argues that the definition refers to internet access bought from a provider like AT&T or Comcast. “A conventional data center ordinarily performs an entirely different function,” she wrote, arguing data centers aren’t in play. But land use attorneys Matthew McKerley and Richard Frank, in another op-ed, say many modern data centers fit the bill because they house equipment used to transmit consumer data to and from the internet. They also highlight conspicuous campaign finance contributions, including $250,000 from Prologis, which developed two data centers in San José. Ethan Elkind, director of the climate program at UC Berkeley Law, said data centers will argue they fit the definition — and then it will be up to the courts to decide. “Anyone telling you that it’s definitely not going to be data centers, they cannot read the future,” he said. “The way they’ve written the language, they can’t provide 100% assurance.” Eric Biber, a UC Berkeley law school professor with expertise in environmental law, pointed to language in the measure requiring it to be interpreted broadly “to afford the fullest possible weight to the interest of, and the approval and realization of, essential projects.” In a blog post, he called it “a thumb on the scale” that could lead courts to conclude that projects should be covered when their eligibility is in doubt. But Ryan Thomason and J. Scott Miller, partners at the law firm Mitchell Chadwick with CEQA expertise, think it’s likely courts would rule otherwise. In an article, they note that the definition used in the measure hews closely to another section of California law, which distinguishes providing internet services from offering content, services and applications online. “Courts generally interpret identical language in related statutes to have the same meaning,” they write. Dunmoyer, of the California Building Industry Assn., stressed that the measure doesn’t overthrow local zoning rules. Opponents are “making it sound like in your backyard will be a data center,” he said. “Well, that doesn’t happen at all by this initiative. That has to happen by a county board of supervisors voting to put a data center in your backyard. And if they decide to do that, this initiative does nothing to expedite that CEQA review.” But what if local officials run afoul of their constituents? In the case of the Imperial Valley Data Center Campus, the roughly 75 acres of unincorporated land where it would go had already been zoned for data centers. artigo.texto: Empresa espanhola Solaria anuncia um investimento de 5 bilhões de euros no Uruguai para centros de dados O megaprojeto prevê gerar 3.100 postos de trabalho durante a fase de construção - até 2029 - e cerca de 1.500 empregos permanentes com o parque pronto Clique aqui e escute a matéria O presidente do Uruguai, Yamandú Orsi, anunciou a assinatura de um acordo com a empresa espanhola Solaria Energía y Medio Ambiente para o desenvolvimento de um parque tecnológico de centros de dados que representará um investimento de 5,7 bilhões de dólares (5,08 bilhões de euros). Trata-se, conforme destacou o governo uruguaio, do maior investimento estrangeiro que o país sul-americano receberá em toda a sua história. O megaprojeto, que operará sob o regime de zona franca, destinará 5,5 bilhões de dólares (4,9 bilhões de euros) à construção de centros de dados com capacidade de 500 megawatts, aos quais se somarão outros 200 milhões de dólares (178 milhões de euros) para instalar 350 megawatts de geração solar fotovoltaica que fornecerão energia renovável ao complexo. As instalações serão desenvolvidas em duas fases e distribuídas de forma descentralizada entre os departamentos de Canelones, San José e Florida, com a previsão de gerar 3.100 postos de trabalho durante a fase de construção - até 2029 - e cerca de 1.500 empregos permanentes assim que o parque estiver em pleno funcionamento. Durante a apresentação do acordo, Orsi caracterizou essa operação como um "sinal do Uruguai para o mundo", que consolida o país como um destino onde "as regras são claras e respeitadas" O presidente atribuiu essa conquista ao "acúmulo positivo" de políticas de Estado mantidas ao longo dos anos por diferentes governos, destacando a estabilidade macroeconômica e jurídica, bem como uma matriz elétrica quase 100% renovável, um fator estratégico que se torna cada vez mais determinante para os grandes investidores internacionais. Com este acordo, a multinacional Solaria consolida sua presença no país sul-americano, onde atua há quase uma década administrando usinas solares nas localidades de Young (Río Negro) e Mercedes (Soriano). Conforme destacou a Presidência do Uruguai, este projeto combina a aposta nacional na inovação tecnológica, a retenção de talentos locais e o desenvolvimento de uma economia digital ligada à preservação ambiental.

artigo.texto: Battery Energy Storage System Plugs into the Smart Grid Enphase Energy introduced its first first commercial battery storage system. The all-in-one, grid-connected IQ Battery C80 will deliver 80 kWh of usable energy capacity and up to 40 kVA of continuous power in a single, compact enclosure, with battery packs and microinverters fully integrated. Available in capacities between 80 kWh to 2 MWh, the system is engineered for commercial, industrial, and multifamily applications where it can support demand charge management, time-of-use shifting, solar self-consumption, and other smart grid services and even participate in virtual power plants (VPPs). All models use active air cooling without the need for liquid cooling or external HVAC, helping simplify installation and improve reliability. Its modular architecture will allow customers to right-size projects and expand storage capacity over time, helping customers manage energy costs and maximize the value of onsite solar generation. The IQ Battery C80 will be available in two three-phase configurations: a 120Y/208 V model delivering 33 kVA for multifamily properties and smaller commercial buildings, and a 277Y/480 V model delivering 40 kVA for larger commercial and industrial applications. Both are based on the lithium iron phosphate (LFP) chemistry, deliver greater than 90% AC round-trip efficiency, and operate across an ambient temperature range of -22°F to 131°F. Shipments of the IQ Battery C80 are expected to begin in the first half of 2027. About the Author Lee Goldberg Contributing Editor Lee is the author of the popular PowerBites series. Lee Goldberg is a self-identified “Recovering Engineer,” Maker/Hacker, Green-Tech Maven, Aviator, Gadfly, and Geek Dad. He spent the first 18 years of his career helping design microprocessors, embedded systems, renewable energy applications, and the occasional interplanetary spacecraft. After trading his ‘scope and soldering iron for a keyboard and a second career as a tech journalist, he’s spent the next two decades at several print and online engineering publications. Lee’s current focus is power electronics, especially the technologies involved with energy efficiency, energy management, and renewable energy. This dovetails with his coverage of sustainable technologies and various environmental and social issues within the engineering community that he began in 1996. Lee also covers 3D printers, open-source hardware, and other Maker/Hacker technologies. Lee holds a BSEE in Electrical Engineering from Thomas Edison College, and participated in a colloquium on technology, society, and the environment at Goddard College’s Institute for Social Ecology. His book, “Green Electronics/Green Bottom Line - A Commonsense Guide To Environmentally Responsible Engineering and Management,” was published by Newnes Press. Lee, his wife Catherine, and his daughter Anwyn currently reside in the outskirts of Princeton N.J., where they masquerade as a typical suburban family. artigo.texto: Brazil's Chamber of Deputies approved the emergency procedure for Bill 3.716/2026 , an initiative that seeks to eliminate the obligation for electricity generators to exclusively bear the costs of contracting energy storage systems. The initiative takes on special relevance in a market that has accumulated 296.8 GW of registered power for the upcoming storage auctions , scheduled for December 2 and 4 of this year, while the Energy Research Company (EPE) projects the incorporation of 7.2 GW of batteries by 2036 . It was approved on October 13, 2026 , allowing the proposal to proceed directly to the plenary session without going through the relevant committees. However, the regulatory change still requires the corresponding legislative approval. The project, presented by deputy Arnaldo Jardim , seeks to repeal section 6 of article 3-A of Law 10.848/2004, incorporated by Law 15.269/2025, which establishes that the costs of contracting storage systems as capacity reserves are distributed exclusively among the generation agents. The legislative document argues that the current regulations establish unequal economic treatment for an infrastructure that benefits the entire National Interconnected System (SIN) , and not exclusively the generation companies. In that sense, the project's rationale argues that the benefits of storage, linked to the security, flexibility and reliability of the system, "go beyond individual interests and reach all agents of the SIN" . The discussion has direct implications for the economic structuring of projects, since a modification of the charge scheme could alter the distribution of financial obligations between generators and consumers. Furthermore, the legislative document states that the contracting of capacity and flexibility services should be governed by criteria of technological neutrality, without establishing differentiated treatment for solutions that offer equivalent performance. In particular, it warns that the application of different financing mechanisms "introduces unjustified regulatory asymmetries, distorts economic signals and compromises comparability between technological alternatives" . According to the initiative, these regulatory differences make it difficult to evaluate the economics of different technologies and can lead to investment decisions that do not reflect the lowest costs for the electricity system as a whole. The rationale summarizes its position with the statement: "Systemic charges require systemic distribution," referring to the need to distribute the economic burdens of an infrastructure whose benefits reach multiple participants. The impact on tariffs and a market projected at 77.2 billion reais One of the most relevant aspects of the project is its questioning of the tariff impact of the current system. Although the costs of contracting storage are formally charged to the generators, the text argues that these costs can be passed on to the prices of the energy sold, with consequences for end consumers. The legislative justification warns that this transfer could lead to "higher rates, less transparency and no guarantee of systemic efficiency" , especially due to the impact of taxes along the electricity chain. In turn, the document points out that imposing exclusively on generators the financing of infrastructure intended to guarantee the reliability of supply creates a problem of proportionality in the allocation of obligations. He even considers the current system to represent an "act of regulatory expropriation" and questions its compatibility with the constitutional principles of equality, legal certainty, and free enterprise. These observations correspond to the legal grounds of the authors of the project and form part of the parliamentary discussion, without constituting a judicial ruling on the validity of the current legislation. The economic magnitude of the debate is also reflected in the projections for the expansion of Brazilian energy storage. According to a sector study cited in the legislative justification, Brazil could reach approximately 71.8 GWh of installed storage capacity between 2025 and 2034 , with cumulative investments of around 77.2 billion reais . Of the total projected, around 42%, equivalent to approximately 36 billion reais , would correspond to the capacity reserve segment integrated into the National Interconnected System. That market is precisely one of the most exposed to the modification of the cost distribution mechanism promoted by Bill 3.716/2026. The same analysis estimates that storage systems could account for 25% of the growth in installed power capacity of the Brazilian electricity matrix during the period. It is important to differentiate these estimates, partially expressed in GWh of accumulated energy capacity, from the power projections in GW presented by the EPE for 2036. Continue reading The legislative proposal argues that repealing the section in question would not create a regulatory vacuum, since Article 3-A already includes a cost distribution mechanism between end users and generation agents. In fact, the document states that "the deletion of section 6 does not create a legislative gap," considering that the general regulations maintain the legal basis for financing capacity reservation services. If approved, the reform would not eliminate the charges associated with battery procurement, but would modify who should assume them, a fundamental distinction to assess its effects on the various participants in the sector. BESS auctions: 296.8 GW of interest, national content and 7.2 GW towards 2036 The acceleration of the legislative debate coincides with preparations for Brazil's first capacity reservation auctions specifically for storage systems. artigo.texto: BENNINGTON, NE. — As U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright visits Nebraska to encourage data center growth, two candidates for the Omaha Public Power District Board's District One seat offer competing visions for regulating projects in northwest Omaha. Wright visited Louisville, Nebraska, addressing data centers in the state and saying he wants to see more communities welcome the projects "It's a community decision," Wright said. "If they think it's a win, great. I think they'd be tremendous." Communities across Nebraska have taken action to either limit or ban data centers in their neighborhoods, often citing concerns about water usage and electricity prices. Sara Kohen and Christian Mapes are running to represent District One on the OPPD board. The district covers large areas of northwest Omaha and Bennington. Both say data centers are here to stay, but the difference is how they would regulate them in northwest Omaha if elected. Kohen says more research is needed first. "I think what we really need is more information," Kohen said. "How much power are these big data centers using, and as members of the public, we actually don't know." Mapes says it's case-by-case. "It depends on how the project is developed, what it costs our electric system, who pays those costs and what the benefits are that (it) brings to the community," Mapes said. Kohen has laid out her steps in what she calls the "Bill of Rights for Nebraska," an eight-step plan to address data centers in northwest Omaha. "I'd like to see them moved into a separate customer class," Kohen said. "Let's see how much power they are using, and then once we see that, we can really make sure they are doing their fair share." Mapes is drawing on his five years working in the energy industry. He says since 2020, OPPD is forecast to grow 100 megawatts annually — the equivalent of roughly 100,000 houses. "Data centers are a large reason for that growth as well, but as people transition to electric vehicles, as they start trading out equipment that used to be gas-powered for electric power, that adds up," Mapes said. The race between Mapes and Kohen will be decided on November 3.

artigo.texto: A scale-up italiana nomeou Brian Turnbow para liderar a sua expansão técnica em inteligência artificial e computação de alto desempenho, com uma estratégia “energy-to-compute” que procura tirar partido de fontes renováveis e reaproveitar ativos existentes para desenvolver infraestruturas de computação mais sustentáveis. TRENTO, Itália, 15 de outubro de 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- A ALPS anunciou a nomeação de Brian Turnbow como Diretor Técnico para IA. Fundada em Trentino em 2018 e hoje presente em quatro continentes, a empresa está a aplicar o seu know-how no desenho, construção e operação de data centers integrados com sistemas energéticos ao segmento de IA e HPC. O acesso à energia é um dos principais fatores limitativos para o desenvolvimento de infraestrutura de IA. Segundo dados da Terna a 31 de agosto de 2026, os pedidos de ligação de data centers à rede em Itália ultrapassavam os 100 GW, face a cerca de 30 GW no final de 2024 — uma subida que torna críticos tanto a escolha dos locais como os prazos de ligação à rede. A abordagem energy-to-compute da ALPS assenta numa decisão estratégica: localizar data centers onde a energia já está disponível, incluindo fora dos grandes hubs, reduzindo a dependência de zonas da rede mais congestionadas. A empresa pretende integrar fontes de energia renovável e reconverter antigos polos industriais desativados, reaproveitando sempre que possível ligações à rede, edifícios e outros ativos existentes. O objetivo é desenvolver uma infraestrutura de computação mais sustentável, alavancando recursos locais e, através da reutilização de ativos, limitando a ocupação de solo e reduzindo a necessidade de novas construções. Esta expansão complementa as operações de mining da ALPS, que continuam em linha com o seu plano de negócios. Turnbow irá liderar a estratégia técnica de IA/HPC da ALPS, desde a avaliação de arquiteturas e localizações até ao relacionamento com parceiros tecnológicos e industriais. Itália será um mercado prioritário. A ALPS pretende trazer de volta ao país a experiência acumulada internacionalmente e colaborar com empresas italianas de engenharia e indústria, também integrando a sua experiência em projetos no exterior. > "A Itália e a Europa dispõem de recursos energéticos, ativos industriais e competências técnicas que podemos valorizar", afirma Francesco Buffa, CEO e cofundador da ALPS. "Com a nossa abordagem energy-to-compute, queremos transformar o potencial energético e industrial das regiões onde operamos numa vantagem competitiva e ajudar a reduzir o fosso da Europa em IA." Com mais de 25 anos de experiência em telecomunicações e infraestrutura digital, Turnbow ocupou funções técnicas na TWT, Unidata e CDLAN. Integra ainda o conselho de administração da ITNOG. > "A infraestrutura de IA começa muito antes da instalação das GPUs", sublinha Brian Turnbow. "Cada projeto tem de partir dos workloads que deve suportar e das necessidades dos clientes, não apenas da potência disponível. O meu objetivo é traduzir esses requisitos em decisões de arquitetura consistentes, construindo capacidade de computação flexível, escalável e sustentável, tirando partido de fontes de energia renovável e de ativos já existentes." Sobre a ALPS A ALPS projeta, constrói e opera data centers para aplicações intensivas em energia e computação, combinando competências em energia com engenharia e operação de data centers. O seu crescimento internacional tem sido apoiado pela Azimut através de uma operação de 40 milhões de euros em 2023 e de um club deal de 105 milhões de euros em 2024. artigo.texto: Câmara aprova urgência de projeto que muda rateio de custos para contratação de baterias elétricas A regra é um dos pontos mais controversos no setor elétrico para a realização do primeiro leilão para contratação de sistemas de armazenamento, previsto para dezembro A Câmara dos Deputados aprovou nesta terça-feira (13) um requerimento de urgência para a análise de projeto de lei que propõe alteração no rateio dos custos para contratação de baterias para armazenar energia elétrica. A regra é um dos pontos mais controversos no setor elétrico para a realização do primeiro leilão para contratação de sistemas de armazenamento, previsto para dezembro deste ano. Na prática, a medida possibilita que a proposta seja votada diretamente pelo plenário da Casa, sem ser analisada por comissões temáticas antes. A votação do mérito, contudo, deverá ficar para depois das eleições. De autoria do deputado Arnaldo Jardim (Cidadania-SP), o projeto revoga alteração legislativa feita no ano passado, que determina que os custos das contratações com baterias seja dividido exclusivamente entre os geradores de energia, conforme regulamentação da Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel). Com a revogação, a avaliação de alguns agentes do setor é de que os custos passariam a ser rateados entre os consumidores. Segundo o autor da proposta, o texto ainda deverá ser negociado com o governo. “Nós iremos aproveitar esse período dessa semana e a outra para arredondar o projeto, avançar no diálogo com o governo para votar após a eleição”, disse o deputado. Na justificativa da proposta, Jardim critica o dispositivo que determina que os custos da contratação de baterias para armazenamento de energia sejam divididos exclusivamente entre as empresas geradoras de eletricidade. Ele afirma que, como consequência, há “distorções relevantes na alocação de custos do setor elétrico” e que isso “compromete a segurança jurídica dos investimentos em geração de energia renovável no Brasil”. Segundo o parlamentar, o enfrentamento dos desafios operativos do Sistema Interligado Nacional (SIN) passa pelo incentivo ao aumento da flexibilidade operativa do sistema. Em nota, a Associação Brasileira de Soluções de Armazenamento de Energia (ABSAE), avaliou que o avanço da proposta é importante para ampliar a segurança jurídica e criar condições mais previsíveis para a realização dos primeiros leilões de baterias em larga escala no Brasil. "A entidade alerta que o cumprimento do cronograma dos leilões é fundamental para que os sistemas de armazenamento estejam disponíveis em 2028. O adiamento dos certames pode comprometer a entrada das baterias em operação no prazo previsto e aumentar o risco de déficit de potência e de apagão em períodos críticos de atendimento."

Summary The transition to 800G and 1.6T networks is creating new challenges for data centers, requiring physical infrastructure that can support higher speeds, increased density, and faster deployment timelines. Join Legrand's experts for a fireside chat exploring the technologies enabling next-generation network architectures, including the evolution of Very Small Form Factor (VSFF) connectivity, silicon photonics, high-density fiber trunks, and color-indexed fiber infrastructure with Chroma Link. We'll discuss how advancements in optical networking and physical layer design are helping data centers simplify installation, accelerate deployment, improve scalability, and build infrastructure ready to support evolving connectivity demands. Whether you're planning a new high-density deployment or upgrading existing network environments, you'll gain practical insights into the physical layer strategies driving the move toward 1.6T.

artigo.texto: Microsoft Weighs 20% Cost Cuts In Azure Vertical Amid Soaring AI Data Center Spending: Report - Girish Bablani, president of Azure's software development group, instructed team leaders to identify ways to lower expenses by at least 20%, The Information reported. - The potential savings aim to help offset heavy capital expenditures for AI data centers and finance higher salaries to retain talent against competitors like Meta and Anthropic. - Scott Guthrie announced an internal restructuring elevating senior executive Arun Ulag to oversee key cloud units. Microsoft Corp.’s (MSFT) cloud business top executives have discussed strategies to cut expenses by at least 20%, reflecting growing pressure on major technology firms to fund artificial intelligence infrastructure. Girish Bablani, president of the Azure group that develops software for cloud servers, recently directed leaders in his roughly 11,500-person division to outline cost-saving proposals, The Information reported, citing people familiar with the matter. While the exact measures remain under consideration and could include parting ways with external contractors, the report did not state categorically whether internal discussions could lead to staff layoffs. However, a Microsoft spokesperson disputed the characterization of planned cuts, saying, "Azure leadership has not directed teams to develop cost-cutting plans. Every responsible company prepares for a range of scenarios and market dynamics, both positive and negative,” according to The Information. Balancing Infrastructure Costs And Talent Retention The potential cost-cutting comes despite strong financial performance for Azure. Microsoft recently disclosed that the cloud unit generated $101.9 billion in revenue for the 12 months ending in June—a 40% year-over-year increase—accounting for approximately 31% of the company's total annual revenue. In the June quarter alone, Azure’s revenue rose 43%. However, the rapid acceleration of AI deployment has driven massive capital expenditure on data center infrastructure, pressuring cash reserves. Similar financial pressures have affected competitors such as Amazon Web Services (AMZN) and Oracle (ORCL), both of which have implemented workforce reductions to protect cash flows amid rising AI expenses. Moreover, competitors like Meta (META) and Anthropic have aggressively targeted Microsoft personnel, forcing executives to offer counteroffers with higher compensation packages. Leadership Restructuring Alongside the cost discussions, Microsoft is reorganizing leadership within its cloud organization. In an internal announcement on Monday, Guthrie revealed that senior executive Arun Ulag will assume broader oversight across key divisions, The Information reported. Ulag, who previously managed Azure's database product line, will now oversee executives responsible for Azure Core—the business providing raw computing capacity to key clients, including OpenAI. His expanded purview includes senior leaders such as Bablani, Billy Anders, Douglas Phillips, Mark Russinovich, and former security chief Charlie Bell. The management shakeup reflects a broader push by Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella to elevate a new generation of leadership as several veteran executives step back or retire. MSFT Stock: Retail View Retail sentiment on Stocktwits was ‘bearish’ with ‘normal’ message volumes. MSFT stock has gained about 12% year-to-date.

artigo.texto: SCOTTSDALE, AZ — Republican Jay Feely and Democrat Amish Shah are locked in a toss-up race for Arizona's 1st Congressional District, which includes Scottsdale. A sharp difference emerged between the two candidates during a recent Clean Elections debate: their views on data centers. Shah, an emergency room physician and former Arizona legislator, said he does not want data centers built in CD-1. He acknowledged the country will need them as artificial intelligence continues to grow, but said voters in the district have made their feelings clear. "When I'm talking to the voters, what they have said to me clearly is they don't want them in CD-1," Shah said. We're all about Scottsdale — the schools, the neighborhoods, the businesses, the decisions being made at City Hall and in the community that affect your daily life. Connect with your community by joining the Your Scottsdale News Facebook Group! Feely, a former NFL player and broadcaster, took a different view, arguing that data centers are important for economic growth. "They add about a billion dollars in revenue to the state of Arizona. That's giving you the opportunity to increase teacher's pay. It's giving you the opportunity to do programs to actually help people," Feely said. Feely said local communities should decide whether they want data centers built in their areas. He also criticized Shah for supporting tax breaks for data centers while serving in the state legislature. "I think it's really hypocritical for you to stand up here and say to the voters that you're now against data centers. When you were in office, you voted for the tax credits to bring those data centers here," Feely said. Shah defended his position, saying when that vote was taken, artificial intelligence was not on the radar. "However, when the situation changes and suddenly you've got massive amounts of people applying as we have seen, and you see that you're going to double the amount of wattage that these things are going to take. You're going to have to think about the ratepayers." The full debate is available on the Clean Elections website. The last day to request an early voting ballot is Oct. 23. Election Day is Nov. 3. CD1 is home to about 820,000 people. The district covers northeast Phoenix along with Scottsdale, Fountain Hills and Cave Creek. Joe Biden narrowly won the district in 2020, and Donald Trump narrowly carried it in 2024.

artigo.texto: Estudo com o CPQD vai identificar áreas com potencial para expansão do setor até 2035 13/10/2026 Fonte: Magnific A Agência Brasileira de Desenvolvimento Industrial (ABDI) e o CPQD estão desenvolvendo um diagnóstico para identificar quais regiões brasileiras apresentam condições para receber novos data centers e quais dependem de investimentos em energia, conectividade e outros serviços essenciais. O levantamento produzirá uma Matriz de Atratividade Territorial e cenários para o setor até 2035. O estudo integra o Projeto ECOS – Data Centers Sustentáveis, iniciativa com duração de 24 meses que também prevê testes de tecnologias para melhorar a eficiência energética e operacional dessas instalações. A proposta é fornecer informações para decisões de investimento, planejamento territorial e formulação de políticas públicas. Além da infraestrutura disponível, serão examinados fatores como recursos hídricos, licenciamento, tributação, disponibilidade de profissionais qualificados e capacidade da indústria nacional de atender à demanda do setor. Matriz apontará potencial e gargalos regionais A Matriz de Atratividade Territorial será uma das principais entregas do diagnóstico. O instrumento deverá identificar localidades com condições para receber empreendimentos e aquelas que precisam de investimentos estruturantes, especialmente em transmissão de energia, telecomunicações e abastecimento de água. O trabalho abrangerá oito dimensões: panorama nacional e internacional; diagnóstico territorial; cadeia produtiva e desenvolvimento industrial; energia, sustentabilidade e infraestrutura; regulação e tributação; capital humano e inovação; soberania digital; e impactos, cenários e recomendações estratégicas. A metodologia combina levantamento de dados, entrevistas com representantes do mercado, consultas ao ecossistema, workshops e análises técnicas. Em setembro, durante a Campinas Innovation Week, em Campinas (SP), o projeto realizou um encontro para colher contribuições de participantes ligados à infraestrutura digital e à inovação. As informações serão incorporadas às demais etapas do levantamento. Além da matriz, estão previstas avaliações de impactos econômicos, sociais, ambientais e tecnológicos, projeções para o período de 2026 a 2035 e um roteiro estratégico para o desenvolvimento do setor. Quer receber notícias da ACAERT? Assine a newsletter - Assine aqui e receba por e-mail Indústria nacional entra no diagnóstico Outra frente do estudo será a identificação de oportunidades para fornecedores brasileiros de equipamentos, tecnologias e serviços associados à implantação e operação de data centers. A análise também considerará formação de profissionais, capacidades tecnológicas nacionais e os efeitos da expansão dessa infraestrutura sobre o desenvolvimento regional. Para o presidente da ABDI, Olavo Noleto, o objetivo é relacionar o crescimento da capacidade de processamento de dados à política industrial. “Com o Projeto ECOS, buscamos gerar inteligência, fortalecer a cadeia produtiva nacional e criar condições para que o crescimento desse setor se converta em desenvolvimento industrial, inovação e soberania para o Brasil”, afirma. Projeto prevê testes de eficiência energética Além do diagnóstico, a parceria entre ABDI e CPQD contempla uma jornada de inovação aberta, na qual empresas de data centers, startups e ambientes de validação poderão desenvolver e testar soluções para problemas operacionais do setor. Entre as tecnologias consideradas estão sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias (BESS), inteligência artificial, automação e ferramentas de monitoramento. As aplicações poderão envolver gestão térmica, redução do consumo de água, integração de fontes renováveis e confiabilidade operacional. Os projetos-piloto deverão gerar dados técnicos sobre desempenho e sustentabilidade das soluções avaliadas. “Com essa jornada, o projeto busca desenvolver modelos e soluções nacionais para o setor, alinhando o avanço tecnológico às metas ESG e posicionando o Brasil como referência na próxima geração de data centers sustentáveis e inteligentes”, afirma Sebastião Sahão Junior, presidente do CPQD. (Com assessoria de imprensa) Repórter: Tele.Síntese
