artigo.texto: Is CATL eyeing the AI business? In the late 19th century, the founders of Standard Oil, the predecessor of ExxonMobil, began buying shares of railway companies in their personal names. Jabez Bostwick, one of the founding partners, later simply served as the president of the New York and New England Railroad Company, while another partner Camden guarded the oil-producing regions for Standard Oil and financed the Ohio River Railway at the same time. Over thirty years, these individual shareholdings quietly formed a network. In 1904, investigative journalist Ida Tarbell wrote the well-known assertion in The History of the Standard Oil Company: Standard Oil "holds shares in most of the large railway systems and has representatives on the boards of directors of almost all major railway systems". At that time, Standard Oil under the management of John D. Rockefeller was the largest crude oil extraction, gasoline and lubricant production enterprise in the United States. For Standard Oil, taking shares in railways could not only ensure that it could obtain cheap and safe oil transportation routes, but also make railway companies themselves major customers for lubricant sales. It can be said that this method guaranteed Standard Oil's position in the industry to a certain extent. The same story is still happening today. On October 6, 2026, Bloomberg, citing people familiar with the matter, reported that DeepSeek's new round of financing is nearing completion, with a scale ranging from 800 billion yuan to 1 trillion yuan. Tencent and CATL have once again become one of the investors with the highest capital contribution. It has been only more than four months since CATL first appeared on DeepSeek's shareholder list. As a leader in power batteries, CATL used to invest its capital in mining, materials and automobile companies: securing supply in the upstream and connecting customers in the downstream. Now, its investment tentacles are beginning to extend to large models, data centers, computing power operation, and embodied intelligence. Why does a battery manufacturer invest in AI? The story of Standard Oil provides a perspective to understand CATL. What CATL is looking for is not a new story unrelated to batteries, but the next batch of customers for batteries and electric energy, as well as new capabilities required to access these customers. In those days, oil needed to be transported by trains; today, electricity needs to be sent to data centers and supplied to robots. What CATL is trying to do is to become a shareholder at the table before the next round of demand really expands. Is the Battery Giant Chasing the AI Trend? If you make a list of CATL's investment targets in the past few years, you will find a change: in the early days, the list was densely populated with mining, materials, battery equipment and automobile companies, while now large models, data centers and robots are occupying more and more positions. This is not a sudden cross-border move. In the middle of this year, Zeng Yuqun, founder of CATL, was asked in an exclusive interview with Caijing why CATL's business boundaries are expanding wider and wider. His answer was: "All our expansions are centered on our core capabilities." One of the previous priorities was to carry out industrial layout around electric vehicles. By 2026, the CATL ecosystem has invested in more than 10 automobile enterprises in total. For example, in 2021, CATL contributed 770 million yuan to participate in the capital increase of AVATR and became its second largest shareholder. In the same year, it also participated in Zeekr's Pre-A round of financing. In addition to equity investment, CATL has also established joint battery companies with many automobile enterprises, advancing the cooperation from procurement relationships to joint R&D, production and supply. AVATR is a typical example of this strategy. In the cooperation system composed of Changan, Huawei and CATL, CATL does not just wait for new cars to be launched to receive orders, but participates in product development earlier as a shareholder and technical partner. For battery suppliers, this means the opportunity to integrate their own technologies into customers' solutions at the vehicle model planning stage. At the same time, the venture capital institutions under the CATL ecosystem, including Puquan Capital, Wending Investment, Chendao Capital and Mindong Times, have also expanded to both ends of the industrial chain: moving upstream to mining, materials and equipment to ensure supply and technical support; extending downstream to automobile enterprises, battery swapping and recycling to find markets and new business models for batteries. Direct investment and fund investment together form a network, and the role of capital has extended from obtaining returns to establishing cooperative relationships and complementing industrial capabilities. In the AI era, CATL has also begun to shift its focus. An early signal came from Qianxun Intelligence. In November 2024, Qianxun Intelligence announced the completion of the angel+ round of financing exclusively invested by Borey Capital, with an amount of tens of millions of yuan. Borey Capital is not an affiliate of CATL, but a venture capital firm established with personal capital from Li Ping, co-founder and vice chairman of CATL. On the other hand, CATL's presence can be seen in the business dealings of Qianxun Intelligence: CATL provides batteries for Qianxun's robots, and Qianxun has obtained the identity of "CATL Ecological Enterprise". Subsequently, in the field of embodied intelligence, CATL invested in Galaxea, Songyan Power, Zhongqing Robot and Weita Power. Among them, in addition to the direct investment from CATL, Puquan Capital and Chendao Capital, the industrial investment platforms under the CATL ecosystem, also participated in the investment in Galaxea and Songyan Power. artigo.texto: TAIPEI (TAIPEI NEWS) – Hsinchu-based Industrial Technology Research Institute said Thursday that it has partnered with local battery maker eJoule to make high-capacity batteries for drones and electric vehicles. Medium-and high-lithium ternary batteries use nickel, cobalt, and manganese. Higher lithium content means greater storage capacity, making them suitable for drones, robotics, and electric vehicles. According to a press release, drones and EVs are driving demand for lighter, longer-lasting batteries. Although ternary batteries are valued for their capacity, there are lifecycle and safety bottlenecks that need to be addressed before commercialization. ITRI and eJoule co-developed a solution using single-crystal structures, electrode fabrication, and power cell certification to speed commercialization for drones, robotics, and storage applications. The project also aims to achieve production and supply chain self-reliance. Electrode fabrication combines raw materials with metal foils to create the positive and negative charges required for batteries to function. The common method involves mixing the materials with additives and solvents such as water for coating onto the foils, which are then vacuumed and pressed into batteries. ITRI Material and Chemical Research Laboratories Director Chiu Kuo-chan (邱國展) said eJoule provided the material while ITRI designed battery specifications and conducted performance tests. He noted that the material proved stable after extensive, repetitive cycles of charging and discharging, making it a suitable candidate comparable to lithium iron phosphate batteries in terms of lifespan as well as safer than traditional ternary materials. ITRI said eJoule’s patented dynamic crystallization process yields simple, high-performing structures without using toxic precursors. eJoule Vice President Liu Min-tuan (劉敏端) said the initiative would combine ITRI's battery expertise to speed material applications from laboratory settings to commercially viable products.

artigo.texto: TOKYO - Major telecommunications provider NTT Inc. is considering building the first core data center for U.S. artificial intelligence startup Anthropic in Japan, a source familiar with the matter said Wednesday. The construction cost for the data center, to be built in a coastal area in southern Osaka Prefecture and handled by NTT Data Group Corp., is expected to total roughly 1 trillion yen ($6.3 billion), making it one of the leading projects in the country. Anthropic opened its first office in Asia in Tokyo in October last year and the launch of a data center is expected to help the company expand its business in Japan amid the AI boom. Since data centers handle confidential corporate and personal data, having domestic facilities is seen as desirable from a national security perspective and can help mitigate risks related to operations and data transfers. Japanese digital minister Toshiharu Furukawa said Tuesday the government had asked Anthropic to consider the country as a site for a data center during a meeting in Tokyo with Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark, adding that the government was willing to support such a project. Anthropic is a leading developer of generative AI, and its Claude Mythos model is seen as highly capable of finding security vulnerabilities. Governments around the world have worked to strengthen ties with the startup to gain access with its technology and information.

artigo.texto: Renewable energy illustration: Chen Xia/Global Times One of the challenges emerging from India's rapid economic growth is how to meet its rising demand for electricity. The Indian Express reported that Ghanshyam Prasad, chairperson of the country's top power planner, said that India may need to add 105-150 gigawatts of coal-based power capacity by 2035, significantly more than the 97 gigawatts currently planned. The remarks come amid growing concerns over whether India's electricity supply can keep pace with rising demand. Bloomberg recently reported that smaller factories, farmers and households are facing power cuts as demand outweighs supply on the grid. Manish Dhuppad, general secretary at the Chhattisgarh Mini Steel Plant Association, was quoted as saying that small steel mills in the central state of Chhattisgarh are facing outages of 10 to 12 hours a day, forcing plants to reduce output. India's electricity challenges are complex. Yet recent signs of supply constraints suggest that ensuring a reliable power supply is becoming increasingly important as the economy expands. The focus, therefore, is shifting toward how India can expand electricity supply to meet rising demand. The paradox is that India's electricity supply challenges have emerged even as its renewable energy sector has expanded rapidly. India now ranks third globally in renewable energy installed capacity, with solar power accounting for the largest share of its renewable energy mix. As of July 31, the country's installed solar capacity had reached 164.59 gigawatts, up from just 2.8 gigawatts in 2014. The scale of this increase highlights the rapid pace of India's solar development over the past decade. The question, then, is why India's power shortages have persisted alongside rapid growth in renewable energy. One part of the answer is that some renewable electricity has not been fully utilized. Citing data from the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA), Reuters reported that India turned away nearly 1.8 billion units of renewable electricity in July and August, even as it grappled with power shortages. CREA analysts attributed the curtailment to grid and operational constraints. In other words, India's renewable energy expansion has created a new challenge: some of the electricity generated has gone to waste because the grid has not been able to absorb it. The build-out of renewable energy has outpaced the development of transmission infrastructure. Expanding grid capacity and energy storage could offer a more effective way to address this mismatch. One area with potential is battery storage. Deploying battery storage systems could help integrate more renewable power into the grid and allow more of the electricity generated to be used. Battery storage, however, is a highly specialized industry that requires technological expertise and mature supply chains. India has invested heavily in this area and has continued to strengthen its capabilities. Yet imports and international cooperation can also offer a faster way to access advanced technologies and help address the country's immediate energy challenges. Given the scale of India's electricity needs and the importance of reliable power supply for economic development, expanding access to battery storage through trade and cooperation could be highly beneficial. China's years of experience in battery manufacturing and its extensive industrial supply chain have made it a major participant in the global energy storage sector. This creates potential areas for cooperation between China and India, which could help India expand its options as it seeks to address its energy challenges. If this potential is better realized, battery storage could become another tool for India to ease pressure on its power system and reduce the need to rely on expanding coal-fired capacity. As the global energy transition continues, whether coal can provide a long-term solution to India's growing electricity demand remains uncertain. Greater international cooperation in energy storage could help India overcome the bottlenecks holding back renewable energy and create a more balanced path for meeting future power needs. The author is a reporter with the Global Times. bizopinion@globaltimes.com.cn

artigo.texto: Israel to cap new data centers at 200 megawatts amid AI power crunch The Electricity Authority is preparing rules that would block larger facilities as developers seek grid connections totaling 27,000 megawatts, well above the country’s installed generation capacity. Data centers could account for about 20% of electricity consumption by 2030. The Electricity Authority is moving to curb the construction of large data centers by limiting the maximum capacity of any new facility to 200 megawatts, Calcalist has learned. According to sources familiar with the matter within the Electricity Authority’s plenum, a draft decision regulating data center connections to the electricity grid is expected to be released for public comment on Sunday. Meanwhile, estimates suggest that data centers could account for approximately 20% of Israel’s total electricity consumption by 2030. A data center’s power capacity determines how much computing it can support, including the training and operation of artificial intelligence models. Its electricity demand is driven by processors and the extensive cooling systems needed to keep them running. While a 200-megawatt facility would be large by Israeli standards, Noga, Israel’s independent electricity system operator, has already received connection requests for 50 facilities with higher capacities. For example, Mega DC, owned by Zahi Nahmias, is seeking to build a 1,100-megawatt facility on the site in Hadera where the Alliance tire factory operated until 2024. SDS, a company controlled by Yossi Schonfeld, has requested approval for an 875-megawatt facility in Nesher. Under the proposed rules, projects of this scale would not be eligible for approval as currently planned. According to officials familiar with the plenum’s deliberations, limiting individual facilities to 200 megawatts would allow more data centers to be built while helping protect the electricity grid. A sudden failure at a large facility could disrupt grid frequency and potentially affect the stability of the electricity supply. The global boom in demand for data centers supporting AI models has prompted Israeli entrepreneurs to race to establish facilities and submit connection requests to Noga. But the scale of the applications has raised concerns about whether the country’s electricity infrastructure can accommodate them. The total requested capacity has reached 27,000 megawatts, compared with Israel’s installed electricity generation capacity of 18,800 megawatts. Israel’s average electricity consumption is approximately 9,000 megawatts, while peak demand reached 17,300 megawatts in August 2025. The total capacity sought by data center developers therefore exceeds the country’s entire existing generation capacity, even before accounting for other electricity consumers. Data centers also pose a particular challenge because they are designed to operate continuously. Unlike many factories or other large electricity consumers, they cannot easily suspend operations without disrupting the services they provide. Their customers, including major technology companies such as Google, Microsoft and OpenAI, expect reliable, uninterrupted computing capacity. This creates a large and relatively inflexible source of electricity demand that requires long-term planning. Last June, the Electricity Authority temporarily halted the processing of new data center applications for 140 days while conducting an internal review ahead of the regulatory decision. The draft is expected to be released for public comment, followed by a three-week consultation period. The authority’s plenum will then consider objections before publishing the final framework. Notably, the draft does not appear to impose geographic restrictions on data centers. Developers could therefore apply to build facilities in areas with high existing electricity demand as well as in more remote regions. Noga is likely to find it easier to approve projects in outlying areas, where connecting a new facility may have less impact on other consumers and the existing grid. The framework is also expected to address whether data centers should be allowed to connect directly to power plants, bypassing the Israel Electric Corporation’s grid. Such an arrangement could be rejected out of concern that generation capacity intended to serve the wider public would instead be allocated to a single customer. Another issue is whether data centers could be required to disconnect from the grid at short notice. A senior executive at a data center developer said such a requirement would be a deal-breaker. The cost of installing backup generators or energy storage systems capable of supporting a 200-megawatt facility, he said, could make the project economically unviable. The executive nevertheless described the proposed 200-megawatt ceiling as reasonable. “Currently, there are no data centers of this scale in Israel, and given the electricity generation capacity, establishing massive facilities here is not feasible,” he said. “Even in the U.S., data centers are hitting a wall. Demand is enormous, but you can’t just build a 1,000-megawatt facility anywhere; there are power constraints. Furthermore, you can’t buy unlimited quantities of GPUs.” The difficulties of building data centers in the U.S. and Europe could make Israel an attractive destination for technology companies. Electricity prices in Israel are lower than in the U.S., potentially making operations more cost-effective for data center developers. The senior executive cited other advantages, including Israel’s technology sector and its experience building hardened data centers. “Israel is a technological powerhouse, a ‘Startup Nation.’ All the major players are here. Furthermore, Israel possesses expertise in constructing hardened data centers,” he said. artigo.texto: Hyundai Motor has adopted CATL’s latest thermal propagation (TP) control technology in its recently launched IONIQ V electric vehicle in China. Equipped with a Chinese-made lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery, the IONIQ V is the first electric vehicle under Hyundai’s IONIQ brand priced in the 20 million won range. CATL said on Oct. 14 that the IONIQ V features its third-generation TP prevention technology, NP3.0 (No Propagation 3.0), according to battery safety materials released the previous day. This marks the first time the technology has been adopted in a Hyundai vehicle. The IONIQ V is an electric vehicle developed specifically for the Chinese market and was first unveiled at the 2026 Beijing International Auto Show in April. Launched on Sept. 29, it is produced by Beijing Hyundai, a joint venture between Hyundai Motor and Beijing Automotive Group (BAIC). Its locally discounted price ranges from 99,900 yuan to 131,900 yuan (approximately 20 million to 26 million won). Equipped with a 66.8-kilowatt-hour (kWh) LFP battery from CATL, the vehicle offers a driving range of more than 650 kilometers on a single charge under China’s Light-Duty Vehicle Test Cycle (CLTC). However, CLTC tends to produce longer range estimates than South Korea’s Ministry of Environment standard, with differences reaching as much as 200 kilometers. CATL’s NP3.0 technology is designed to help vehicles continue moving safely even after battery thermal runaway occurs. Thermal runaway is a phenomenon in which a battery’s internal temperature rises rapidly, spreading heat to neighboring cells and potentially causing fire or explosion. CATL has developed three generations of TP prevention technology since introducing NP1.0 in 2018. NP3.0 is designed to detect abnormalities within seconds of thermal runaway, warn the driver and maintain high-voltage power supply. CATL said its internal tests showed that vehicles could continue driving safely for at least five minutes after thermal runaway without losing power. The technology focuses on giving drivers enough time to move their vehicles to a safe location. Hyundai’s adoption of NP3.0 comes amid tighter battery safety regulations in China. The previous national standard, GB 38031-2020, required occupants to receive a warning at least five minutes before a fire or explosion caused by battery thermal runaway. The revised standard, GB 38031-2025, which took effect in July, strengthened requirements to prevent fires or explosions even when thermal runaway occurs. Under its “In China, For China” strategy, Hyundai has reduced costs by using locally sourced components and manufacturing facilities, enabling it to introduce a midsize electric vehicle priced in the 20 million won range. Demand for similarly affordable EVs is also growing in South Korea as Tesla rapidly expands sales with Chinese-made vehicles and Chinese automakers including BYD and Zeekr target the Korean market. Tesla sold 11,421 Model Y vehicles in South Korea in September, surpassing Hyundai’s Grandeur sedan at 8,898 units. Tesla’s Korean sales reached 89,148 vehicles in the first nine months of the year, up 104.4% from a year earlier. Hyundai’s domestic EV sales, including Genesis, totaled just 55,733 units during the same period. Hyundai has yet to decide whether to launch the IONIQ V in South Korea. Even if introduced, maintaining its Chinese-market price in the 20 million won range would be difficult. Eligibility for EV purchase subsidies is also uncertain, as the government revised its subsidy program this year to consider contributions to domestic supply chains and the use of locally sourced components. Hwang Kyung-in, head of the Strategic Industry Analysis Division at the Korea Institute for Industrial Economics and Trade (KIET), said automakers must weigh the benefits of lower costs against potential subsidy disadvantages. “Even if using Chinese batteries reduces EV production costs, companies need to assess the trade-offs if they face disadvantages in domestic subsidies,” he said. “Automakers must consider not only battery prices but also subsidies, supply chains and other factors.” Hwang added that Korean battery manufacturers also need to develop cost-competitive LFP batteries for electric vehicles, while deciding where to concentrate their limited investment resources and production capacity.

artigo.texto: US solid-state battery developer Factorial Energy is building a solid-state battery production line in Cheonan, South Korea, with local equipment suppliers playing key roles. PNT has been selected to supply dry electrode equipment, a critical component of mass production, while Philenergy will provide turnkey equipment for the assembly process. According to industry sources on Oct. 15, Factorial issued purchase orders this week for equipment needed at its solid-state battery pilot line. Korean equipment manufacturers will participate across the battery production process, from electrode manufacturing and assembly to downstream processes. Factorial CEO Siyu Huang was also understood to have visited South Korea to inspect the company's Cheonan production facility. Headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, Factorial develops solid-state batteries and has attracted investments from global automakers including Stellantis, Mercedes-Benz and Hyundai Motor. The company listed on the US Nasdaq in June through a merger with a special purpose acquisition company (SPAC). Factorial established its Korean subsidiary, Factorial Korea, in April 2022 and set up a production facility in Cheonan. The facility currently produces its FEST semi-solid-state batteries on a bench-scale production line to validate manufacturing processes and sample performance. Unlike conventional lithium-ion batteries, semi-solid-state batteries use electrolytes in gel or slurry form rather than liquid electrolytes. Factorial decided to expand its Cheonan production line to meet customer letters of intent (LOIs) and order volumes. The new line will be used to verify productivity and secure manufacturing technologies needed for future mass production. Factorial has previously tested the performance of its FEST batteries in electric vehicles from Stellantis and Mercedes-Benz. Factorial's battery manufacturing process is largely similar to that of conventional lithium-ion batteries. Cathodes and anodes are produced during electrode manufacturing, then processed and assembled into cells. The batteries are completed through downstream processes including formation and inspection. Factorial plans to introduce dry electrode technology for cathode production to improve battery performance and simplify manufacturing. Dry electrode technology involves mixing cathode active materials, conductive additives and binders without liquid solvents, then compressing the mixture into electrodes. By reducing the need for drying equipment used in conventional wet processes, the technology can lower energy consumption and capital expenditure. It is particularly important for solid-state batteries, whose solid electrolytes are sensitive to moisture and solvents. Factorial combines dry cathodes with ultrathin lithium-metal anodes, an approach that can significantly increase battery energy density. However, manufacturing dry cathodes is more difficult than producing dry anodes because cathode materials are harder and more brittle, making it challenging to achieve uniform electrodes during compression. Factorial selected PNT for its competitiveness in technically demanding dry electrode equipment. PNT has developed roll-to-roll technology capable of processing electrodes up to 1,500 millimeters wide at high speeds. The company has also secured five orders for dry electrode equipment and two for solid-state battery equipment. Philenergy will supply assembly equipment, including notching machines that cut electrodes into specified shapes and stacking systems that layer cathodes and anodes. The notching process will use a press method in which dies stamp out electrode shapes. Yujin Technology will supply the die components. Philenergy disclosed on Oct. 15 that it had signed a new equipment supply contract with Factorial. The contract runs through the end of December 2027. Although the contract value was not disclosed, it is estimated at several billion won. "Factorial selected equipment suppliers based on the capital expenditure required for its Cheonan pilot line," an industry official said. "It chose relatively large companies such as PNT and Philenergy for core processes including electrode manufacturing and assembly, while assigning other processes to smaller suppliers." "Semi-solid-state and solid-state batteries still require further technological validation to achieve stable mass production," the official added. "Factorial plans to establish a mass production line in Boston after securing process stability and satisfactory yields in Cheonan. Existing equipment suppliers are also likely to participate in the US investment." Factorial's batteries are expected to be commercialized in drones and robots before electric vehicles. In July, the company announced its first commercial order for drone batteries. Earlier, in May, it established a partnership with US-based KULR, Netherlands-based Tulip Tech and South Korea's JR Energy Solution to commercialize drone batteries. KULR is responsible for battery thermal management and safety improvements, while Tulip Tech will develop battery packs. JR Energy Solution will oversee the Asia-Pacific market from its base in South Korea. Factorial is also working with SK On. The companies signed a memorandum of understanding in July to cooperate on solid-state battery manufacturing. SK On will contribute manufacturing technology and production experience, while Factorial will provide battery cell design technology. They will also evaluate the feasibility of mass-producing solid-state batteries using existing production equipment. In South Korea, Samsung SDI, LG Energy Solution and SK On have established solid-state battery production lines. Samsung SDI operates its S-Line pilot facility at its Suwon research and development center and aims to begin mass production of solid-state batteries for humanoid robots in the second half of next year. LG Energy Solution produces solid-state battery samples at its Ochang mother line. A

artigo.texto: Eco&Dream has raised 35 billion won to purchase raw materials for battery precursor production. The company aims to achieve record precursor shipments in 2027 while expanding development of next-generation battery materials. Eco&Dream said on Oct. 14 that it completed payment for 35 billion won in convertible bonds (CBs). Both the coupon rate and yield to maturity are 0%. The conversion price was set 10% above the reference share price, with no downward conversion price adjustment, or refixing, provision. The company plans to use the proceeds to purchase raw materials needed for precursor production. It aims to increase customer shipments from its Saemangeum Campus and achieve its highest-ever precursor shipment volume in 2027. Eco&Dream is also developing next-generation battery materials, including precursors for lithium iron phosphate (LFP), lithium manganese-rich (LMR) and all-solid-state batteries. It is expanding research and development into sulfide-based solid electrolytes and lithium sulfide (Li₂S), a key raw material. "Building on our proprietary precursor technology and supply experience, we will pursue record shipments in 2027 and expand our next-generation materials portfolio," an Eco&Dream representative said.

artigo.texto: Warda Battery The group of neighbors fighting against a battery energy storage system (BESS) in Warda may finally get their day in court. Fayette County landowners Jim Clements, Guadalupe Gutierrez, Cynthia Gutierrez, and Carolyn Lehmann sued Pct. 1 Commissioner Jason McBroom and his family in 2024 over a proposed BESS facility on the McBroom family property in Warda. The plaintiffs want to stop the facility from being built. They’re worried about the potential for industrial disaster such as lithium battery fires and claim the facility poses a nuisance to the enjoyment of their property. The local District Judge, Jeff Steinhauser, recused himself from the case. Todd A. Blomerth, Senior Judge of the 421st Judicial District, was assigned to preside over the lawsuit. He dismissed the suit last year, siding with the defendants’ argument that an emotional reaction to a proposed facility cannot be the basis for a nuisance claim. The plaintiffs appealed to the Texas Third Court of Appeals in Austin, which ruled that the lawsuit can proceed in district court. Plaintiffs say that after the ruling, construction began on the BESS facility. The McBroom family appealed the decision to the Supreme Court of Texas. On Oct. 2, the Supreme Court of Texas denied the defendants’ petition for review. “The order leaves intact the victory secured by landowners in the Third Court of Appeals at Austin, confirming that the landowners can proceed with their lawsuit seeking an injunction and damages against the Warda Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) facility before a Fayette County jury,” said the plaintiffs’ attorney, Alex Ross Hernandez, in a press release issued last week. “The Texas Supreme Court’s denial of the Defendants’ petition for review, allowing the ruling of the Third Court of Appeals to remain the law, stands as a definitive confirmation that Texas landowners maintain with the cognizable right to sue to protect their homesteads, rural investments, and/or farm land when a substantial and unreasonable interference, such as a Battery Energy Storage System under the pleaded facts of this case, is built or proposed to be built at the fence line or in their community,” Hernandez said. “We look forward to trying this matter to a Fayette County jury and remain thankful for a judiciary that remains open to the adjudication of truth, justice, and fairness for all Texans. ‘We the people’ remains with teeth, as shown by the Texas Supreme Court’s denial of the Defendants’ petition for review.” So far, no trial date has been set. Northern Fayette County has become a breeding ground for dispute between rural property owners and land-hungry technology projects. Over in Winchester, just a few miles from Warda, property owners hope to stop construction of a data center on FM 448. A community meeting concerning the Winchester data center will take place Nov. 2 at the St. Michael’s Park in Winchester starting at 7 p.m.

artigo.texto: SINEXCEL conclui o envio de PCS para projeto de armazenamento de energia de 100 MW/400 MWh no Chile AGÊNCIA DE COMUNICAÇÃO Conteúdo de responsabilidade da empresa 15 de outubro de 2026 VALLENAR, Chile, 15 de outubro de 2026 /PRNewswire/ — A SINEXCEL (300693.SZ) concluiu o envio de todos os sistemas de conversão de energia (PCS) StellaON 1250K para o projeto de armazenamento de energia em baterias de 100 MW/400 MWh da RelyEZ Energy Storage Technology Co., Ltd., no Chile. O sistema de armazenamento de energia de quatro horas, localizado em Atacama, será carregado nos períodos de menor demanda e descarregado nos horários de pico, contribuindo para aumentar a flexibilidade da rede elétrica e melhorar a rentabilidade do projeto. A entrega dentro do prazo apoia a execução do projeto. Em projetos de grande escala no exterior, os cronogramas de produção, inspeção e envio precisam estar rigorosamente alinhados ao andamento das obras no local. A SINEXCEL concluiu o fornecimento de todo o lote de PCS dentro do prazo, ajudando a RelyEZ Energy a manter o cronograma de transporte, instalação, comissionamento e conexão à rede elétrica. Em um projeto dessa escala, atrasos na entrega de um único lote podem comprometer o cronograma de construção. A entrega coordenada reduz as incertezas e ajuda as equipes locais a planejar as próximas etapas do projeto. PCS StellaON 1250K projetado para as condições extremas do Atacama Os equipamentos de energia instalados no Atacama precisam operar em condições ambientais adversas, que podem incluir altas temperaturas, poeira e areia. O PCS StellaON 1250K apresenta eficiência máxima de 99% e eficiência de 98,5% na potência nominal. O equipamento opera em temperaturas de ?40 °C a 60 °C, mantém a potência máxima a 55 °C e conta com grau de proteção IP65. Manter a potência nominal em altas temperaturas ajuda a minimizar a redução de potência e a necessidade de capacidade adicional. A maior eficiência de conversão também reduz as perdas de energia ao longo de ciclos sucessivos de carga e descarga, contribuindo para a estabilidade operacional e a rentabilidade a longo prazo. Expansão da capacidade de atendimento local nas Américas Após o envio, o projeto avançará para as etapas de instalação e comissionamento no local. A SINEXCEL conta com uma equipe dedicada ao atendimento pós-venda na América Latina e sete centros de serviço distribuídos pelas Américas. As solicitações técnicas podem ser respondidas em até 30 minutos. A empresa também oferece suporte 24 horas por dia e garante o fornecimento de peças de reposição em até sete dias. A SINEXCEL já forneceu equipamentos para mais de 17 GW de capacidade de armazenamento de energia, distribuídos por mais de 5.000 projetos, e mantém parcerias com mais de 600 empresas em mais de 60 países e regiões. Após o embarque, o projeto chileno avança para a fase de entrega e implementação no local. A SINEXCEL continuará ampliando sua presença local na América Latina e prestando suporte aos clientes ao longo de todo o ciclo de vida dos projetos. Sobre a SINEXCEL Fundada em 2007, a SINEXCEL é pioneira em armazenamento de energia, carregamento de veículos elétricos e soluções de qualidade de energia. Com 17 GW de capacidade instalada de armazenamento, 200.000 carregadores CC para veículos elétricos e quase 20 milhões de amperes de filtros harmônicos ativos instalados, a SINEXCEL estabelece parcerias com líderes do setor para promover a liberdade energética. artigo.texto: QCOM, AVGO, NVDA Stocks In Focus As ByteDance Reportedly Closes In On A MediaTek Pact For AI Data Center Chips - ByteDance is close to contracting MediaTek for AI data center chips, Bloomberg reported. - Earlier this year, ByteDance agreed to buy millions of AI chips from Qualcomm. - Retail sentiment was ‘bearish’ on QCOM and ‘extremely bearish’ on AVGO and NVDA on Thursday. Qualcomm (QCOM) and Broadcom (AVGO) shares are in focus after a Bloomberg report said ByteDance is close to a deal to buy custom AI chips from Taiwan’s MediaTek for its data centers. MediaTek would supply ByteDance with application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs), which are designed for particular computing tasks. MediaTek is a major vendor for Google’s tensor processing units (TPUs). The deal is a competitive signal for Qualcomm and Broadcom. ByteDance agreed earlier this year to buy millions of AI chips from Qualcomm, while it would give MediaTek a stronger foothold in a market where Broadcom is already well established. Nvidia (NVDA) could also face pressure if ByteDance shifts more AI workloads to custom ASICs, reducing its reliance on GPUs, although U.S. export restrictions on advanced chips are already forcing Chinese companies to look for alternatives. ASIC Chips Market Demand for ASICs has grown as AI companies seek alternatives to general-purpose GPUs, with major cloud providers such as Amazon and Google and AI developers increasingly investing in their own chips to cut costs. Bloomberg reported that ByteDance is considering capital expenditure of up to $70 billion this year, more than double last year’s total, as it builds out its AI infrastructure. MediaTek expects AI-chip sales to reach about $2 billion this year and is targeting 15% of an $80 billion market next year, according to Bloomberg. Global Chip Rout Global semiconductor stocks extended their selloff on Thursday as hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation data heightened interest-rate concerns, compounding worries about AI spending and intensifying Chinese competition. The iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) fell for a seventh consecutive session on Wednesday and dropped 1.7% overnight, while South Korea’s Kospi tumbled more than 7% on Thursday, with Samsung and SK Hynix among the biggest decliners. AVGO, AVGO and NVDA were down 0.7% to 1.3% overnight ahead of Thursday’s session. Retail View On QCOM, AVGO, NVDA On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment was ‘bearish’ for QCOM, and ‘extremely bearish’ for AVGO and NVDA. “NVDA all I can say is the stock market is bipolar. One day Nvidia is changing planet earth and next world is going bankrupt. The amount of manipulation is unreal. It’s not even weeks but days that story lines change,” a trader wrote. Year to date, QCOM stock is up 2.5%, while AVGO is up 0.5% and NVDA is up 19%.

artigo.texto: ALPS nomeia Brian Turnbow para liderar o desenvolvimento de data centers de IA de última geração A startup italiana nomeou Turnbow para liderar sua expansão tecnológica em inteligência artificial e computação de alto desempenho, com uma abordagem de energia para computação que planeja aproveitar fontes de energia renováveis e reutilizar ativos existentes para desenvolver uma infraestrutura de computação mais sustentável. TRENTO, Itália, 15 de outubro de 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- A ALPS anuncia a nomeação de Brian Turnbow como diretor técnico de IA. Fundada em Trentino em 2018 e com atuação em quatro continentes, a empresa aplica sua expertise em projeto, construção e operação de data centers integrados a sistemas de energia às áreas de IA e HPC. O acesso à energia é uma das principais restrições ao desenvolvimento da infraestrutura de IA. Segundo dados da Terna de 31 de agosto de 2026, as solicitações de conexão à rede elétrica de data centers na Itália totalizaram mais de 100 GW, um aumento em relação aos cerca de 30 GW no final de 2024 — um crescimento que torna a seleção do local e os prazos de conexão à rede extremamente críticos. A abordagem de conversão de energia em computação da ALPS baseia-se em uma escolha deliberada: Localizar data centers onde a energia já está disponível, inclusive fora dos principais polos, para reduzir a dependência de áreas congestionadas da rede elétrica. A empresa tem como objetivo integrar fontes de energia renováveis e revitalizar áreas industriais desativadas, reutilizando conexões de rede, edifícios e outros ativos existentes sempre que tecnicamente viável. O objetivo é desenvolver uma infraestrutura computacional mais sustentável, utilizando recursos locais e, por meio da reutilização de ativos, limitando a ocupação de terrenos e reduzindo a necessidade de novas construções. Essa expansão complementa as operações de mineração em andamento da ALPS, que continuam em linha com seu plano de negócios. Turnbow liderará a estratégia técnica de IA/HPC da ALPS, desde a avaliação de arquiteturas e locais até o engajamento com parceiros de tecnologia e industriais. A Itália será um mercado prioritário. A ALPS pretende trazer de volta à Itália sua expertise internacional e trabalhar com empresas italianas de engenharia e do setor industrial, aproveitando também sua experiência em projetos no exterior. "A Itália e a Europa possuem recursos energéticos, ativos industriais e conhecimento técnico que podemos aproveitar", afirma Francesco Buffa, CEO e cofundador da ALPS. "Por meio de nossa abordagem de conversão de energia em computação, queremos transformar o potencial energético e industrial das regiões onde atuamos em uma vantagem competitiva e ajudar a reduzir a lacuna da IA na Europa." Turnbow traz para a empresa mais de 25 anos de experiência em telecomunicações e infraestrutura digital, tendo ocupado cargos técnicos na TWT, Unidata e CDLAN. Ele é membro do conselho administrativo do ITNOG. "A infraestrutura de IA começa muito antes da implementação de GPUs", afirma Brian Turnbow. "Cada projeto deve começar com as cargas de trabalho que precisa suportar e os requisitos dos clientes, e não apenas com a energia disponível. Meu objetivo é traduzir esses requisitos em decisões de projeto coerentes, construindo capacidade computacional flexível, escalável e sustentável, ao mesmo tempo que utilizo fontes de energia renováveis e ativos existentes." Sobre a ALPS A ALPS projeta, constrói e opera data centers para aplicações de alta demanda energética e computacional, combinando conhecimento especializado em energia com engenharia e operação de data centers. Seu crescimento internacional foi apoiado pela Azimut por meio de uma transação de € 40 milhões em 2023 e um acordo de € 105 milhões em 2024. Para informações adicionais: www.alps.it FONTE ALPS

artigo.texto: Brighton singer-songwriter Bess Atwell returns to Australian stages in March 2027 with a new album due in February and a freshly released single written about her time in Quebec. Bess Atwell is heading back to Australia in March 2027, bringing songs from her forthcoming album due in February alongside the just-released single and video ‘The Act’. The Brighton-based artist last toured Australia as a headline act in 2025. That run built on the quiet momentum she has gathered since her 2021 album Already, Always and the 2024 release Light Sleeper. The new Australian dates land just after the arrival of the next full-length record, giving local audiences an early chance to hear the material live. ‘The Act’ was written about the period Bess Atwell spent living in Quebec. The track and its accompanying video are available to stream, download and watch now. It sits in the same emotionally direct lane that has defined her work: intimate storytelling delivered with melodic restraint and a clear, crystalline vocal. Bess Atwell first drew wider attention with Already, Always in 2021. The record established her as a writer capable of turning private observation into something that feels shared. Three years later Light Sleeper expanded that approach. Produced by Aaron Dessner and released through Real Kind Records (the label founded by Lucy Rose), the album added luminous textures while keeping the focus on her voice and the detail of the lyrics. Reviews noted the increased sonic range without any loss of the quiet assurance that marked the earlier work. Her path into music began with Taylor Swift songs on guitar before a Johnny Flynn concert shifted her focus toward the early 2010s London nu-folk scene. Influences such as Fleet Foxes, Bon Iver, Joni Mitchell, The National and Sharon Van Etten sit alongside later admiration for Julia Jacklin, Stella Donnelly, Phoebe Bridgers and Soccer Mommy. Those threads appear in the careful economy of her arrangements and the unflinching honesty of the words. Live, Bess Atwell has steadily moved from smaller rooms to sold-out headline shows across the UK, Europe, Canada and Australia. The songs tend to feel like confidences rather than performances: vulnerable, precise and delivered with an understated power that rewards close listening. The 2027 Australian run continues that pattern, placing her in rooms that have become familiar stops for independent artists who prioritise connection over scale. The new album remains untitled at this stage, but the February 2027 release window places it just weeks before the Australian dates. That timing suggests the tour will function as both a celebration of the new material and a continuation of the relationship Bess Atwell has been building with Australian audiences since her previous visit. Her catalogue now stretches from the 2016 debut Hold Your Mind through the 2019 EP Big Blue, Already, Always, the 2022 remix collection Already, Rearranged, Light Sleeper and the 2024 EP More Than Science. Each step has refined the same core strengths: careful melody, emotional clarity and a refusal to overstate. ‘The Act’ continues that trajectory, offering a first glimpse of the writing that will shape the next chapter. For Australian fans who caught the 2025 shows or who have followed the records from a distance, the March 2027 dates present a clear opportunity to hear the next phase of the work in rooms designed for listening. The combination of a new album, a fresh single and a return to the same cities creates a natural moment of connection between artist and audience. artigo.texto: Dow launches VOLTRICELL battery cell materials platform to advance next-generation battery innovation - VOLTRICELL materials are designed to help address performance needs in high-energy-density battery applications. - Alongside existing technologies, the introduction of VOLTRICELL means Dow can support customers across multiple stages of the battery value chain. - Dows newest battery fire protection materials DOWSIL EF-6559 and DOWSIL FC-2024 will be also on display at The Battery Show North America 2026 Dow (NYSE: DOW) announced the addition of VOLTRICELL to its existing portfolio of battery solutions at The Battery Show North America. VOLTRICELLopens in a new tab is a brand-new suite of materials designed to optimize battery manufacturing processes and improve the performance of todays battery and emerging sodium-ion, silicon-anode and solid-state battery technologies. It is Dows first material platform designed specifically for supporting optimal electrochemistry inside the cell. As battery technologies continue to evolve, manufacturers face growing pressure to improve energy density, extend cycle life, increase charging speed and scale production across multiple chemistries and manufacturing approaches. VOLTRICELL brings together Dows growing portfolio of battery cell materials under a unified platform designed to support innovation across electrodes, separators, coatings and battery cell packaging applications. The portfolio includes binders, dispersants, rheology modifiers, surfactants and specialty additives that can be selected and combined to help support performance, manufacturability and scalability. In the battery industry, there are a multitude of chemistries and cell manufacturing strategies in play today and under development for the future, said Joel McDonald, Global Technical Director for Dow MobilityScience. Battery manufacturers need materials partners that can evolve with their technology roadmaps. Through VOLTRICELL, we can help customers innovate with confidence, leveraging Dows broad toolbox to support todays cell chemistries and the next generation of energy storage. Designing Materials that Support the Whole Battery The launch of VOLTRICELL reflects Dows continued commitment to the industry and to customers across the battery value chain. By combining deep materials science expertise with application development capabilities and global technical support through its global MobilityScience Studiosopens in a new tab, Dow helps battery manufacturers accelerate innovation from cell design to system-level integration. At The Battery Show North America 2026, Dow will also showcase its latest materials to support battery fire protection including: - VORAFORCE TP1415 Polyol: a polyurethane resin system for manufacturing lightweight fiber-reinforced composites, designed to support impact resistance, corrosion resistance and flame-retardant performance in polyurethane pultrusion applications - DOWSIL EF-6559 Silicone Foam: a two-part, expanding foam for narrow, complex shapes within battery assemblies that forms a protective ceramic layer when exposed to high heat and is designed to support thermal management and electrical insulation in high-volume series production - DOWSIL FC-2024 Coating: one-part RTV coating applied to battery housings, enclosures and lids to support battery fire protection by forming a hard protective ceramic layer during a thermal event and is intended for a cylindrical, prismatic or pouch-based battery system Visitors can meet with Dow experts at Booth #3000 in Exhibit Halls A-E to explore how advanced materials are helping drive the next generation of battery innovation. For more information and to schedule a meeting with Dow at or before The Battery Show North America, visit https://www.dow.com/en-us/market/mkt-mobility/sub-mobility-electronics/app-mobility-elec-battery-systems.htmlopens in a new tab. About Dow Dow (NYSE: DOW) is one of the worlds leading materials science companies, serving customers in high-growth markets such as packaging, infrastructure, mobility and consumer applications. Our global breadth, asset integration and scale, customer-focused innovation and leading business positions enable us to achieve profitable growth and help deliver a sustainable future. We operate manufacturing sites in 29 countries and employed approximately 34,600 people as of year-end 2025. Dow delivered sales of approximately $40 billion in 2025. References to Dow or the Company mean Dow Inc. and its subsidiaries. Learn more about us at www.dow.comopens in a new tab. artigo.texto: Transformar sal e areia em baterias para armazenamento de energia. Após três anos desenvolvendo o armazenamento térmico em células de areia para a fabricação, a Alternō expandiu sua atuação para o sistema de armazenamento de energia de longo prazo Alternō E. Os primeiros pedidos internacionais chegaram, marcando o início de uma trajetória tranquila de crescimento e amadurecimento no mercado. Fundada em 2023 na cidade de Ho Chi Minh, a Alternō Vietnam (Alternō) optou por se concentrar na pesquisa e desenvolvimento de soluções de armazenamento de energia para a agricultura e a indústria. Após três anos dedicados à sua linha de baterias à base de areia, especializada em armazenamento de calor para necessidades de secagem e aquecimento na indústria, a Alternō lançou recentemente um sistema de armazenamento de energia de longo prazo chamado Alternō E. Diferentemente das baterias de areia, que armazenam energia na forma de calor, a Alternō E aborda diretamente o problema do armazenamento de energia elétrica. Em vez de usar compostos orgânicos inflamáveis, como nas baterias de íon-lítio, as células Alternō E utilizam sais e materiais inorgânicos como os principais componentes envolvidos no carregamento, armazenamento e liberação de energia elétrica. De acordo com o projeto da Alternō, o sistema tem uma vida útil de aproximadamente 30 anos, atendendo à necessidade de armazenamento de energia sustentável para operação a longo prazo. 2026 marca um novo marco, com a Alternō garantindo seus primeiros pedidos de exportação. Ho Viet Hai, cofundador e CEO da Alternō, afirmou que a previsão é de que essas encomendas internacionais comecem a ser entregues em 2027. Recordando a jornada de levar um produto tecnológico desenvolvido no Vietnã para o mundo, o Sr. Hai relatou que, ao levar a bateria de célula de areia da fase de pesquisa para a fábrica, a equipe percebeu que aquecer e manter o calor na areia não era a parte mais desafiadora. A verdadeira dificuldade residia em descobrir como "extrair o calor" e integrar o sistema às linhas de produção já estáveis das fábricas. Uma série de questões práticas, nunca antes levantadas em pesquisas anteriores, começou a surgir. A equipe de engenharia foi obrigada a analisar cada caso, calculando meticulosamente tudo, desde isolamento, tubulação, válvulas de exaustão e fluxo de ar, até o espaço de instalação e os hábitos de trabalho dos operários… Atender às demandas do mercado Você também pode gostar Resolver o problema técnico não significa necessariamente que o produto será aceito pelos clientes. Segundo o Sr. Hai, um sistema que funcione bem não atenderá às necessidades do cliente se o custo do investimento inicial exceder a capacidade de pagamento da empresa parceira. Diante dessa realidade, a Alternō optou por mudar seu modelo de negócios: oferecendo opções de pagamento parcelado ou permitindo que os clientes pagassem mensalmente com base no consumo real de energia. Ao se concentrar na criação de um dispositivo funcional, a empresa aprendeu a resolver os desafios financeiros de tornar o produto acessível aos compradores. As rejeições do mercado obrigaram a Alternō a ajustar o seu próprio produto. Com os clientes precisando de aquecimento, mas sem espaço para energia solar ou eólica, a Alternō desenvolveu uma solução adicional utilizando biomassa para gerar calor e armazená-lo em areia. Por outro lado, muitas fábricas com telhados solares têm excedente de eletricidade ao meio-dia ou em feriados. A pergunta "Existe alguma maneira de armazenar esse excedente de eletricidade para uso quando necessário?" era feita repetidamente pelos clientes, levando gradualmente a equipe da Alternō a uma nova direção de pesquisa. Assim nasceu a Alternō E. "A cada encontro com a realidade, os profissionais de tecnologia aprendem uma lição simples: o mercado não precisa necessariamente do que a empresa tem, mas a empresa precisa encontrar uma maneira de criar o que o mercado realmente precisa", compartilhou o Sr. Hai. Outro teste de resiliência ocorreu em seu primeiro ano de operação (2023). Naquela época, uma subvenção financeira que a Alternō esperava receber para sustentar suas atividades de pesquisa e desenvolvimento foi adiada em cerca de 4 a 5 meses devido a problemas processuais. A falta de fluxo de caixa ajudou a Alternō a perceber os riscos inerentes a uma empresa de tecnologia: se muito tempo fosse gasto em laboratórios de pesquisa, dependendo ao mesmo tempo de financiamento externo, a empresa poderia perder o fôlego antes de ver seu produto chegar ao mercado. A partir daí, a equipe estabeleceu como meta a comercialização mais rápida, incorporando as necessidades dos clientes diretamente no processo de desenvolvimento tecnológico. Ao iniciar o projeto Alternō E, desde a ideia inicial até a versão de teste comercial, a equipe levou apenas cerca de 18 meses. "Se este investimento não produzir um produto funcional, então será um investimento malsucedido", afirmou o CEO da Alternō. Competir com produtos importados Como uma das clientes da Alternō, a Sra. Pham Thi Thuy Trang, Diretora da Phuc Khang Phat Production Co., Ltd. (marca de café Arista), ofereceu uma perspectiva prática sobre o valor da tecnologia quando implementada em fábricas. A Sra. Trang afirmou que a Arista é especializada na produção de café instantâneo para exportação. Desde o início da construção da fábrica, a empresa estabeleceu requisitos rigorosos para o controle preciso da temperatura, otimização dos custos de energia e preparou-se para atender aos padrões cada vez mais elevados de produção sustentável no mercado internacional. Você também pode gostar Durante a busca por uma solução, a Arista considerou diversas opções. Segundo a Sra. Trang, para o mesmo escopo de sistema, importar um sistema completo da Alemanha ou do Japão provavelmente custaria cerca de 15 vezes mais do que a solução completa proposta pela Alternō. VOLTRICELLopens in a new tab is a brand-new suite of materials designed to optimize battery manufacturing processes and improve the performance of todays battery and emerging sodium-ion, silicon-anode and solid-state battery technologies. It is Dows first material platform designed specifically for supporting optimal electrochemistry inside the cell. As battery technologies continue to evolve, manufacturers face growing pressure to improve energy density, extend cycle life, increase charging speed and scale production across multiple chemistries and manufacturing approaches. VOLTRICELL brings together Dows growing portfolio of battery cell materials under a unified platform designed to support innovation across electrodes, separators, coatings and battery cell packaging applications. The portfolio includes binders, dispersants, rheology modifiers, surfactants and specialty additives that can be selected and combined to help support performance, manufacturability and scalability. In the battery industry, there are a multitude of chemistries and cell manufacturing strategies in play today and under development for the future, said Joel McDonald, Global Technical Director for Dow MobilityScience. Battery manufacturers need materials partners that can evolve with their technology roadmaps. Through VOLTRICELL, we can help customers innovate with confidence, leveraging Dows broad toolbox to support todays cell chemistries and the next generation of energy storage. Designing Materials that Support the Whole Battery The launch of VOLTRICELL reflects Dows continued commitment to the industry and to customers across the battery value chain. By combining deep materials science expertise with application development capabilities and global technical support through its global MobilityScience Studiosopens in a new tab, Dow helps battery manufacturers accelerate innovation from cell design to system-level integration. At The Battery Show North America 2026, Dow will also showcase its latest materials to support battery fire protection including: - VORAFORCE TP1415 Polyol: a polyurethane resin system for manufacturing lightweight fiber-reinforced composites, designed to support impact resistance, corrosion resistance and flame-retardant performance in polyurethane pultrusion applications - DOWSIL EF-6559 Silicone Foam: a two-part, expanding foam for narrow, complex shapes within battery assemblies that forms a protective ceramic layer when exposed to high heat and is designed to support thermal management and electrical insulation in high-volume series production - DOWSIL FC-2024 Coating: one-part RTV coating applied to battery housings, enclosures and lids to support battery fire protection by forming a hard protective ceramic layer during a thermal event and is intended for a cylindrical, prismatic or pouch-based battery system Visitors can meet with Dow experts at Booth #3000 in Exhibit Halls A-E to explore how advanced materials are helping drive the next generation of battery innovation. For more information and to schedule a meeting with Dow at or before The Battery Show North America, visit https://www.dow.com/en-us/market/mkt-mobility/sub-mobility-electronics/app-mobility-elec-battery-systems.htmlopens in a new tab. About Dow Dow (NYSE: DOW) is one of the worlds leading materials science companies, serving customers in high-growth markets such as packaging, infrastructure, mobility and consumer applications. Our global breadth, asset integration and scale, customer-focused innovation and leading business positions enable us to achieve profitable growth and help deliver a sustainable future. We operate manufacturing sites in 29 countries and employed approximately 34,600 people as of year-end 2025. Dow delivered sales of approximately $40 billion in 2025. References to Dow or the Company mean Dow Inc. and its subsidiaries. Learn more about us at www.dow.comopens in a new tab. artigo.texto: In between jeers and boos from an audience of Elizabeth Township residents, a Bucks County-based developer laid out an initial concept for a sprawling data center campus on a 549-acre former landfill bordering the Youghigheny River on Tuesday night. Tim Hendricks, a New Hope resident, told attendees that he hopes to develop a 20-building data center campus and associated natural gas power plant at a township-organized town hall meeting. Communications between Hendricks and local officials obtained by Pittsburgh’s Public Source last week revealed several project plans presented to the township over the summer. Those plans for a 549-acre parcel on Henderson Road near the Youghiogheny River included anywhere from 11 to 28 two-story data center buildings. They were met with opposition from some residents and advocates last week, and hesitancy from the local state representative. Hendricks provided few specific details regarding the final size, scope and environmental impact of the project at the town hall, stressing that the project was still in its development phase. “A project like this obviously has an impact on the community, everybody knows that,” Hendricks said. “We don’t know anything about what’s going to get approved.” Hendricks has not formally submitted any plans to the township or applied for any permits. “Frankly, Elizabeth Township deserves better than another sales pitch about how an industrial project is going to save this community,” said Joelle Whiteman, a township resident and local organizer for the D.C.-based advocacy organization Food & Water Watch, in an interview prior to the meeting. Whiteman is also a member of Protect Elizabeth Township, an environmental advocacy organization that was originally formed to oppose a power plant previously intended for the site. Whiteman, who has been collecting signatures for a petition to stop the development, said she has signed up 350 residents. Attendees, who nearly filled most of the Elizabeth Forward Middle School auditorium, raised questions regarding the water and energy demands of the site, its proximity to houses in the area, the planned natural gas plant and noise concerns. Many in the crowd held signs and wore pins opposing the project. The crowd applauded after one resident shouted, “We don’t want this.” Hendricks said he couldn’t provide specific numbers regarding the site’s water and electricity usage, but said that there was “no way” the site would have an impact on residents’ electricity bills. He also said it would use less water than “typical factories.” The data center buildings would be 2,000 feet away from the nearest homes in the township, a community of manufactured homes called Rolling Hills Village. Noise “will not exceed anything that exists today,” Hendricks said. “Everything is designed so far back from the homes that we don’t have [noise] as an issue.” Hendricks said the data center buildings would be around 150,000 square feet each, which would total 3 million square feet, dwarfing a planned site in Springdale Borough opposed by some local residents. “We’re at step one, maybe step two. There’s probably 100 steps,” Hendricks said, adding that he hadn’t previously attended a meeting this early on in a data center process. He said he’d have to obtain permits from the township, state and potentially the Federal government. State official not convinced State Rep. Andrew Kuzma, R-Elizabeth Township, previously expressed hesitation about some aspects of the project. In an interview after the meeting, he said he is opposed to the project in its entirety. “There is no end user, there are no facts that are in writing and it’s apparent a majority of the residents are against it,” said Kuzma. At the meeting, Hendricks said he was in discussion with end users but did not identify them. Hendricks said his role in the development is to identify the property and obtain all the required permits and approvals. Another person or company would build and operate the property, he said. The proposal became public on Sept. 15, when township commission President Josh Walls announced at a commission meeting that Elizabeth had been approached about a data center project. Tuesday’s town hall was moderated by Eric Piper, a township redevelopment authority member, who asked selected questions submitted by residents. Piper said he received 330 questions from residents that he condensed into 45. Elizabeth Township by the numbers - 22.8 square miles - 12,690 population - 92% white (vs. 76% countywide) - 5.7% in poverty (vs. 11.5%) - $80,589 median household income (vs. $78,548) - $167,000 median value of owner-occupied homes (vs. $227,600) Source: U.S. Census American Community Survey data compiled by Census Reporter The site could generate $125 million in annual tax revenue for the municipality and Elizabeth Forward School District, according to Hendricks’ emails to commissioners. Hendricks reiterated the $125 million number at the town hall. The township expects to bring in around $10.6 million in revenue in 2026, according to its budget. The district brought in $52 million in revenue during the 2024-2025 school year. “Everybody wants this township to be bailed out,” Whiteman said. “Seeing a number that high, I understand why some of the elected officials are like, ‘Oh, this could really save us.’” Walls said that he could not comment on the revenue figures because they were not prepared by the township or local taxing bodies. Walls also stressed that the development is still in the discussion phase. “There’s a lot of residents with very, very serious concerns. Without adequate answers to those, I could not personally support this project moving forward,” he said. artigo.texto: Planejado para abrigar até 17 edifícios verticais e três subestações com 600 MW, o Campus Tamboré, da Scala Data Centers, em Barueri (SP) — considerado um dos principais do setor da América Latina e um dos maiores do mundo — está avançando no projeto de expansão de sua capacidade. Com mais de 220 mil m² de área total e cerca de 150 mil m² já edificados, o complexo já possui dez prédios construídos, sendo oito em operação. “Hoje temos dez edifícios construídos, três subestações energizadas e uma infraestrutura preparada para novas expansões conforme a demanda do mercado”, afirmou Carlos Nomura, head de Construção da Scala Data Centers. Durante as fases iniciais de implantação, o canteiro de obras reuniu cerca de 3.500 trabalhadores, além de mobilizar fornecedores, empresas de engenharia e prestadores de serviços especializados. A empresa aposta em uma engenharia própria e soluções customizadas. A adoção de sistemas construtivos modulares e industrializados também contribui para reduzir prazos e aumentar a previsibilidade das obras. Outro destaque do Campus Tamboré, é que os clientes utilizam sistemas de resfriamento a ar, com uma infraestrutura preparada para incorporar tecnologias de resfriamento líquido, tendência associada a ambientes de alta densidade computacional – como é o caso dos data centers. Ainda de acordo com a companhia, toda a energia consumida pela empresa é proveniente de fontes renováveis contratadas por meio de parques eólicos e solares. A companhia também busca certificações internacionais de desempenho ambiental. Fundada em 2020, a Scala Data Centers atua no Brasil, Chile, Colômbia e México, atendendo principalmente clientes hyperscale e edge. No país, além do complexo em Barueri, a empresa está construindo uma cidade de data centers em Eldorado do Sul (RS). PROJETO NO RIO GRANDE DO SUL REFLETE A CORRIDA POR DATA CENTER Em desenvolvimento na região metropolitana de Porto Alegre, em Eldorado do Sul, a Scala AI City terá capacidade inicial de 54 megawatts (MW) de TI, mas foi planejada para alcançar até 4,75 gigawatts (GW) em sua configuração final. O projeto está sendo construído em uma área que poderá chegar a 10 milhões de m². Um dos marcos recentes para a implantação do complexo ocorreu em maio de 2025, quando o Ministério de Minas e Energia autorizou a conexão de 5 GW à rede elétrica. O empreendimento será instalado próximo à subestação Guaíba 3, infraestrutura que oferece condições para suportar a expansão prevista para os próximos anos. Além da energia, fatores como disponibilidade de áreas para crescimento, segurança regulatória e condições climáticas também influenciaram a escolha do município gaúcho. O terreno destinado ao projeto foi enquadrado como distrito industrial voltado à instalação de data centers, criando um ambiente favorável para investimentos de longo prazo. Outro aspecto relevante, é que no Scala AI City a infraestrutura foi projetada para operar com sistemas de resfriamento líquido e suportar racks com densidade superior à encontrada em instalações tradicionais. O novo campus também será integrado ao data center que a Scala mantém em Porto Alegre e deverá se conectar futuramente ao cabo submarino Malbec, que interliga Brasil e Argentina. A expectativa é ampliar a capacidade de transmissão de dados e fortalecer a inserção da região em rotas internacionais de conectividade. Nova York suspende aprovação de datacenters Cresce a oposição das comunidades à construção de data centers nos EUA. Nova York decretou moratória na aprovação de novos projetos desses empreendimentos e vai realizar estudos sobre o impacto nas redes de energia e no uso de recursos hídricos. A suspensão do governo de Nova York tem validade de um ano e impede a aprovação de novas licenças ambientais para instalações com potência de 50 megawatts ou mais. Conheça Carlos Nomura Carlos Nomura atua há mais de 38 anos na cadeia da construção civil e instalações. Iniciou a carreira na área de projetos de instalações elétricas e na área de Automação Industrial, com foco em programação de PLC. Atuou também fora do país, por 5 anos no Japão, onde trabalhou em projetos de instalações elétricas participando da execução de hangares, usinas de beneficiamentos de materiais, edifícios comerciais e indústrias diversas. Custos ainda são o principal desafio para novos investimentos no Brasil O Regime Especial de Tributação para Serviços de Data Center (Redata) foi sancionado pelo presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva no dia 15 de setembro. O programa concede incentivos fiscais para estimular a instalação, ampliação e modernização de centros de processamento de dados no Brasil. O texto suspende a cobrança de Imposto de Importação na aquisição de equipamentos destinados aos empreendimentos. Executivos da área avaliam que o Brasil reúne condições favoráveis para ampliar sua participação no mercado global de infraestrutura digital e inteligência artificial. A disponibilidade de energia renovável em larga escala e a extensa rede de fibra óptica aparecem entre os principais atrativos. No entanto, especialistas apontam que a competitividade do país dependerá da definição de regras e, principalmente, da redução dos custos operacionais e tributários. A expansão dos data centers tem impulsionado resultados de fornecedores globais do setor. Na Schneider Electric, por exemplo, a atividade foi um dos destaques do desempenho registrado no primeiro trimestre em diferentes regiões, incluindo América do Norte, Europa, China e Austrália. Globalmente, os centros de dados respondem por cerca de um quarto da receita da companhia. Além da expectativa em torno do Redata, representantes do setor defendem outras medidas para reduzir o custo de implantação de novas estruturas. Entre as propostas em discussão estão a diminuição do ICMS incidente sobre equipamentos de tecnologia da informação e comunicação e a revisão das alíquotas de importação aplicadas a itens como servidores e semicondutores.
