artigo.texto: Interior Secretary Doug Burgum spent Wednesday evening in Fairbanks, after campaigning with President Trump in Wasilla earlier this week. Burgum spoke at a Fairbanks Chamber of Commerce event, where he touted Alaska’s potential for Artificial Intelligence data centers. He held up a project in his home state of North Dakota as an example. “We have people knocking on our door that want to drop 10 billion on a data center, and they don't want any tax breaks,” Burgum said. “We said, ‘Hey, we're worried about electric rates.’ They said, ‘Don't worry, we'll do a rebate for everybody in the entire area.’” But that pitch comes amid looming questions about the region’s power supply. Golden Valley Electric Association, the utility co-op that serves Fairbanks and surrounding communities, issued its first-ever energy emergency alert on Monday. The alert urged users to conserve electricity and prepare for possible outages until Wednesday morning. The utility said the problem that caused the shortage will take years to fix. Data centers see public pushback Burgum said Alaska has the resources to become an economic powerhouse, and he blamed regulatory and permitting processes for holding back that development. He said he hopes Congress will pass legislation to roll back environmental regulations after the midterm elections. The sole Democratic candidate in Alaska’s gubernatorial race, Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, attended Burgum’s speech as an audience member. Kreiss-Tomkins said he mostly agrees with Burgum about Alaska’s potential for oil and gas development, but not about data centers. He said he favored a more cautious approach. “I think we should pause,” Kreiss-Tomkins said. “We should make sure that we have laws in place that protect the public interest. And then, in a thoughtful way, development can proceed.” Alaska has seen proposals for as many as 15 data centers, including on military land near Railbelt and Interior communities. They’ve drawn pushback from Alaska residents. In July, state officials received more than 500 public comments on a proposed North Slope data center and power plant. And in August, the Fairbanks North Star Borough Assembly passed a resolution to ask the Alaska Legislature to impose a moratorium on data centers, pending a plan to address community concerns.

artigo.texto: A Tower Semiconductor (NASDAQ:TSEM) e a Semtech Corporation (NASDAQ:SMTC) expandiram sua parceria de fabricação de longo prazo por meio de um novo acordo plurianual, projetado para aumentar a capacidade de produção de silício-germânio (SiGe) para produtos avançados de conectividade de data centers. Anunciado em 13 de outubro de 2026, o acordo fornecerá à Semtech capacidade de produção dedicada nas instalações de fabricação da Tower Semiconductor nos Estados Unidos, Israel e Japão. O acordo visa atender à crescente demanda por tecnologias de interconexão óptica e de cobre de alta velocidade utilizadas em infraestrutura de inteligência artificial e centros de dados. O acordo ampliado dá continuidade a uma parceria que já dura aproximadamente 20 anos e inclui planos para desenvolver futuras gerações de tecnologia de conectividade. Os detalhes financeiros do acordo não foram divulgados. Capacidade dedicada de SiGe em três regiões de fabricação Nos termos do acordo ampliado, a Semtech garantirá capacidade de fabricação dedicada de SiGe nas instalações da Tower Semiconductor em três países. A distribuição geográfica tem como objetivo melhorar a resiliência do fornecimento e proporcionar maior flexibilidade de fabricação à medida que a demanda por componentes avançados para centros de dados aumenta. A tecnologia de semicondutores SiGe é utilizada em aplicações de alta frequência que exigem alto desempenho de sinal e transmissão de dados eficiente. A Semtech utiliza os processos de fabricação SiGe da Tower para diversos produtos de seu portfólio de integridade de sinal, incluindo amplificadores de transimpedância, drivers de modulador, drivers de laser e equalizadores lineares. Esses componentes suportam comunicações de alta velocidade, processando, amplificando e mantendo os sinais elétricos usados em sistemas de interconexão óptica e de cobre. As empresas esperam que a capacidade de produção adicional ajude a Semtech a atender às futuras necessidades dos clientes, ao mesmo tempo que apoia o desenvolvimento de redes de data centers cada vez mais avançadas. Ao garantir recursos de produção em várias regiões, a Semtech também visa reduzir sua dependência de locais de fabricação individuais. Acordo prevê suporte para conectividade de 800G, 1.6T e futura de 3.2T A expansão da produção abrange várias gerações de tecnologia de interconexão de alta velocidade. As empresas afirmaram que o acordo dará suporte aos produtos de conectividade atuais de 800G e 1,6T, bem como às futuras tecnologias que operam em velocidades de 3,2T e superiores. Esses avanços estão se tornando cada vez mais importantes à medida que as cargas de trabalho de inteligência artificial criam uma demanda maior por conexões de alta largura de banda entre sistemas de computação. Os modernos centros de dados de IA exigem que grandes volumes de informações se movam entre processadores, servidores e equipamentos de rede. À medida que a infraestrutura de computação se expande, o desempenho das interconexões pode influenciar a eficiência geral do sistema e a capacidade de suportar cargas de trabalho cada vez mais complexas. Os produtos de conectividade óptica e de cobre da Semtech são projetados para atender a esses requisitos por meio de processamento e transmissão de sinal de alta velocidade. O acordo de fabricação ampliado tem como objetivo fornecer a capacidade de produção necessária para dar suporte às gerações sucessivas dessas tecnologias. A Semtech destaca a importância da conectividade com IA O presidente e diretor executivo da Semtech, Hong Hou, enfatizou a crescente importância da infraestrutura de conectividade no suporte a sistemas de inteligência artificial. “A conectividade tornou-se um fator crucial para determinar o alcance da escalabilidade dos sistemas de IA”, disse Hou. “Atender a essa demanda exige planejamento de capacidade a longo prazo e compromissos firmes com nossos parceiros de fabricação.” Seus comentários refletiram a crescente importância dos componentes semicondutores que possibilitam a comunicação entre os sistemas de centros de dados. Com o crescimento da infraestrutura de IA, os fabricantes buscam garantir que a disponibilidade de componentes de rede acompanhe a demanda por equipamentos de computação. A ampliação da parceria com a Tower tem como objetivo proporcionar à Semtech maior visibilidade sobre sua futura capacidade de produção. A Semtech recebe o Prêmio de Inovação em Tecnologia Óptica O anúncio surge na sequência do recente reconhecimento do trabalho da Semtech em conectividade óptica de alta velocidade. Na Conferência Europeia de Comunicação Óptica (ECOC) 2026, a Semtech recebeu um prêmio de Inovação em Componentes Ópticos por sua família de amplificadores de transimpedância de 224 Gbps por canal. Os produtos são projetados para óptica linear plugável e são fabricados utilizando a tecnologia de processo SiGe da Tower Semiconductor. Os amplificadores de transimpedância são componentes importantes em receptores ópticos, convertendo sinais de corrente elétrica gerados por fotodetectores em sinais de tensão que podem ser processados por outros sistemas eletrônicos. O prêmio destacou uma família de produtos desenvolvida por meio da relação de fabricação já estabelecida entre as empresas. artigo.texto: BlackRock CEO Larry Fink warned that a halt to data center construction could trigger an economic slowdown. "If we have a moratorium of some sort in this country, we will be in a recession," Fink told CNBC Wednesday, after BlackRock reported better-than-expected third-quarter earnings early Wednesday. BlackRock advanced about 1% in late morning trading. "So much of our economy is based on the buildout of this capex," Fink added, referring to the massive investments made to develop artificial intelligence infrastructure. Fink's warning comes as strong, local opposition to data center construction has emerged as a key issue in the Nov. 3 midterm elections, as communities struggle with rising utility costs, water use, environmental damage and questions over investment transparency. While Fink acknowledged fears about the data center buildout, he also noted "most of it is on misinformation." The stakes are high. Wall Street analysts estimate total AI capital expenditures could climb above $1 trillion in 2027 and total in excess of $5 trillion by 2030. "Data centers are not the problem. They're creating more new jobs than ever before," the BlackRock CEO explained. The scale of investment has created demand for construction workers, physical digital infrastructure, AI compute hardware and energy infrastructure to secure grid power, he said.

artigo.texto: Siga o Times Brasil - Licenciado Exclusivo CNBC no Dell despenca 11% e lidera queda de empresas de data centers por temor com IA Publicado 14/10/2026 • 18:07 | Atualizado há 13 horas OpenAI é processada em oito estados nos EUA devido a preocupações com a segurança do ChatGPT Bank of America contratou 1.000 terceirizados para corrigir falhas de software expostas pelo Mythos da Anthropic Trump vai recorrer da decisão que impede a Casa Branca de banir a MS NOW, a CNN e a Politico Netflix demite mais de 1.000 funcionários, cerca de 6% de seu quadro, em meio à desaceleração do crescimento ASML divulga resultados acima da expectativa do mercado, carteira de pedidos até 2030 e ações puxam índices europeus KEY POINTS Foto: Wikimedia Commons As ações da Dell despencaram 11% nesta quarta-feira (14) e arrastaram outros fabricantes de equipamentos para data centers, em meio ao aumento das preocupações de que os gastos corporativos com inteligência artificial não justifiquem a expansão da infraestrutura de IA. Hewlett-Packard Enterprise (HPE), Oracle e Super Micro também acompanharam o movimento de queda. Leia também: Dell dispara 11% em NY após reportar faturamento recorde impulsionado por IA Em relatório enviado a clientes nesta quarta-feira, analistas do Barclays rebaixaram as recomendações para Dell, HPE e NetApp, após uma valorização significativa das ações e diante de dúvidas sobre o momento da adoção da IA pelas empresas. Os fabricantes de servidores para data centers e de outros equipamentos de infraestrutura estiveram entre os preferidos de Wall Street neste ano, graças ao otimismo de que venderiam grandes volumes de produtos associados à demanda por chips e sistemas de IA nos próximos anos. A Dell acumula alta superior a 300% em 2026, enquanto a HPE avançou cerca de 160% e a NetApp dobrou de valor. O sentimento em relação à infraestrutura de IA, porém, mudou recentemente, em parte por causa de dados preocupantes sobre a receita da OpenAI e do receio de que a alta dos juros torne mais difícil financiar uma expansão que depende fortemente de dívida. Leia também: Ações de Nvidia, Oracle, CoreWeave e outras empresas de IA despencam após dados sobre receita da OpenAI A Oracle, que recorre intensamente a empréstimos, caiu 9% nesta quarta-feira e acumula perda de 33% no ano. Já a CoreWeave, fornecedora de infraestrutura de nuvem para IA, despencou 15%, apagando seus ganhos de 2026. Siga o Times | CNBC no Google e receba as principais notícias do Brasil e do Mundo. Siga o Times | CNBC Os analistas do Barclays afirmaram que ainda não observaram uma “inflexão significativa da IA” nos gastos corporativos com produtos da Dell, HPE e NetApp. Por isso, reduziram a classificação das três empresas do equivalente a compra para manutenção. Na avaliação do banco, o aumento das receitas está relacionado à escassez global de memória, já que as empresas de infraestrutura repassaram aos clientes os preços mais altos desses componentes. Leia também: Wall Street avalia impacto de possível desaceleração da IA na expansão de data centers “Há um sentimento crescente de que a adoção da IA pelas empresas está criando uma renovação do parque de hardware”, escreveram os analistas do Barclays, acrescentando que as companhias costumam destinar apenas 5% de seus orçamentos de tecnologia da informação à IA. “Acreditamos que as fortes receitas corporativas sejam mais uma consequência dos custos de memória do que de uma migração para a IA empresarial neste momento.” Os analistas também constataram que apenas cerca de um quarto dos gastos corporativos totais com IA é destinado a hardware. Eles afirmaram que a normalização e, posteriormente, a queda dos preços de memória poderão pressionar as receitas das empresas de infraestrutura. O setor de memória é conhecido por seus ciclos acentuados, e as ações foram atingidas nesta semana depois que a chinesa ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) informou, no fim de semana, avanços em uma nova estrutura de chips. Latest articles by Peter View Peter Albin's full profile Chenglin Wu Research Analyst, Carbon Markets Chenglin Wu Research Analyst, Carbon Markets Chenglin analyzes compliance carbon markets and global climate policies. Latest articles by Chenglin - Opinion Four carbon policy developments set to impact E&P decision-making in H2 - Opinion 4 carbon policy developments that impact E&P decision-making - The Edge Five key takeaways from COP30 View Chenglin Wu's full profile Haotian Ni Research Analyst, Carbon Mitigations, Carbon Management Haotian Ni Research Analyst, Carbon Mitigations, Carbon Management Haotian is a CCUS expert focused on carbon capture project valuation, market and policy analysis across APAC, View Haotian Ni's full profile Shashank Atreya Senior Research Analyst, Carbon Markets, Carbon Management Shashank Atreya Senior Research Analyst, Carbon Markets, Carbon Management Shashank focuses on the North American carbon market and covers both the voluntary and compliance markets. Latest articles by Shashank View Shashank Atreya's full profile As we have repeatedly emphasised in 2026, carbon policy has become a key factor in commercial decision making for oil and gas exploration and production (E&P). Many E&P firms are required to comply with the Emissions Trading Schemes (ETS) in place in different jurisdictions around the world. Keeping up with proposed and implemented changes to these schemes is therefore vital. Our research analysts have been closely tracking ETS globally throughout Q3 2026. Read on to get our take on the implications of the European Commission’s proposed changes to the EU ETS, or fill out the form to download a complimentary insight with views on this and three other policy developments destined to have a material impact for E&P firms globally. The European Commission ETS review aims to trade pressures for incentives Aiming for implementation in 2028, the European Union ETS review looks to align carbon market rules with the EU’s overall target of 90% net emissions reduction by 2040 (versus 1990 levels). Key proposals include: - Cap phase-out and Linear Reduction Factor (LRF): Downward adjustment of the fixed annual percentage rate at which the total cap on greenhouse gas emissions decreases - Market Stability Reserve (MSR): Removal of the invalidation mechanism, cutting the intake rate and lowering the buffer for the mechanism to balance supply and demand of emissions allowances - Free allocation and carbon leakage: Changing the timelines for free allocation phase-out by sector based on level of carbon leakage risk - Sectoral expansion: Changing the rules for aviation, maritime and waste sectors to cover more cases - Carbon removals, international offsets and carbon capture and utilisation (CCU) accounting: - Allowances for centralised purchase of domestic carbon dioxide removal (CDR) - Allowances for the purchase of offsets from non-EU countries - Changes to allow embedded emissions in non-permanent CCU products to be accounted for at release rather than capture - Revenue: At least 50% of ETS auction revenues to be directed towards decarbonisation - Industrial Decarbonisation Bank (IDB) Fund: Financing initially to be “first-come, first-served” to unlock ready-to-go projects, then competitive bidding that prioritises lowest abatement cost - International cooperation: Non-EU countries can opt in to price aviation and maritime emissions on routes and split revenue with the EU Our take: - Market fundamentals: If adopted, the proposals will lower the risk of extreme end-game price spikes without eliminating the bulk of emissions reduction obligations. The long-term price trajectory will be more predictable albeit lower, but the targeted financial help should compensate. - Accelerating investment: Measures signal that capital is available but must be actively pursued and progress demonstrated. Support for individual companies will be based on the credibility of their decarbonisation plans. The IDB could push hard-to-abate sectors towards built capacity significantly earlier. - Global implications: The proposal points to a more collaborative role for the EU in global carbon markets. Non-EU companies stand to benefit via international credit mechanisms from 2036, while the proposal also signals willingness to help non-EU countries build carbon pricing capacity. The reform also raises questions for the EU’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM). artigo.texto: Three county leaders called for local data center development oversight and protections for Harris County residents during a press conference Oct. 15. The overview Harris County Attorney Abbie Kamin, alongside county commissioners Adrian Garcia and Lesley Briones, held a press conference to ask the state legislature to expand the county’s authority to oversee data center development. The three Democratic officials are seeking reelection in November. Currently, counties have “little to no authority” to stop data centers from developing in the county, Briones said. “We need to be informed so we can be leaning in to do everything we can to protect our community and environment,” Briones said. During its Oct. 15 meeting, the Harris County Commissioners Court passed a motion to increase information on oversight. The court’s action will require: - County departments to notify the court when major data centers apply for permits - The County Attorney’s Office to report on the county’s existing authority and oversight over data center development - The county’s Office of Intergovernmental and Global Affairs to identify and advocate for statutory changes to strengthen county oversight in unincorporated areas during the next legislative session Harris County has 55 operating, under construction or planned data centers, according to agenda documents. In Texas, Harris County is second to Dallas County in the number of data centers, per a press release. The background In September, Gov. Greg Abbott directed the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality to halt all data center permits until the state can complete an audit, per previous Community Impact reporting. The decision bars state agencies from advancing regulatory approvals on data center development until the audit is complete. Kamin said the findings are expected in December. “We know data centers place a significant demand on our electrical grid, our water supply, air quality and impact the neighborhoods around them,” Kamin said. “Whether a project is a net benefit depends largely on where it’s located, how it’s designed and in terms under which they’re approved. The question is, ‘What can Harris County do about this?’” Harris County is not permitted to regulate data center locations through zoning because the county does not have zoning laws, Kamin said. According to agenda documents, residents near existing and proposed data center sites have raised concerns about: - Environmental impacts - Grid reliability - Noise - Property values - Public safety - Utility costs - Water and energy use Kamin said CenterPoint Energy, the county’s primary utility provider, expects to connect eight gigawatts of new data center load in the Houston area by 2029, with about four additional gigawatts to follow. That would increase “peak demand” in the region by about half, she said. Large data centers can generate significant tax revenue, but they require substantial land, electricity, water and supporting infrastructure while creating relatively few permanent jobs, agenda documents state. Kamin said state law offers sales tax exemptions of 10-20 years to qualifying data centers. “This isn’t about being against technology or new technology, but growth has to go hand in hand with accountability,” Kamin said. “And any facility that comes to our county should follow the rules, be a good neighbor and be transparent with the community that they are joining.” What’s next Garcia said the upcoming legislative session, which begins in January, will be an opportunity to regain some local control. “We need real authority and the opportunity to have a real voice,” Garcia said. Garcia, a board member of the Texas Conference of Urban Counties, said the group is working to bring “meaningful legislation” to obtain local control and “make sure that we are protecting the quality of life of our neighbors.” “We are working to understand what opportunities the county has in terms of legal authority,” Garcia said. “But the reality is that there’s very little. That’s the bottom line. There’s very little that the county can do. However, we have to work toward legislation to make sure that local officials have an actual seat at the table.”

artigo.texto: Mecklenburg County supervisors voted unanimously Tuesday to postpone until November any decision on a siting agreement for a proposed 100-megawatt battery energy storage facility northwest of Chase City. In another land-use matter, supervisors gave the green light for a proposed residential development in the Clarksville area, The Faireborough at Shiney Rock, which is described by its developers as a “Shire-like” village of 20 cottages on a family farm. In the Chase City area, TerraForm Power is proposing to build the Mitchell Energy Center on a 170-acre site near Fort Mitchell Road, Lenhart Road and Virginia 49, close to the existing Otter Creek Solar development. TerraForm Power says the battery facility would occupy about 10 to 15 acres, with the remainder of the site timbered. Access would be gained from Lenhart Road. Under an agreement being negotiated, TerraForm will pay the county $2.9 million after receiving a special exception permit authorizing the project to move forward. That payment would be followed by another $3.9 million over the project’s anticipated 20-year lifespan. Three Chase City residents — Kathy Keel, Charles Jackson and Carlos Davis — urged supervisors to reject the project. Davis, at times raising his voice, said battery storage, data centers and solar projects approved near Chase City “do nothing for us [the residents of Chase City].” He said he was tired of the town “looking like a dump site” because of the industrial development around it and would rather see more stores and amenities. Keel questioned whether the project could strain water resources needed by the town and raised concerns about possible contamination of nearby land in the event of a fire or other hazardous incident. Tony Deyerle, representing TerraForm, outlined what he described as the project’s economic and energy benefits. He estimated the facility would generate an $8.5 million economic benefit during construction, create as many as 30 jobs and produce another $6.8 million in tax revenue. Deyerle said the facility would help meet growing electricity demand, improve the resilience and reliability of the local power grid, and store energy for release when demand peaks. He also argued that the facility could help prevent future brownouts as Mecklenburg County’s energy needs increase. In the other land-use matter, supervisors approved Laurie Pearson’s request for a special exception permit to develop The Faireborough at Shiney Rock, a 20-cottage, “shire-like” village on a century-old family farm off Union Chapel Road. The owners have described the project as a woodland retreat of quaint, earth-sheltered cottages intended to attract tourism while preserving the area’s rural character. Tom Tanner moved to approve the permit. Tanner, Brenda Blackwell, Claudia Lundy, Board Chair Jim Jennings, David Brankley, Sterling Wilkinson and Dennis Spence voted in favor. Vice Chair Andy Hargrove and Kirk Gravitt voted against the request without explaining their votes. Nearby resident Herbert Ramsey and Clarksville resident David Billings opposed the project, questioning whether it was suitable for an area dominated by farmland. Ramsey told supervisors that he operates a trucking and hauling business nearby and that his property is zoned commercial rather than agricultural. Pat Charles, executive director of the Clarksville Lake Country Chamber of Commerce and a board member of Historic Downtown Clarksville, supported the proposal, saying it advances one of the county and region’s key goals: promoting tourism. In approving the permit, supervisors overruled the Mecklenburg County Planning Commission, which recommended denial of the project. In other business, supervisors also adopted amendments to the county zoning ordinance. The revisions grew out of an Aug. 17 review by the board’s legislative committee and a subsequent recommendation from the planning commission. County officials said the changes are intended to clarify and improve development standards. One amendment clarifies what vehicles and business equipment may be kept at a residence by someone operating a home-based business. Tanner raised the issue, saying the ordinance should not prevent lawn-maintenance operators from storing trailers, tractors or similar equipment at home. For lakefront lots, revised language allows certain accessory buildings to be placed toward the road-facing front of a parcel instead of beside or behind the house, helping homeowners preserve lake views. The amendments also clarify which large recreational equipment must be kept under cover. Other changes set a five-story height limit in R-3 residential districts to better fit the county’s rural character; adjust setbacks for accessory structures; extend the validity of a variance from one year to two; require food trucks to obtain permits from both the health department and fire marshal; clarify special-event requirements; require temporary construction facilities to comply with the Statewide Fire Prevention Code; and make a perimeter access road a condition of special exception approval for battery-storage sites. In other action, supervisors approved a boundary adjustment with the Town of South Hill and conveyed a 0.386-acre strip of land along Virginia 92 to VDOT to allow construction of a turn lane near Chase City.

artigo.texto: Microsoft Pushes Custom AI Chips with Azure Maia 300 Microsoft unveiled Maia 300, its third-generation AI chip, as Maia 200 goes live, powering Copilot. Microsoft on Monday (Oct. 12) unveiled Maia 300, its third-generation in-house AI accelerator, and said that Maia 200 is now in production, powering Copilot and other Microsoft cloud services. The company said it plans to scale deployments of its Azure Maia processor family at multi-gigawatt scale in 2027, positioning Maia as a primary inference system for Microsoft products and services, according to a blog post by Scott Guthrie, Microsoft’s executive vice president, cloud + AI. Microsoft said Maia 200 is deployed across its data centers in the US, Europe, and Australia, delivers up to 1.7 times more tokens per watt than leading GPU infrastructure, and powers built-in AI capabilities in Microsoft Teams, Copilot, and Cowork. By the end of the year, the chip is also expected to power GitHub Copilot and Microsoft Foundry, a platform for developing, deploying, and managing AI applications and agents, according to Guthrie’s blog post. Maia 300, which Microsoft said will be deployed in production in 2027, is designed with an inference-first architecture optimized “for long-context, memory-intensive, and decode-heavy AI workloads,” according to the blog post. The company said the chip is expected to deliver 40% more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU-based systems and, in a full 96-accelerator rack, up to seven times the rack-scale token throughput of Maia 200. Like other hyperscalers, Microsoft continues to rely heavily on Nvidia and AMD GPUs for AI workloads. At the same time, it has spent the last few years building its own custom silicon to improve performance and efficiency across its infrastructure and cloud services. Unlike Amazon Web Services, which offers Trainium and Inferentia chips via public cloud instances, and Google Cloud, which provides access to its TPUs, Microsoft has not made Maia available to customer workloads via Azure instances. In Monday’s blog post, the company did not say whether that could change in the future. Because Microsoft is using Maia primarily for internal workloads, the competitive dynamic is different from a traditional chip war among hyperscalers, said Matt Kimball, vice president and principal analyst at Moor Insights & Strategy. This is about Microsoft and other cloud providers delivering services faster, more efficiently, and more reliably. “That’s good for the customer because they’re getting better quality of service, and it’s good for the cloud provider because they’re doing it at lower cost, which means they’re more profitable,” Kimball said. Kimball said that Maia 300 appears to represent a significant step forward in Microsoft’s custom silicon strategy. “Maia 100 was a proof of concept. Then 200 came out, and they solved the issues they had seen in the 100. They are powering GitHub and Copilot,” he said. “It validated the design choices they were making, and 300 was where they said, ‘Let’s go big,’ and that’s what you are seeing with the Maia 300.” Microsoft’s plan to deploy the Azure Maia family at multi-gigawatt scale suggests broad global adoption across its infrastructure, Kimball noted. “It’s going to be used very broadly to support their workloads across the globe,” he said.

artigo.texto: North Carolina’s official policies on two hot-button issues — data centers and marijuana — are widely out of step with what North Carolina voters say they want, according to a new WRAL/WSOC Poll. The Republican-led state legislature for years has refused to allow a vote on bills that would legalize or decriminalize marijuana for recreational use. The state Senate has passed bills in several recent years to legalize medical marijuana, under what sponsors say would be the strictest rules in the country. But the state House has never allowed that legislation up for a vote. Other WRAL Top Stories The new poll, out Friday, found that only 15% of North Carolina voters oppose medical marijuana, and 74% want it legal — including majorities of every age group, political party, region of the state, and racial or ethnic demographic. As more states legalize marijuana, more people are becoming familiar with the drug — particularly if they know someone using it for medical reasons, said Ken Alper, the president of Survey USA, which conducted the poll. “They're much more comfortable with it than they would have been 10 or 20 years ago,” Alper said. Similarly, the poll found that full legalization of marijuana — not just for medical purposes, but for recreational use, too — is supported by 63% of the population. The poll shows 52% of Republicans, 73% of Democrats and 65% of independents support marijuana legalization. The only demographic in which a majority of voters don’t support legal marijuana is among those age 65 or older. But even those voters aren’t necessarily opposed to the idea. The poll found a tie, at 42% each, for support or opposition among senior citizens with another 16% undecided. North Carolinians are likely becoming more open to the idea of recreational marijuana legalization because they’ve seen it done in other states and “society hasn’t collapsed,” Alper said. Marijuana is illegal under federal law, but dozens of U.S. states have legalized it. And nearly all states have legalized medical marijuana prescriptions for certain ailments. North Carolina is among the remaining states to resist any form of legalization. A state advisory council formed by Democratic Gov. Josh Stein is recommending that North Carolina lawmakers legalize marijuana through a tightly regulated system that would allow retail sales to adults — a shift that the group says will make consumption safer and bring millions of dollars in revenue to the state. The more states that legalize marijuana, the more likely the federal government will be to relax its laws, said Chris Cooper, a Western Carolina University political scientist. “The one thing everybody agrees on is that the current system is confusing: what's legal, what's legal where, and the rationale behind that,” Cooper said. Meanwhile 42% opposed their development, with 29% saying North Carolina should oppose additional data-center development in the state. Another 13% said the state should support the moratoriums that are in place in several parts of the state. Sixteen percent said they don't know enough to have an opinion. Support for at least some data-center development was at 53% among Republicans, while 58% of Democrats opposed the development. Data center development is so divisive that high-profile political candidates are likely to punt on the issue, Cooper said. “What we're going to see a lot of is folks running for federal office saying, ‘Let's give the power to local governments,’” Cooper said. “That's going to be the rhetorical strategy going forward: Not folks saying we need a ban, not saying folks we should embrace it, but let local people decide.” Decisions on whether to allow data centers to be built can require a balance between promoting economic growth and protecting local residents, state lawmakers said this year as they debated restrictions for data centers without banning development altogether. But critics have raised concerns that they could use too much water or electricity, and that the loud hum they produce is annoying to people who live nearby. The tech industry, meanwhile, opposes the regulation as it looks for ways to store enormous amounts of data as the use of artificial intelligence grows. Lawmakers had proposed requiring large data centers to cover electricity and infrastructure costs associated with building and operating them, while also tightening rules on where they can be built, who can own them and how much water they use. They also sought to ban local governments from paying companies incentives to build data centers. Some local governments around North Carolina have banned data centers, while others have enacted moratoriums to come up with policies to guide their development. Some communities have sought to lure data centers with economic incentives. Democratic Gov. artigo.texto: The prime ministers of Denmark, Sweden and Finland have urged the European Union to leave the emissions trading system untouched, warning that any loosening of its rules would put industrial investment at risk and slow the fall in emissions. Their letter went on October 14 to European Council President António Costa, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin, whose country holds the rotating presidency of the Council of the European Union. Mette Frederiksen of Denmark, Ulf Kristersson of Sweden and Petteri Orpo of Finland said the integrity and ambition of the scheme had to be preserved. Known as the ETS, it obliges the most polluting industries to pay for the carbon dioxide they emit. Weakening it “would undermine the predictability on which investment decisions depend”, the three wrote, and would risk slowing the pace of industrial decarbonisation. Lighter obligations on heavy emitters would simply move the burden on to other parts of the economy, they argued, forcing deeper cuts elsewhere to meet the bloc’s climate targets. The three governments want a steady and demanding reduction in the number of allowances available on the market, so that companies keep cutting their pollution. They also want to retain the mechanisms that adjust the supply of permits and prevent sharp swings in their price. Carbon pricing had been among the most effective and cheapest instruments of European climate policy over the past two decades, the letter said, and had driven innovation and the modernisation of industry. Europe’s shift to climate neutrality required long-term investment on an unprecedented scale, the leaders added, and companies needed predictable and reliable rules before committing the money. The appeal lands as Brussels retreats on one green file after another. The Commission proposed in July to slow the pace of emissions cuts in the carbon market and to extend free permits for heavy industry until 2038, and a day before the summit it moved to delay methane reporting duties for importers of gas, oil and coal. EU leaders meet in Brussels on October 15-16 with the review of the carbon market on the agenda. Italy, the Czech Republic and Estonia are among those pressing to push ETS2, the new market covering road transport and heating fuels, beyond its 2028 start. The three Nordic capitals have fought off earlier attempts at postponement, with Luxembourg alongside them. Their difficulty is that the mood has shifted, with high energy prices and the cost of living pushing other member states to seek relief for households and industry rather than tighter carbon rules.

artigo.texto: Volkswagen, Ford and Tesla are among the electric carmakers whose batteries may contain nickel mined in indigenous woodlands plagued by deforestation, an analysis has found, highlighting the struggle to make vehicles that are free from environmental destruction. Corporate disclosures and trade flows from the last two years show mines in the battery supply chains of automotive giants are linked to the loss of trees in Sulawesi, a wildlife hotspot in Indonesia that houses the world’s largest nickel deposits. The metal is widely used in cathodes in car batteries because it boosts energy density and increases range. Ore from the Cahaya and Hengjaya mines was traced through regional smelters and Chinese processing plants run by Zhejiang Huayou Cobalt, a cathode manufacturer that supplies CATL, the world’s largest battery maker. Huayou’s corporate reports list US and European carmakers as end-users, while additional corporate files and trade data show a separate route from Huayou to LG, a South Korean group that also supplies battery products to leading carmakers, via Poland. Satellite analysis shows the mines have led to widespread deforestation of primary rainforest in nickel-rich lands inhabited by the indigenous Tolaki people. “We used to ask the forest for protection in return for our offerings,” said Wadimula, a Tolaki elder whose home sits on the edge of the 21,000-hectare Cahaya mining concession. “Destroying it means destroying our own life.” Electric vehicles are less environmentally harmful than fossil fuel-burning engines, which spew gases that foul the air and heat the planet, but western carmakers have struggled to clean up supply chains for batteries built with critical minerals from Africa, Asia and South America. Environmental groups warn that a failure to curb the boom of material-hungry SUVs is exacerbating the destruction by increasing the quantity mined. Ore from the two mining concessions is sent to a nickel smelter in an industrial complex in Morowali, on Indonesia’s eastern coast, operated by Huayou’s local subsidiary, where limonite is refined into mixed hydroxide precipitate, the primary raw material used to make battery cathodes. In 2024, $606m worth of mixed hydroxide precipitate was shipped from the Morowali plant to ports in China, followed by further shipments worth $470m in 2025. The processed ore was transported overland to Huayou cathode manufacturing sites in Quzhou, near Shanghai, and Yulin, near the border with Vietnam. Public filings do not disclose specific volumes or timings of sales from Huayou to CATL, which would be needed to directly connect specific ore shipments to car batteries, but Huayou confirmed group-level supplies to CATL in response to a regulatory inquiry by the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2024. Chengdu B&M, a downstream subsidiary of Huayou, has also confirmed the supply of “large quantities” to CATL. The investigation, published in partnership with Voxeurop and other European media partners, traced shipments from mines and refineries in Sulawesi to China, and then again from Huayou cathode and CATL battery factories to the assembly lines of carmakers in the US and Europe. Volkswagen’s facility in Braunschweig, for instance, received a shipment in October 2024 of 24 tonnes of cell modules worth about $390,000, according to data from Volza, a trade platform. The shift to a carbon-free economy is pushing up demand for critical minerals in countries with weak environmental safeguards, though experts have argued the mining boom can be tempered without slowing the shift away from dirty fuels. In 2023, a report found lithium demand in the US transport sector could be reduced by 18% to 66% compared with a business-as-usual scenario, by improving public transport, walking and cycling more, and buying smaller cars. Better recycling could bring demand reductions as high as 92%, the report found. Global demand for nickel is set to double to 5.5m tonnes by 2040, according to the International Energy Agency, much of it mined in Indonesia and then refined in China. The loss of trees in mining concessions means the carbon footprint of nickel from the worst mines may be up to 500 times greater than previously reported, a study in Nature Communications found last year. The Cahaya and Hengjaya mines are located in woodlands designated as “production forest”, which are intended for forestry rather than industrial activities. However, successive Indonesian governments have weakened safeguards and carved out exemptions for miners as demand for nickel has soared. Nickel mining may be responsible for two-thirds of the forest loss recorded since 2001 within the area encompassed by the Cahaya concession, and over half of the loss in the Hengjaya concession, spatial analysis conducted by geospatial firm The TreeMap suggests. Sulawesi Cahaya Mineral (SCM), the company that operates the Cahaya mine, contributed to clearing an additional 330 hectares of forest in 2024, according to an analysis by Auriga, an Indonesian nonprofit. The same year, it delivered 11m tonnes of limonite ore – almost all of its production – to Huayou’s smelter. Deliveries increased to nearly 12.5m tonnes throughout 2025. The plant also continued to receive ore from the Hengjaya mine by road, local lorry drivers said. SCM received two administrative sanctions last year for illegally clearing more than 450 hectares of forest beyond the boundaries of its permitted clearing area. The company is a subsidiary of Merdeka Battery Materials, part of a group whose shareholders include Huayou and CATL. The carmakers identified as end-users of Huayou cathodes or recipients of shipments from CATL include Volkswagen, Volvo, Ford, General Motors, Tesla, BMW, Stellantis and Hyundai. Mercedes-Benz was separately linked to Huayou. Many of the companies said they did not source nickel directly, they assessed and mitigated adverse impacts, and they required suppliers to comply with responsible sourcing standards.

artigo.texto: Data centers have emerged as a top political issue in the 2026 midterm elections, and one of the few to unite Democrats and Republicans. A recent poll from Quinnipiac found 73% of voters say they would oppose the building of an AI data center in their community, including 55% of Republicans, 85% of Democrats and 76% of Independents. Those numbers were echoed in a recent Vermont Public poll that found 64% would support a ban on large-scale data centers in that state. The thing is, there aren’t any large-scale AI data centers in Vermont — or anywhere else in New England — at least not yet. This region isn’t seeing the data center boom that’s created so much controversy in other parts of the U.S. The week of Oct. 19, 2026, the NENC stations will explore some of the reasons why not in a special series called Awaiting Data. The week-long series will consist of audio, digital and video stories on topics including: - Why large AI data centers aren't being built in New England, and how the region is preparing for a future where they do come to town - Skepticism of the tech industry that’s fueling some of the opposition in our region - New England’s tradition of local control, giving residents a forum and tools to fight data center development - How leaders in the region’s tech and robotics fields view the role of data centers in the growth of AI - How retrofits of existing data centers could bring more AI capability to New England Awaiting Data’s contributing stations are WBUR, NHPR, Connecticut Public, and NEPM.

artigo.texto: Amazon rallies support for Tri-State data center plan ahead of possible voter ban TRENTON, Ohio (WKRC) - Amazon is ramping up its push for a proposed data center complex in Trenton as voters prepare to decide in a few weeks whether to ban data centers entirely. At Edgewood Middle School, Amazon set up booths addressing topics that have come up in public meetings, including noise, jobs, water, and energy usage, ahead of the November vote on whether the complex of 18 data centers can move forward. “Many people interact with a data center every day without even knowing it. So if you stream Netflix, if your doctor stores your records online, if you play keynote at the local bar, if you're doing anything that's interacting with the internet, you're running through a data center at some point in time,” said Brandon Oyer, AWS energy and water director. Oyer said the project would bring utility costs down and use less water than some residents fear. “Three percent of the year we're going to use water for cooling, so 97% of the year, we're going to use zero water for cooling; there's just going to be outside air that'll blow across the servers. That'll keep everything cool and let us operate,” Oyer said. While Amazon’s event was held inside, opponents of the project and the effort to change the city charter and ban data centers were outside. “I want to be able to do my homework. I want to understand their side; I want to understand their new processes, possibly better than Prologis,” said Amy Humbert of the Water for Charter Change PAC. “And so, this was my way of saying, 'Change my mind. Try to change me to a no-look.'" John Werkman did not say what Amazon would do if it lost the vote but said the project would create hundreds of long-term jobs if it gets the “green light.” “At least 500 AWS employees are going to be employed at these facilities if they do get built. What that does not count is the non-employee contractors that are also going to be on site. Electricians, pipe fitters, and fiber splicers,” Werkman said. The debate over the data center proposal came as Trenton Mayor Ryan Perry announced his resignation at the Trenton City Council meeting a couple hours ago, effective Jan. 1. “I have moved on in my career, and I have moved to a place where I don't have that kind of time to spend with the citizens anymore, and that's irresponsible for me,” Perry said. Perry did not mention the long-running data center conflict in his remarks.

artigo.texto: GreenYellow and Tilt Energy Partner to Deploy Battery Storage at Industrial Sites GreenYellow finances and operates the batteries, while Tilt Energy handles their dispatch and market valorisation. The two companies launch a behind-the-meter storage offer with no upfront investment for industrial and commercial sites. GreenYellow and Tilt Energy announce a partnership aimed at accelerating the deployment of Behind-the-Meter (BTM) electricity storage systems in the industrial and commercial sectors. According to the two companies, the offer is built on an integrated, contractually backed Battery Energy Storage System (BESS). Energy storage is drawing in other players across different segments, such as Trinasolar, which is unveiling 760 W solar modules and battery storage in Vietnam, or, on the gas side, Naftogaz and Siemens Energy, which are considering five compressor units for Ukrainian gas storage. GreenYellow describes itself as an industrial orchestrator of flexible electrification since 2007, and Tilt Energy as a specialist in valorising electrical flexibility. A split of roles between financing and dispatch GreenYellow designs, finances, builds, operates and maintains the energy storage infrastructure. Tilt Energy handles its real-time dispatch and valorises the flexibility on electricity markets. The two companies say this complementarity gives customers access to a solution combining infrastructure, financing and energy management. They state that the offer allows customers to benefit from storage flexibility with no upfront investment, no exposure to electricity market risk and with contractually guaranteed performance. Company GreenYellow: company profile Three obstacles identified by the partners According to GreenYellow and Tilt Energy, many companies remain held back despite growing interest in batteries. The partners cite three obstacles: the level of initial investment, the technical and operational complexity of projects, and uncertainty around flexibility revenues. In the proposed model, GreenYellow bears the investment and performance commitments are contractualised. Operation of the asset and valorisation of its flexibility are entrusted to specialists, and the customer receives a turnkey solution. The two companies specify that the offer goes beyond a simple "Battery-as-a-Service" formula, without the customer having to handle the complexities of financing, operation and valorisation. Storage integrated into flexible electrification GreenYellow places this offer within a broader vision of flexible electrification. The company says the aim is not only to install a battery but to integrate it into a package combining energy efficiency, electrification of uses, local renewable power generation and smart management. "Electricity storage should no longer be considered as a mere energy technology, but as a full-fledged industrial infrastructure," says Mathieu Cambet, Strategy Director at GreenYellow. He adds that companies need solutions that improve their efficiency and resilience without tying up more capital. artigo.texto: O país abriga 71% da capacidade em construção na região, impulsionado pela inteligência artificial e nuvem. A expansão exige engenharia avançada e forte uso de energia renovável, consolidando o Brasil no mercado digital. O Brasil se firmou como o maior mercado de infraestrutura digital da América Latina. De acordo com o relatório da JLL, o país concentra 71% da capacidade de data centers atualmente em construção na região. Além disso, abriga aproximadamente 48% da capacidade instalada que já está em operação. Esse crescimento é impulsionado pela rápida evolução da inteligência artificial, da computação em nuvem e da digitalização dos serviços. A mudança de hábitos de consumidores, empresas e governos aumentou drasticamente a quantidade de dados que precisam ser armazenados e processados com segurança. - O Brasil lidera a América Latina com 71% dos data centers em construção. - A inteligência artificial e a nuvem são os principais motores dessa expansão. - A energia renovável brasileira dá vantagem competitiva ao país. - Data centers são estruturas críticas que exigem funcionamento 24 horas por dia. - A integração entre engenharia e operação reduz riscos e custos dos projetos. Energia limpa fortalece a competitividade A matriz elétrica brasileira, rica em fontes renováveis como hidrelétrica, eólica e solar, é uma das grandes vantagens do país. Essa característica favorece a implantação de data centers que atendem às metas globais de redução de emissões de carbono. Os novos projetos vêm incorporando soluções de eficiência ambiental, sistemas avançados de refrigeração e redução do consumo de água. Há também uma busca ativa por certificações internacionais, como LEED e normas ISO, que garantem a sustentabilidade das operações. Apesar da energia limpa, o setor exige grandes volumes de energia com qualidade e estabilidade. Marco Alberto Silva, cofundador e CEO do Grupo Engemon, afirma que um data center precisa ser concebido como um ecossistema integrado. Sistemas elétricos, climatização, automação, conectividade, segurança e prevenção de incêndios devem funcionar de maneira coordenada, com alta disponibilidade e redundância. É essa visão completa que permite reduzir riscos e garantir a continuidade das operações. Engenharia integrada reduz riscos e prazos Os data centers são estruturas de missão crítica, onde uma interrupção pode comprometer serviços financeiros, bancos digitais e sistemas públicos. A Engemon atua nesse mercado oferecendo soluções que vão do planejamento à manutenção, acompanhando o empreendimento em todas as fases. A atuação integrada permite compatibilizar sistemas elétricos, mecânicos, de automação e segurança. Em uma instalação que funciona ininterruptamente, essa coordenação é essencial para a confiabilidade. Silva acrescenta que na Engemon, trabalhamos para que cada solução seja dimensionada de acordo com a realidade e as necessidades do cliente. A integração entre engenharia, construção, tecnologia, operação e manutenção permite antecipar interferências, acelerar a implantação e entregar uma infraestrutura mais segura, eficiente e preparada para futuras expansões. A empresa também integra serviços de operação e monitoramento contínuo. Esse modelo reduz a fragmentação entre fornecedores diferentes e aumenta a previsibilidade, essencial em projetos de alta complexidade técnica e grandes investimentos. Desafios para o protagonismo global Ainda que líder na região, o Brasil precisa expandir sua infraestrutura energética e fortalecer a conectividade para se aproximar dos maiores mercados globais. É necessário estimular a formação de profissionais especializados e oferecer previsibilidade regulatória para investimentos de longo prazo. A demanda deve continuar crescendo com a popularização da inteligência artificial generativa e a digitalização industrial. O relatório da JLL aponta que os mercados de colocation e hyperscale mantiveram crescimento sustentável na América Latina em 2025, com o inventário de colocation da região avançando 20% em um ano. Empresas que integram engenharia, tecnologia e sustentabilidade terão papel estratégico na transformação do potencial brasileiro em infraestrutura efetiva. O próximo passo é transformar as vantagens territoriais e energéticas em condições para que o país avance entre os principais polos globais da economia digital.

artigo.texto: - Ukrainian drones attacked Russia's largest data center, targeting Russia's AI ambitions. - Sberbank's systems remain operational; Yandex's supercomputers' status is unclear. - Western sanctions are also hindering Russia's AI progress, complicating its chip purchases from China. MOSCOW — Ukrainian drones hit Russia's biggest data center on Wednesday, part of a series of attacks appearing to target Moscow's ambitions to develop Russian artificial intelligence capabilities on a par with those from the U.S. and China. The strike on the Balakovo data center, owned by Sberbank, the country's largest bank and technology company, followed three attacks in the past week on data centres owned by Russian technology group Yandex. "We confirm that the data processing center was attacked. At the same time, all of Sberbank's systems and services are operating normally and without disruption," Sberbank First Deputy CEO Alexander Vedyakhin told reporters. President Vladimir Putin held a previously unannounced meeting on Wednesday with top officials on "information security," in which Sberbank CEO German Gref took part. The Kremlin said that the meeting was not linked to the attacks on data centers. Russia's state RIA Novosti news agency reported in 2024 that the Sberbank center hit on Wednesday would host Russia's biggest supercomputer, which is scheduled to go into operation in 2027. The Yandex data centres, hit earlier, hosted all three of that company's operating supercomputers. Neither Yandex nor Sberbank has said whether supercomputers, used to train the AI models, were damaged in the Ukrainian attacks. Along with Yandex, its main domestic rival, Sberbank is Russia's leading developer of artificial intelligence. The domestic market is shared between Sberbank's GigaChat model and YandexGPT. Difficulties purchasing chips Both companies have invested heavily in the development of their models but lag global leaders in the United States and China by up to nine months, according to Sberbank's own estimates, partly due to Western sanctions which hinder Russia's access to the most advanced hardware. "It's clear what difficulties we face when purchasing modern graphics processing units. Both we and Yandex suffer from this," Gref said on Sept. 29, calling it the biggest reason why Russia lags behind the U.S. and China in AI. Sberbank is in talks to buy chips from Chinese makers, but in an interview with Reuters on June 3, Vedyakhin said that chipmaker Nvidia's monopoly on its CUDA software platform, which has become an AI industry standard, is an even greater problem. Yandex said previously that its supercomputers operated on Nvidia A100 chips, a model launched in 2020 and since then succeeded by more advanced H100 chips. Sberbank has two functioning supercomputers. The most advanced one, called Christofari Neo, ranked 167th in the Top 500 list of the world's most powerful supercomputers, is located in Moscow and is based on Nvidia A100 chips. Yandex's most advanced Chervonenkis supercomputer is ranked No. 101 in the same list. IT expert Mikhail Klimarev told Reuters it could take a long time to replace the chips due to Western sanctions, while damage to the supercomputers could set back the Russian AI industry, which already suffered from sanctions. "The equipment is being imported, but it's done at a high cost, through indirect routes. First, you need to negotiate so that someone is willing to sell it to you and is not afraid of sanctions," he said. Protect assets Some commentators compared the lack of reported disruption at state-controlled Sberbank with Yandex, whose taxi and food delivery units had reported disruptions, saying it showed that Sberbank's centers are better protected. "This is a great example of what a business owner can do to protect their assets," wrote military blogger Alexander Kots. Under an August decree by Putin, the state can take over administration of poorly protected facilities. The Sberbank site is located close to the Balakovo nuclear power plant, which the data centre uses as an energy source, and the Saratov hydroelectric power plant. No damage was reported to either plant from the attack. Ukraine says it is responding to Russian attacks on its own data sites. Both countries have attacked each other's refineries, power stations, ports and e-commerce companies. Russia's digital development ministry said this week it was in talks with the military on protecting the data centers, while some lawmakers called for them to be moved underground where the hardware will be out of reach for drones. "We need a so-called Doomsday data vault," Valery Yermakov, deputy CEO of state-controlled Rostelecom, another major data center operator, told a conference in Moscow. Contributing: Gleb Stolyarov

artigo.texto: Siga o Times Brasil - Licenciado Exclusivo CNBC no A vantagem brasileira na corrida pelos data centers Publicado 14/10/2026 • 12:00 | Atualizado há 12 horas OpenAI é processada em oito estados nos EUA devido a preocupações com a segurança do ChatGPT Bank of America contratou 1.000 terceirizados para corrigir falhas de software expostas pelo Mythos da Anthropic Trump vai recorrer da decisão que impede a Casa Branca de banir a MS NOW, a CNN e a Politico Netflix demite mais de 1.000 funcionários, cerca de 6% de seu quadro, em meio à desaceleração do crescimento ASML divulga resultados acima da expectativa do mercado, carteira de pedidos até 2030 e ações puxam índices europeus Foto: Divulgação/Ascenty A inteligência artificial parece existir na nuvem, mas sua infraestrutura é profundamente física. Por trás de cada modelo ou agente inteligente existem servidores, chips, redes, sistemas de refrigeração e instalações que funcionam 24 horas por dia. A nuvem, afinal, tem endereço, ocupa terreno, consome energia e precisa ser resfriada. Estamos entrando em uma transformação mais profunda: inteligência deixa de ser apenas uma capacidade humana e passa a existir também como infraestrutura disponível em escala. Carros poderão dirigir sem motorista, fábricas operar com crescente autonomia e agentes de IA comprar, contratar e negociar. Governos poderão antecipar congestionamentos, fraudes e falhas de infraestrutura. É a capacidade de produzir, decidir e antecipar multiplicada por milhões de máquinas. Mas inteligência em escala exige energia em escala. Segundo a Agência Internacional de Energia, os data centers consumiram cerca de 485 TWh de eletricidade em 2025 e poderão chegar a 950 TWh em 2030, ligeiramente mais que todo o consumo atual do Japão. A revolução aparentemente imaterial da IA encontrou um limite concreto: eletricidade. Isso começa a mudar a geografia da economia digital. Conectividade, segurança e talentos continuam importantes, mas uma nova pergunta entrou na mesa: onde está a energia? Servidores podem ser instalados rapidamente; redes de transmissão e geração levam anos. A infraestrutura digital começa a correr mais rápido do que a energética que precisa sustentá-la. Há ainda a água. Sistemas de refrigeração podem demandar volumes relevantes. A questão não é ser a favor ou contra data centers, mas quais queremos, onde instalá-los e com que padrões de eficiência. Reúso de água, refrigeração eficiente e energia de baixo carbono podem transformar restrição ambiental em vantagem competitiva. É aqui que o Brasil ganha relevância. Em 2025, 86,8% da matriz elétrica brasileira foi renovável; eólica e solar responderam juntas por 26,4% da geração. Poucos grandes mercados combinam escala territorial e econômica com uma matriz dessa natureza. Na economia da IA, um ativo que durante décadas enxergamos principalmente como ambiental passa a ser também tecnológico. Siga o Times | CNBC no Google e receba as principais notícias do Brasil e do Mundo. Siga o Times | CNBC A dimensão do movimento já aparece nos números. Em junho de 2026, o Ministério de Minas e Energia informou 38 GW em pedidos de acesso relacionados a data centers, dos quais 7,1 GW estavam associados a cerca de R$ 159 bilhões em investimentos previstos. Os 38 GW superam em mais de duas vezes e meia a capacidade instalada de Itaipu. São grandezas distintas, mas revelam a pressão potencial sobre o sistema. O Redata, aprovado pela Câmara em fevereiro, prevê benefícios tributários e contrapartidas. Mas a questão decisiva será menos quantos servidores atrairemos e mais quanto valor permanecerá no país. Um data center isolado é infraestrutura. Ligado a energia, telecomunicações, software, universidades, fornecedores e talentos, pode integrar um ecossistema de inovação. Estados e municípios disputarão esses investimentos como no passado disputaram montadoras e siderúrgicas. Os vencedores dificilmente serão os que oferecerem apenas o maior incentivo fiscal, mas os que conseguirem combinar energia, água, conectividade, licenciamento, qualificação profissional e integração com a economia regional. A próxima fronteira da inteligência artificial será definida tanto pelos algoritmos quanto pela infraestrutura capaz de executá-los. O Brasil pode transformar energia de baixo carbono, eficiência ambiental e escala territorial em uma razão para esses investimentos virem para cá. Na economia da IA, sustentabilidade não precisa ser o preço que se paga pelo desenvolvimento. Pode ser uma de suas vantagens competitivas. artigo.texto: O Ministério Público Federal (MPF) instaurou um procedimento administrativo para acompanhar o diálogo entre comunidades tradicionais da Reserva Extrativista Cazumbá-Iracema, no Acre, e a empresa Joias Ecológicas da Amazônia Desenvolvimento de Projetos Ltda. sobre a possibilidade de implantação de um projeto de geração de créditos de carbono na unidade de conservação. A medida foi formalizada por meio da Portaria nº 54/2026, assinada pelo procurador da República Luidgi Merlo Paiva dos Santos, publicada nesta quinta-feira (15). O procedimento terá duração de um ano e tem como objetivo acompanhar o processo de diálogo e uma eventual consulta livre, prévia e informada das comunidades sobre o projeto. O mecanismo garante que os povos e comunidades tradicionais sejam ouvidos antes da adoção de medidas que possam afetar seus territórios, modos de vida e interesses. De acordo com a portaria, a empresa informou ao MPF, por meio do Ofício nº 004/2026, que realizou reuniões informativas nos núcleos de base da reserva, a convite da Associação dos Seringueiros do Seringal Cazumbá (ASSC). A empresa também convidou o órgão federal para acompanhar uma assembleia comunitária destinada à apresentação dos resultados dessa etapa e à manifestação das comunidades sobre a eventual abertura do processo formal de consulta. A atuação do MPF considera as regras previstas na Convenção nº 169 da Organização Internacional do Trabalho (OIT), que assegura aos povos interessados o direito de serem consultados por meio de suas instituições representativas, de boa-fé e com o objetivo de alcançar um acordo ou obter consentimento sobre as medidas propostas. A portaria também cita a Lei nº 15.042/2024, que estabelece regras para o mercado de carbono e reconhece às comunidades extrativistas a titularidade originária dos créditos de carbono gerados em reservas extrativistas. A legislação permite o desenvolvimento de projetos desse tipo em unidades de conservação de uso sustentável, desde que não haja impedimento no plano de manejo. A norma prevê ainda que a comercialização de créditos de carbono por povos e comunidades tradicionais, por meio de suas entidades representativas, depende de consentimento obtido após consulta livre, prévia e informada. O processo deve respeitar os protocolos de consulta elaborados pelas próprias comunidades, quando existentes, e ser custeado integralmente pelo interessado no desenvolvimento do projeto, com participação e supervisão da 6ª Câmara de Coordenação e Revisão do MPF. Entre as garantias previstas na legislação estão a repartição justa e equitativa dos benefícios financeiros, a gestão participativa dos recursos e a previsão contratual de indenização por eventuais danos coletivos, materiais e imateriais. Nos projetos de REDD+ de abordagem de mercado, a lei assegura às comunidades o direito a pelo menos 70% dos créditos decorrentes dos projetos, conforme as condições legais aplicáveis.

artigo.texto: Câmara aprova urgência para PL que muda divisão de custos de armazenamento de energia Em redação dada pela lei de 2025, foi fixado que os sistemas de armazenamento de energia, na forma de baterias, terão custos de contratação rateados apenas entre os geradores de energia A Câmara dos Deputados aprovou nesta terça-feira (13) o requerimento de urgência do projeto de lei que abre margem para o custo da contratação de baterias ser arcado pelos usuários finais de energia elétrica do Sistema Interligado Nacional (SIN), incluídos os consumidores. Ainda não há data para a votação do mérito do texto (PL 3716/2026), que deve ficar para após o segundo turno. Em redação dada pela lei de 2025, foi fixado que os sistemas de armazenamento de energia, na forma de baterias, terão custos de contratação rateados apenas entre os geradores de energia. Isso gerou críticas do setor e um dos argumentos é a falta de um tratamento isonômico. As baterias serão contratadas na modalidade de "reserva de capacidade". Em geral, os custos administrativos e financeiros e os encargos tributários precisam ser rateados entre todos os usuários finais de energia elétrica do SIN, incluídos os consumidores. A exceção, contudo, foi dada aos sistemas de armazenamento de energia. A proposta de mudança é do deputado Arnaldo Jardim (Cidadania-SP). O tema é controverso porque a Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel) já está trabalhando na regulamentação do tema com base na legislação em vigor. Os inéditos leilões para baterias estão previstos para dezembro. Em nota conjunta, um grupo de seis entidades apontou que o armazenamento de energia, inclusive em baterias, é capaz de reduzir outros encargos suportados pelo consumidor ao otimizar a operação do parque gerador em suas diversas fontes. Foi citado estudo da Volt Robotics, ao demonstrar que as baterias podem reduzir a variação do preço da energia (PLD) e o acionamento de termelétricas, gerando economia superior a R$ 1,6 bilhão ao ano para o consumidor. "Os custos da reserva de capacidade são distribuídos entre todos os usuários finais, conforme parâmetros definidos em lei. Porém, apenas os sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias são tratados de maneira diversa, sendo custeados exclusivamente pelos geradores e sem definição legal dos parâmetros de custeio", apontou o grupo de entidades. Assinaram a nota conjunta: a Associação Brasileira de Energia Eólica e Novas Tecnologias (ABEEólica), a Associação Brasileira dos Investidores em Autoprodução de Energia (Abiape), a Associação Brasileira da Indústria do Hidrogênio Verde (ABIHV), a Associação Brasileira de Soluções de Armazenamento de Energia (ABSAE), a Associação Brasileira de Energia Solar Fotovoltaica (Absolar) e a Associação Brasileira dos Produtores Independentes de Energia Elétrica (Apine). O que diz a ABSAE? A Associação Brasileira de Soluções de Armazenamento de Energia (ABSAE) disse em nota que o avanço da proposta com urgência aprovada hoje "é importante para ampliar a segurança jurídica e criar condições mais previsíveis para a realização dos primeiros leilões de baterias em larga escala no Brasil". "A aprovação da urgência representa um avanço para que o Congresso discuta o tema com a celeridade necessária. Em paralelo precisamos olhar para o prazo dos leilões: o sistema elétrico necessita de potência adicional em 2028, e é plenamente possível corrigir a isonomia no rateio enquanto prossegue o cronograma. Assim vamos equilibrar segurança energética, redução de custos sistêmicos e segurança jurídica", afirma Fabio Lima, diretor-executivo da ABSAE.

artigo.texto: ACC (Automotive Cells Company) JV Stellantis, Mercedes, Saft Exide Technologies, headquartered in France, has introduced Solition Powerflex, a modular battery energy storage system (BESS) intended for commercial and industrial use, renewable energy integration, e-mobility infrastructure and agricultural facilities, ESS News reported. The product combines a 261 kWh LFP battery with a 125 kW bidirectional power conversion system (PCS) housed in an outdoor cabinet. In grid-connected setups, as many as 15 cabinets may be paralleled, delivering a maximum combined capacity of 3.915 MWh and 1.875 MW of power output. Off-grid installations can accommodate up to five cabinets. Within each cabinet sit five battery packs, each rated at 52.25 kWh and based on 314 Ah LFP cells. Charge and discharge rates reach 0.5C, while the system runs at 400 V AC and either 50 Hz or 60 Hz. Per the manufacturer's technical datasheet, nominal round-trip efficiency stands at 86%, inclusive of auxiliary power consumption. The IP55-rated outdoor cabinet has dimensions of 1,000 mm x 1,420 mm x 2,250 mm and a weight of approximately 2,720 kg, taking up roughly 1.42 m2. It is built to run at ambient temperatures from -20 C to 50 C, with power derating kicking in above 45 C. A dual-loop liquid cooling and heating system handles thermal management, using separate circuits for the battery and the power conversion system, rated at 5 kW and 3 kW respectively. Built into the cabinet are a battery management system, energy management system, PCS, thermal management and fire protection equipment. Safety provisions encompass automatic aerosol fire suppression, emergency shutdown, audible and visual alarms, explosion relief devices and a dedicated external firefighting interface. Exide stated that the system features a European-developed Storage Control System (SCS) that permits integration with on-site generation assets, grid operators and energy markets. Applications supported include peak shaving, self-consumption optimization, spot-market trading and ancillary services. The control platform further delivers remote monitoring, over-the-air software updates and interfaces for third-party systems. Exide noted that its digital architecture encompasses encrypted remote connections, EU-based data hosting and multilayer access controls. Serge Arbes, senior business director global, energy solutions, at Exide Technologies, said organizations increasingly want to boost energy resilience, integrate renewable generation and optimize energy costs. He added that Solition Powerflex was created to meet these evolving requirements, pairing a scalable architecture with advanced control capabilities in a solution able to adapt to shifting business needs. Standard warranty terms were not disclosed by Exide. The technical datasheet notes that battery capacity and system warranty conditions can be obtained upon request. artigo.texto: Cegonha com carros da BYD tomba em Recife (PE) e causa prejuízo milionário Segundo a Polícia Rodoviária Federal (PRF), o sinistro ocorreu por volta das 4h da madrugada no Km 52 da BR 101, em Paulista, sentido Abreu e Lima Uma carreta com onze carros modelo Dolphin GS, da BYD, tombou no início da manhã desta quarta-feira (14), em Paulista, na Região Metropolitana do Recife (PE). Segundo a Polícia Rodoviária Federal (PRF), o sinistro ocorreu por volta das 4h da madrugada no Km 52 da BR 101, em Paulista, sentido Abreu e Lima. “A suspeita é de que o motorista de um caminhão cegonha perdeu o controle do veículo em uma curva e tombou”, afirmou a PRF. Segundo o órgão federal de fiscalização rodoviária, o motorista ficou ferido e foi encaminhado para uma unidade de saúde. O caminhão está tombado sobre o canteiro central. Cada unidade do BYD Dolphin GS é vendida por R$ 150 mil. Com isso, o prejuízo passa de R$ 1,5 milhão. Apesar do ocorrido, não houve registro de fogo após o acidente com os carros elétricos. Como é o BYD Dolphin GS? O Dolphin GS é o segundo carro elétrico mais vendido do Brasil. Com uma bateria de 44,9 kWh ele consegue rodar 291 km com uma carga completa, segundo os números do Inmetro. Na parte de desempenho, o Dolphin GS tem 95 cv de potência e 18,3 kgfm de torque. A aceleração de 0 a 100 km/h acontece em 10,9 segundos. O modelo vem equipado com chave presencial, piloto automático, sistema de monitoramento da pressão dos pneus, câmera 360º, comandos de voz, conexão de smartphone sem fio com a multimídia e mais. - Comprimento: 4,13 m; - Largura: 1,77 m; - Altura: 1,57 m; - Distância entre eixos: 2,70 m; - Distância do solo: 150 mm.
