artigo.texto: OCP 2026: AI Infrastructure Moves From Scaling to Coordination Key Highlights - Microsoft's Maia 300 roadmap and full-stack co-design strategy reflect the industry's shift toward optimizing AI inference performance per watt and per dollar. - Oracle calls for standardized interfaces between AI data centers and power grids as hyperscale loads create new challenges for utilities and operators. - Intel and HPE emphasize heterogeneous, workload-specific computing architectures rather than one-size-fits-all AI infrastructure. - Google advances the concept of AI for systems, applying artificial intelligence to hardware design, data center operations, capacity planning, and infrastructure efficiency. The next phase of AI infrastructure development may depend less on building bigger systems than on making increasingly complex systems work together. That was a central message running through the second day of keynotes at the 2026 Open Compute Project (OCP) Global Summit in San Jose, where executives from Microsoft, Oracle, HPE, Intel, Google, and the electrical infrastructure industry described an emerging need to coordinate computing, networking, power, cooling, security, and operations as parts of a unified architecture. The discussions extended the opening day's focus on the transformation of data centers into AI factories, shifting attention from the architectural scale of the challenge toward the standards, interfaces, and management capabilities required to make that scale operationally sustainable. Across the presentations, several themes converged. AI inference is increasingly shaping hardware decisions. Power delivery must be engineered in concert with utility infrastructure. Accelerators, CPUs, and networks must operate within more heterogeneous environments. And artificial intelligence itself is becoming a tool for designing and operating the infrastructure on which it depends. Together, these developments suggest that the industry's next competitive frontier will be defined not simply by installed compute capacity, but by how effectively that capacity can be delivered, managed, and converted into useful work. Reynold D’Sa, Microsoft Corporate Vice President of Silicon, Cloud Hardware, and Infrastructure Engineering, addresses the Day 2 keynotes at OCP Global Summit 2026, outlining Microsoft's full-stack AI infrastructure strategy, including its Maia accelerators, 800V DC power architecture, advanced cooling, and open standards for scaling AI from chip to grid. Microsoft: From Frontier Models to Frontier Infrastructure Microsoft Corporate Vice President Reynold D'Sa framed the shift around the transition from increasingly powerful frontier models toward their broader deployment throughout enterprise applications and workflows. The goal, D'Sa argued, is not simply to produce more intelligence, but to make AI useful and accessible across an expanding range of applications. "There can be no frontier firm without a frontier infrastructure," he told attendees. That infrastructure must be optimized for more than raw computational performance. Microsoft is increasingly measuring its architecture in terms of useful intelligence delivered from every watt, byte, chip, and dollar invested. Central to the strategy is full-stack co-design, bringing silicon, software, models, networking, power distribution, and cooling into a coordinated engineering process. D'Sa highlighted Microsoft's newly announced Maia 300 accelerator, its next-generation inference system scheduled to begin production deployments in 2027. Microsoft expects Maia 300 to deliver up to seven times the rack-scale token throughput of Maia 200, its current-generation accelerator, while providing approximately 40% more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU-based systems. The company plans to scale its Maia infrastructure to multi-gigawatt deployments beginning in 2027. The architectural significance extends beyond Microsoft's custom silicon. D'Sa pointed to the Cobalt 200 CPU, designed for the orchestration, retrieval, memory management, and service calls associated with agentic workloads, as another example of infrastructure requirements moving beyond conventional GPU-centric computing. In networking, Microsoft's multipath reliable connection technology is intended to support clusters exceeding 100,000 GPUs using a two-tier network architecture. The company also continues to advance open optical interconnect specifications and Ethernet-based scale-up networking through OCP. Power and cooling are receiving similar attention. Microsoft's Mount Diablo architecture separates power conversion from compute racks, enabling the two systems to scale independently while supporting 800-volt DC distribution. The company is also participating in efforts involving solid-state transformers and common utility-grid interface specifications. Meanwhile, its third-generation Mount Atlas heat exchanger unit is designed to nearly double cooling capacity within the same operational footprint. Taken together, the efforts represent a broader change in infrastructure planning: individual components are no longer sufficient units of optimization. The efficiency of the complete system increasingly determines the economics of the AI service it supports. Pradeep Vincent, Vice President of Compute and AI Infrastructure at Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), addresses the Day 2 keynotes at OCP Global Summit 2026, calling for industry-wide standards governing how large-scale AI data centers interact with power grids, while emphasizing energy efficiency, cooling reliability, and responsible infrastructure development. artigo.texto: Only a predictable, investment-oriented ETS and carbon price can continue driving decarbonization, competitiveness and energy security, a coalition of energy, industry and investor associations said in the runup to the European Council’s meeting in Brussels. The group includes Eurelectric, WindEurope, Nucleareurope and SolarPower Europe. They urge preserving the long-term investment signal and balancing climate ambition with competitiveness. In an open letter to European Council President António Costa and the body’s members, a broad coalition of energy, industry and investor organizations said only a meaningful carbon price can continue driving decarbonization, competitiveness and energy security. The group consists of Eurelectric – Union of the Electricity Industry, WindEurope, Nucleareurope, SolarPower Europe, Federation of European Securities Exchanges (FESE), We Mean Business Coalition and national electricity sector associations. The letter was developed in collaboration with Institutional Investors Group on Climate Change (IIGCC) and its members. In light of the European Council’s two-day meeting that started today, the signatories sent a message that the integrity of the European Union Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) and its long-term investment signal has to be preserved. While EU ETS emissions have halved, the EU economy expanded 30% They called for reinvesting revenues from the mechanism into industrial decarbonization and the energy transition, balancing climate ambition with competitiveness, and keeping decarbonization investments in Europe. “Europe is entering a period of unprecedented investment in its energy system and economy. The sectors our organisations represent contribute hundreds of billions to EU GDP each year and are set to invest trillions by 2050 in the clean energy, energy efficiency, infrastructure and technologies needed to deliver a decarbonised, resilient and competitive EU economy. With Europe’s dependence on imported fossil fuels driving major energy insecurity and price volatility, this investment is urgent,” the letter reads. EU ETS is core part of policy framework According to the group, the policy framework needs to stimulate investor confidence, with EU ETS as a core part. Since 2005, emissions in ETS sectors have fallen by around 50%, while the EU economy has grown by around 30%, showing that carbon pricing can drive emissions reductions cost-effectively, while supporting economic growth, the signatories underscored. “Its influence also extends beyond Europe, as other jurisdictions adopt carbon pricing or seek to link with ours,” they noted. At least 50% of ETS 1 revenues should be reinvested into ETS 1 sector decarbonization As for the integrity of EU ETS, a predictable cap trajectory and rules-based market stability reserve would stimulate demand for homegrown clean energy sources and support innovation, the coalition pointed out. It argued that flexibilities or ad-hoc interventions should not weaken such a long-term signal. At least 50% of ETS 1 revenues should be reinvested into the decarbonization of ETS 1 sectors, the associations added. “We welcome initiatives such as the Investment Booster, the Industrial Decarbonisation Bank and the Innovation Fund, which can help turn the carbon price signal into concrete projects in Europe. These instruments should prioritise mature and scalable decarbonisation solutions, including direct electrification. Remaining revenues should be spent on climate and energy priorities, such as energy efficiency,” the coalition said. Turning to the tradeoff between climate action and competitiveness, it stressed that free allocations should be targeted and conditional, and aligned with the phasein of the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM). The fourth item, keeping decarbonization investments on EU soil, is a proposal for international carbon credits not to substitute domestic emissions reductions under a revision of EU ETS. Any use should be limited to high-integrity credits, deployed indirectly in a predictable manner, the letter said. Energy prices, seven-year EU budget on European Council’s agenda The heads of state or government came to sit with the leaders of the EU administration and discuss, among other issues, the challenges to European competitiveness, including energy prices. Especially important on their calendar is the so-called multiannual financial framework (MFF) – the 27-member bloc’s 2028-2034 budget. In the negotiating box for the current meeting is the introduction of a call rate for revenues from the EU ETS 1. The proposition is 30%, meaning that 30% of the proceeds would go directly to the central budget. The EU administration aims to direct 30% of EU ETS 1 proceeds to the joint budget The member state that hosted the auction of carbon allowances would keep the rest. There is also a 90% call rate for CBAM in the document. The scheme entered fully into force at the beginning of this year and no revenue has been distributed yet. However, the plan was for 75% to go to Brussels. The EU is also creating the European Competitiveness Fund (ECF). The dedicated clean transition and industrial decarbonization item of EUR 55.7 billion would consist of EUR 20.2 billion from the budget and the Innovation Fund covering the rest, according to the negotiation box.

The global flow battery stacks market is entering a decisive growth phase as long-duration energy storage (LDES) shifts from pilot deployments to mainstream grid infrastructure. Flow battery stacks, the modular electrochemical cores of redox flow battery systems, enable independent scaling of power and energy, long cycle life, and inherent safety, making them uniquely suited for storage durations exceeding four hours. Demand is being pulled forward by utility-scale renewable integration, commercial and industrial resilience requirements, and the electrification of remote operations. Vanadium redox flow stacks remain the commercial anchor, while zinc-bromine, iron-chromium, organic, and hybrid chemistries advance toward broader adoption. This report analyzes market size, segmentation, supply chain dynamics, and competitive positioning, providing a data-driven outlook through 2035. It examines how cost reduction, manufacturing scale-up, and policy support for LDES will shape the trajectory of stack demand across five major regions and five end-use sectors. The baseline scenario for the flow battery stacks market through 2035 assumes continued policy support for long-duration energy storage, steady cost declines in stack manufacturing, and accelerating renewable capacity additions. Under this scenario, the market expands at a compound annual growth rate of 18.5% from 2026 to 2035, with the market index rising to 545 by 2035 from a 2025 base of 100. Growth is front-loaded in Asia-Pacific, where utility-scale tenders and manufacturing capacity are concentrated, followed by North America and Europe as grid resilience and decarbonization mandates tighten. Vanadium redox stacks retain the largest share, but zinc-bromine and organic flow chemistries gain ground in cost-sensitive and behind-the-meter applications. Supply chain maturity, membrane and electrode cost reduction, and standardization of stack interfaces are critical enablers. Risks include vanadium price volatility, slower-than-expected policy implementation, and competition from lithium-ion in shorter-duration segments. Overall, the baseline outlook points to a market transitioning from niche to mainstream, with stack manufacturers scaling production and forming strategic partnerships with system integrators and utilities. Utility-scale energy storage is the dominant end-use for flow battery stacks, driven by the need to store excess renewable generation for dispatch during peak demand or low-generation periods. Currently, utilities are procuring flow battery systems for projects ranging from 10 MWh to over 100 MWh, with stacks representing the core power conversion module. Through 2035, demand will accelerate as grid operators seek to replace peaking plants and enhance grid stability. Key demand-side indicators include renewable capacity additions, storage procurement targets, and capacity market reforms. The shift toward longer-duration storage, typically 8 to 24 hours, favors flow battery stacks over lithium-ion due to their scalable energy capacity and low degradation. As utilities gain operational experience, standardizing stack specifications will further reduce costs and drive adoption. Current trend: Rapid expansion driven by LDES tenders and renewable integration mandates. Major trends: Procurement of 8+ hour storage systems in renewable-heavy grids, Integration of flow batteries in capacity markets and ancillary services, Growing preference for non-lithium technologies for fire safety and longevity, and Development of large-scale vanadium and zinc-bromine projects. Representative participants: Sumitomo Electric Industries, Rongke Power, VRB Energy, Invinity Energy Systems, and Stryten Energy. Commercial and industrial (C&I) users are increasingly adopting flow battery stacks for backup power and peak shaving, motivated by grid reliability concerns and rising electricity costs. In this segment, stacks are integrated into systems that provide 4 to 12 hours of backup, often in combination with solar PV. Demand is particularly strong in regions with unstable grids or high demand charges. Through 2035, adoption will be supported by declining stack costs, financing models such as energy-as-a-service, and corporate sustainability targets. Key indicators include commercial construction activity, power outage frequency, and the spread of time-of-use tariffs. Flow battery stacks offer advantages in safety and cycle life, though competition from lithium-ion remains intense for shorter durations. Current trend: Steady growth as businesses prioritize resilience and energy cost management. Major trends: Rising adoption of behind-the-meter storage for demand charge reduction, Corporate decarbonization commitments driving clean backup power, Modular stack designs enabling scalable C&I installations, and Financing innovations lowering upfront cost barriers. Currently, several large-scale projects pair flow batteries with solar or wind farms, and this trend is expected to grow through 2035 as renewable penetration rises. artigo.texto: Nightpeak Energy's Bocanova 2 Battery Storage Project Reaches Financial Close and Commercial Operation Nightpeak Energy reported on October 13, 2026, that its Bocanova 2 battery storage facility in Southeast Texas, sized at 150 MW with a two-hour duration, has achieved both financial close and commercial operation. The company stated the project went into commercial service on September 17, lifting the Bocanova site's total capacity to 300 MW and contributing added flexibility to the ERCOT grid amid surging electricity demand from data centers and other large loads. Located in Brazoria County near the Houston metropolitan area, Bocanova 2 represents the second phase of Nightpeak's battery storage buildout there. Bocanova 1, the initial 150 MW phase, entered commercial operation in August 2025. Tesla's Megapack 2 XL battery storage systems equip the project. It runs under a long-term offtake agreement with an investment-grade counterparty, with financing arranged via a tax equity bridge loan and a construction-to-term loan from MUFG Bank, while U.S. Bank supplied traditional tax equity. Paris Hays, Co-founder and CEO/CDO of Nightpeak Energy, noted that large loads are connecting to the grid at a speed and magnitude that is reshaping how the power sector anticipates new demand. Hays remarked that Texas leads this growth, and addressing it will demand substantial new infrastructure along with resources capable of responding swiftly as conditions shift. Hays further stated that with 300 MW now active at Bocanova, the company is deploying that flexibility in one of the nation's most dynamic power markets, and thanked the City of Alvin, Brazoria County, and the local community for their backing. Founded in 2022, Nightpeak has built and purchased a portfolio exceeding 1 GW of operating and de-risked capacity across gas-fired generation, battery storage, and powered land development, while continuing to push forward an additional pipeline of flexible generation and large-load projects to serve rising U.S. demand. Nightpeak Energy develops, owns, and operates flexible power generation and large-load enablement assets aimed at meeting growing electricity and AI demand while fostering a reliable, lower-carbon electric grid. Using a technology-agnostic strategy spanning gas-fired generation, energy storage, renewables, and large-load project types, the company merges generation and load into integrated solutions for its customers. artigo.texto: Por que a Nvidia apoia a CoreWeave: crise de financiamento da CRWV expõe riscos dos data centers de IA A volatilidade nas ações e títulos da CoreWeave gerou preocupações sobre seu endividamento superior a US$ 40 bilhões e o impacto de juros altos na expansão de data centers de IA. Embora o CEO da Nvidia, Jensen Huang, tenha amenizado os temores ao declarar que a parceira se fortalece, o mercado de crédito exibe alta aversão ao risco, com yields elevados encarecendo o refinanciamento. Como acionista e fornecedora, a Nvidia monitora a situação, visto que gargalos de financiamento em provedoras emergentes de nuvem podem testar a resiliência da demanda por infraestrutura de inteligência artificial e afetar o setor. TradingKey - A volatilidade das ações e títulos da CoreWeave (CRWV) está se tornando um grande teste de estresse para o mercado de infraestrutura de IA, ao mesmo tempo em que coloca sua estreita parceria com a Nvidia (NVDA) sob escrutínio mais uma vez. As ações da CoreWeave despencaram cerca de 15% na quarta-feira, com os preços de seus títulos corporativos caindo em conjunto, à medida que aumentavam as preocupações do mercado de que juros altos e uma dívida massiva pudessem enfraquecer sua capacidade de continuar expandindo data centers de IA. A onda de vendas posteriormente se espalhou para ações de computação em nuvem de IA e data centers, como Nebius (NBIS), Oracle (ORCL), IREN (IREN) e TeraWulf (WULF), arrastando também a Nvidia. Em resposta às dúvidas do mercado, o CEO da Nvidia, Jensen Huang, declarou publicamente em Estocolmo na quinta-feira que a CoreWeave está se fortalecendo, que seu custo de capital na verdade diminuiu e que não há necessidade de a Nvidia fornecer suporte financeiro à empresa. Essas declarações aliviaram parte do pânico, fazendo com que as ações da CoreWeave se recuperassem das mínimas intradiárias e fechassem em alta de cerca de 5,9%. Jensen Huang apoia a CoreWeave enquanto mercado de títulos permanece em alerta máximo As declarações de Jensen Huang enviaram um sinal positivo aos investidores em ações, mas a pressão do mercado de crédito sobre a CoreWeave não desapareceu em paralelo. Dados da ICE Data Services mostraram que o spread dos credit default swaps (CDS) de cinco anos da CoreWeave chegou a subir para 1.194,5 pontos-base, atingindo uma máxima histórica intradiária. Com base em cálculos de modelos relevantes, a precificação de mercado implicava uma probabilidade de inadimplência superior a 60% nos próximos cinco anos. No entanto, essa é apenas uma métrica de risco derivada de premissas como taxas de recuperação de títulos, e não significa que a probabilidade real de inadimplência da empresa tenha sido determinada com precisão. Os preços de alguns títulos de longo prazo da CoreWeave caíram para cerca de 78 a 80 centavos por dólar, com yields ultrapassando 15%. A forte alta nos yields dos títulos significa que, se a empresa precisar captar novos recursos ou refinanciar dívidas existentes por meio do mercado de títulos no futuro, seus custos de financiamento poderão aumentar significativamente. O modelo de negócios da CoreWeave exige investimentos iniciais significativos de capital para adquirir GPUs e construir data centers, enquanto a receita é realizada gradualmente à medida que os clientes utilizam a capacidade computacional. Segundo estimativas do mercado, a empresa possui atualmente mais de US$ 40 bilhões em dívidas, e seu fluxo de caixa livre permanece negativo. Se os custos de financiamento continuarem a subir, os investimentos em capital e as despesas com juros poderão limitar o ritmo de melhoria da lucratividade, mesmo que os pedidos sigam em expansão. A Nvidia é tanto acionista quanto uma grande fornecedora da CoreWeave A saúde financeira da CoreWeave afeta a Nvidia porque as duas empresas mantêm simultaneamente relações societárias, de fornecimento e de clientes. Em janeiro deste ano, a Nvidia anunciou a subscrição de US$ 2 bilhões em ações ordinárias da CoreWeave e ampliou sua parceria de longo prazo. A CoreWeave planeja construir mais de 5 gigawatts em fábricas de IA com tecnologia da Nvidia até 2030, com os data centers correspondentes utilizando GPUs, equipamentos de rede e outras plataformas de computação da Nvidia. A Nvidia detém atualmente cerca de 47,2 milhões de ações da CoreWeave, representando uma participação próxima de 10%, o que a torna uma de suas principais acionistas. Ao mesmo tempo, a CoreWeave também é uma grande compradora de GPUs da Nvidia, operando sob um modelo de negócios baseado na compra de chips da Nvidia para construir clusters de computação e no aluguel dessa capacidade computacional para clientes como Meta e OpenAI. Isso significa que quaisquer obstáculos de financiamento enfrentados pela CoreWeave não apenas afetariam o valor da participação acionária da Nvidia, mas também poderiam desacelerar suas futuras compras de GPUs e a construção de data centers. Embora a Nvidia não garanta as dívidas da CoreWeave, esta última continua sendo um indicador crucial para observar se a demanda por chips de IA pode se traduzir em capacidade real de pagamento. O analista do Bank of America, Tal Liani, permanece otimista em relação à CoreWeave, estabelecendo um preço-alvo de US$ 140. Ele acredita que a Nvidia e a CoreWeave compartilham interesses alinhados: a CoreWeave necessita dos chips e do suporte técnico da Nvidia, enquanto a Nvidia quer que os grandes provedores de serviços de nuvem para IA continuem adotando suas GPUs, em vez de migrarem para a AMD ou outras plataformas concorrentes. Quanto a Nvidia será afetada? Demanda por IA permanece crucial A própria Nvidia possui uma escala operacional maior e uma base de lucratividade mais sólida, de modo que os riscos da CoreWeave não significam que a Nvidia sofrerá inevitavelmente um impacto de mesma magnitude. artigo.texto: Proposed 1-year moratorium on data centers, task force fails after Fort Wayne City Council vote FORT WAYNE, Ind. (WPTA) - Proposals for a one-year data center moratorium and a data center task force failed Tuesday, ending a contentious debate between Fort Wayne City Council members. BACKGROUND: Fort Wayne council member proposes one-year data center moratorium Councilwoman Rohli Booker introduced the proposals last month, which would have kept the city council from approving any new data center projects and created a comprehensive data center development standard. It would have stopped short of halting the existing Google data center project underway in southeast Fort Wayne. “If there was ever a perfect time to pause, it’s now,” Booker said ahead of the proposals failing in a 3-to-5 vote for the task force and a 4-to-4 vote for the moratorium. “We know that Fort Wayne has a lot to offer; we have water, we have infrastructure, we have economic development incentives, we have a state that has made it very clear that it wants these types of developments,” she said. “Indiana has practically put up a neon sign saying that ‘We are open for business.’” “I don’t think anyone is confused about that.” Councilman Russ Jehl also voted yes. He said he thinks a big reason why the resolutions weren’t passed is that the Department of Planning Services is now increasing its involvement. “The Department of Planning Services, whose job is to create some guardrails for land use, is finally getting a little bit in motion,” he said. Tonight’s meeting also had a big turnout from a local electrical workers’ union. Recently, members of the union posted on Facebook to express concerns about the moratorium’s potential impact on future jobs. “I think we finally saw some of the stakeholders, like the trades, come and say, ‘Oh, by the way, there are actually some tangible benefits, like my job being produced, and that there are a lot more jobs than the perception is,’” Jehl said. Councilwoman Michelle Chambers was one of the people voting no. She said some definitions in the moratorium were not specific, including the phrase “data centers.” “We cannot have such an open-ended definition,” she said. “We had to be very clear, so that we don’t have other data-driven organizations, corporations, be affected by a moratorium that was attempting to deal with what data centers do.” RELATED: Fort Wayne neighbors say Google data center noise, lights disrupt their lives | Story continues below previous coverage Councilman Nathan Hartman, who has consistently stated his opposition to the proposal, expressed concerns that it would create issues for developments such as schools and hospitals. “I’m still a no on this. I’m not convinced that this is good policy, and I feel like that this sends the wrong message to not just our community, but to our other partners throughout the state,” he said. artigo.texto: Data Center Developers Face Tighter Margins as Construction Costs Rise JLL says strong AI demand is not enough to protect projects lacking power certainty, anchor tenants, and credible delivery timelines. Data center developers may be able to pass higher construction costs on to tenants, but only when projects have power access, committed customers, and a credible path to delivery, according to JLL. In its Global Construction Costs Index 2026, the real estate services firm said annual construction cost escalation of 3% to 6% has become the new baseline, up from the 2% to 3% range common before 2020. JLL also forecasts another 3.1% to 4.2% increase in global tender prices in 2027, including 3.2% to 4.2% in North America. Those forecasts apply to construction broadly rather than the data center sector alone. The JLL report notes that rising rents and asset values have helped data center projects absorb some of that inflation. However, Matthew Giddings, executive director of technical services with JLL’s Data Centers and Critical Environments team, said stronger market fundamentals do not automatically protect individual projects. “The economics break down when costs outpace contracted revenue or power delays postpone income while financing costs continue to accumulate,” Giddings told Data Center Knowledge. “Higher asset values alone cannot close that gap.” That risk is most acute for speculative campuses without anchor tenants, projects with uncertain power delivery, and developments tied to fixed-rent agreements that leave little room to absorb construction escalation. Older facilities being repositioned for AI workloads may also face difficult economics if upgrades become too extensive. “Strong demand supports the market, but it does not make every project viable,” Giddings said. Developers should reassess projects when rising capital costs erode expected returns, utility schedules slip beyond committed occupancy dates, or tenant demand no longer supports planned capacity, he said. Reduced power availability and delays in anchor-tenant commitments are also signs that a project may need to be reworked. One way to manage that risk is through phased construction. By aligning spending with confirmed electricity supply and customer demand, developers can limit the amount of capital they commit before fundamentals are in place. Skilled Trades Constrain Delivery Labor constraints are adding to the pressure. Giddings said the electrical and mechanical trades are creating the greatest cost and schedule challenges, particularly electricians, high-voltage specialists, pipefitters, and advanced cooling technicians. “Controls, commissioning, and startup teams have also become critical bottlenecks, as their availability often determines when a completed facility can be placed into service,” he noted. Competition for utility and substation construction crews is also intensifying, adding risks that extend beyond the data center site itself. To reduce exposure, Giddings recommended that developers bring in trade partners early and test project schedules against real workforce availability rather than assumed labor capacity. He also pointed to standardized designs, off-site prefabrication, and phased construction as ways to reduce peak labor requirements. In remote markets, developers may need to offer housing, transportation, and travel incentives to attract workers. In the longer term, investment in trade schools, apprenticeships, and union training facilities could help support future construction phases while expanding local employment opportunities, he said. Buy Early Without Freezing the Design Procurement strategy is becoming just as important. Long lead times for critical equipment have pushed many developers to place orders earlier, but doing so can create problems if tenant requirements shift, particularly as AI infrastructure continues to evolve. “The key is to secure manufacturing capacity early without freezing every design decision,” Giddings said. He said developers should reserve production slots for transformers, switchgear, generators, and cooling equipment while negotiating flexibility to modify specifications before fabrication begins. Orders should advance in line with validated tenant requirements and clear decision deadlines. That approach is especially important as operators try to account for shifting rack densities and growing interest in liquid cooling. Modular power and cooling systems, built-in expansion capacity, and design provisions for liquid cooling can help facilities adapt without undermining the overall project. “Early procurement protects the schedule, while flexible design protects the long-term value of the asset,” Giddings said. Retrofitting older facilities can offer another path to faster delivery and lower upfront costs, particularly when a site already has available power, sufficient structural capacity, and infrastructure that can be reused. However, those advantages can disappear quickly if a building requires major mechanical upgrades, higher electrical distribution capacity, heavier floor loading, or large-scale liquid-cooling retrofits. “The economics ultimately depend on how much existing infrastructure can be retained while still meeting current and future performance requirements,” Giddings said.

artigo.texto: Fayette residents seek more stringent data center ordinance standards Several concerned Fayette County residents asked the county board of commissioners about planning commission recommendations they feared would weaken a proposed data center ordinance during Thursday’s regular monthly meeting. The ordinance would place restrictions on potential data center projects, including height and setback restrictions. Shelley Meyers of Dunbar Township said she was alarmed by changes in the most recent draft, which included higher decibel levels and reduced setback levels. “Would you want a data center in your backyard? We really need to be looking closely at this and protect our residents of Fayette County,” she said. Nate Ricketts, an organizer with the Mountain Watershed Association, relayed preliminary results from the association’s survey of area residents. So far, 80% of respondents have said there was “no comfortable distance” they could live from a data center. Setbacks from residential properties, previously at 1,000 feet, had been reduced to 600, Ricketts said. Setbacks from occupied residences had dropped as low as 500 feet. “We and many people in Fayette County thought that early drafts weren’t protective enough, but from a political perspective, to slash setbacks even more is a recipe for public scrutiny,” he said. Ohiopyle resident Annelise Carleton-Hug also backed the restoration of the 1,000-foot setback, which had been recommended as a best practice by a county commissioner from Virginia at a previous data center town hall. She would also like to see language added that would create more sustainable forms of energy generation, such as solar. “I realize we’re sitting on the shale here, but we could get more solar power to power these,” she said. “That would have less impact to future climate change and how that would further impact our community.” In response to public speakers, commissioners said they were not bound by what the planning commission had recommended. “We certainly want their input in it, but ultimately, it’s going to come down to what the commissioners decide,” Commissioner Harry “Dutch” Kaufman said after the meeting. “We’re going to review that … once that’s done, we will have a finished product that we can bring to a public meeting.” Commissioner Vince Vicites said he was “pushing very hard for stringent setbacks.” “Those aren’t etched in stone at this point,” he said. Chairman Scott Dunn agreed with the other commissioners, but said limits that were too strict could lead it to being deemed exclusionary zoning. “If our data center zoning is so much different than other industrial zoning, the data center can sue us in court,” he said. The first vote on the commissioner level would be to schedule a public hearing on the ordinance, a draft of which would be published before the hearing. Kaufman said they were planning to hold the scheduling vote in November. The actual public hearing would have to be at least 30 days later.

artigo.texto: Plataformas Broadcast Soluções de Dados e Conteúdos Soluções de Tecnologia 14 de outubro de 2026, às 15:16 A Cemig anunciou o lançamento de uma chamada pública de projetos de eficiência energética, voltada para atrair iniciativas de clientes da companhia que possibilitem a modernização de unidades consumidoras e propiciem a redução do desperdício ou a geração sustentável de energia elétrica. Foram disponibilizados neste ano cerca de R$ 150 milhões para apoiar as ações, divididos em sete tipologias: Industrial (R$ 40 milhões), Residencial – condomínios (R$ 35 milhões), Comércio e Serviços (R$ 25 milhões), Poder Público (R$ 15 milhões), Serviços Públicos (R$ 15 milhões), Rural (R$ 10 milhões) e Iluminação Pública (R$ 10 milhões). Cada proposta deve contemplar uma única tipologia e prever recursos do Programa de Eficiência Energética (PEE) entre R$ 300 mil e R$ 9 milhões. Segundo a Cemig, a novidade da edição de 2026 da chamada pública é a possibilidade de incluir sistemas de armazenamento de energia por baterias. Também são elegíveis ações de substituição de equipamentos por modelos mais eficientes em diversos usos finais, como iluminação, condicionamento ambiental, motores e refrigeração, além da instalação de geração por fontes incentivadas, como usinas solares fotovoltaicas. O prazo para submissão das propostas segue até 6 de novembro. Regras A chamada pública integra o Programa de Eficiência Energética da Cemig, regulado pela Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel). Com os projetos aprovados, a Cemig reembolsa as etapas executadas pelo proponente. Para entidades públicas e filantrópicas, o financiamento é feito a fundo perdido. Já as unidades consumidoras de natureza privada e sem fins assistenciais, como indústrias, comércios e condomínios, firmam contrato de desempenho, em que parte do valor retorna à Cemig em até cinco anos, pago com a própria economia de energia gerada pelo projeto. artigo.texto: Brasília - Um mês após se tornar lei, as incertezas em relação a quando o Redata de fato será implementado no país ainda permanecem. Dessa vez, a regulamentação do programa que dará incentivos fiscais a data centers brasileiros vem sendo adiada devido ao período eleitoral. Enquanto isso, o setor de data centers aguarda para viabilizar investimentos estimados em cerca de R$ 90 bilhões dentro de cinco anos a partir de 2027. Segundo informações obtidas pelo NeoFeed, a acirrada disputa presidencial nas urnas entre o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) tem travado na Casa Civil a publicação de um decreto previsto pelo governo para definir regras de funcionamento do Redata. Nas últimas semanas, uma série de medidas lançadas pelo Palácio do Planalto durante o processo eleitoral ganharam preferência natural na ordem de prioridades do governo, como a medida provisória que suspendeu as bets e a ampliação dos benefícios tributários para microempreendedores individuais (MEI). Além da forte mobilização encampada pelo governo em torno do fim da escala de trabalho 6x1, aprovada pelo Senado na quarta-feira, 14 de outubro, principal tema de interesse de Lula e do governo nas últimas semanas. O Ministério da Fazenda chegou a prometer o decreto com as regulamentações do Redata para o fim de setembro, como mostrou o NeoFeed. Até hoje, no entanto, isso não aconteceu e na prática o programa ainda não saiu do papel. Inicialmente, a principal razão para o adiamento foi uma divergência dentro do governo sobre se o gás natural também poderá ser usado como energia (além das fontes renováveis já previstas) para abastecer os datacenters. Enquanto os ministérios de Minas e Energia e o de Desenvolvimento, Indústria, Comércio e Serviços (MDIC) acenavam positivamente ao uso do gás para essa finalidade, já a Fazenda defende restrições e entende que apenas as fontes de energia limpas (hidrelétrica, eólica, solar) fossem usadas para abastecer as estruturas de data centers. Uma fonte que acompanha o assunto avalia que, apesar dessa indefinição, atualmente o que vem atrasando mais a regulamentação seria o momento político, em função das novas demandas do governo nas últimas semanas. Também está prevista a edição de uma portaria interministerial, além do decreto presidencial. As pastas do Meio Ambiente, de Comunicações e de Ciência e Tecnologia também têm participado das discussões, junto com a Fazenda, o MME e o MDIC. Mas a regulamentação do programa não dará um norte apenas para a questão energética. As regras sobre o Redata também precisam indicar a lista de quais componentes/equipamentos poderão receber os benefícios fiscais e quais documentos as empresas precisam apresentar para se cadastrar no programa. Nesta quinta-feira, 15 de outubro, 32 entidades empresariais e nove frentes parlamentares divulgaram uma carta aberta pedindo que o assunto seja destravado, intitulada "Presidente Lula, é hora de regulamentar o Redata". "A sanção foi um passo importante, mas a concretização dos investimentos depende de um decreto com regras claras e previsíveis para a implementação do regime", defende o documento. "Presidente Lula, regulamentar o Redata é transformar o potencial brasileiro em investimentos, empregos qualificados, inovação e soberania tecnológica e digital. O momento de regulamentar o Redata é agora!", segue o texto. A carta também enfatiza uma "abordagem tecnologicamente neutra", na defesa de diversas fontes de energia renováveis ou de baixa emissão, incluindo hidrelétrica, solar, eólica, biomassa, biogás, biometano, energia nuclear e gás natural. "Data centers operam 24 horas por dia e exigem energia firme, segura e confiável, sem transferência indevida de custos aos demais consumidores", prossegue. Por fim, o documento ainda sugere uma lista abrangente de bens elegíveis para acessar os benefícios do programa, alinhada às "condições atuais de oferta e com o fortalecimento da indústria nacional, além do avanço das discussões sobre o ICMS no Confaz, em diálogo com os Estados". Tatiana Ribeiro, secretária-executiva da Frente Parlamentar pelo Brasil Competitivo e diretora-executiva do Movimento Brasil Competitivo, defende que a regulamentação possa ser feita de forma "fatiada", caso o governo ainda não consiga decidir sobre a questão das fontes de energia, por exemplo. "Reforço a importância que isso consiga ser definido o quanto antes. O Brasil perdeu uma janela importante. Essa era uma medida que já devia ter sido aprovada no início do ano. E quando realmente houve esforço para que fosse destravado, isso agora fica parado na discussão de regulamentação", disse ela ao NeoFeed. Ela lembra que o Brasil já perdeu potenciais investimentos em data centers para países como Argentina e Índia. A executiva também entende que o período eleitoral pode ter impactado para atrasos nesse processo de regulamentação. "A gente teve dentre essas últimas semanas uma série de novas medidas [do governo] que foram apresentadas e acredito que isso pode ter tido impacto nessa regulamentação." Histórico A discussão em torno de uma lei para criar o Redata foi fruto de ampla discussão originada ainda em 2025. Após o governo propor o programa por medida provisória ainda no fim do ano passado, a proposta caducou em fevereiro de 2026 sem o Congresso votar. Daí em diante, um projeto de lei de autoria do então líder do governo na Câmara, José Guimarães (hoje ministro das Relações Institucionais), até foi aprovado pela Casa, mas ficou paralisado no Senado por meses. E apenas depois de uma reaproximação entre Lula e o presidente do Senado, Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP), que o PL foi aprovado em setembro. Além da proposta do Redata, porém, o Congresso ainda precisou aprovar um projeto de lei complementar para permitir incentivos fiscais ao governo. Na prática, essa lei também garantiu orçamento para programas como o Redata. Em função do longo período em que o projeto empacou no Legislativo, o governo até chegou a admitir

artigo.texto: O primeiro sistema de armazenamento de energia em baterias integrado a uma usina solar no Brasil iniciou os testes em Salvador, Bahia, sob autorização da Aneel. A iniciativa, realizada na usina Sol de Brotas 7 da Statkraft, permite guardar o sol do dia para usar à noite, aumentando a eficiência e valor dos ativos renováveis. Salvador, outubro de 2026. O início dos testes do primeiro sistema de armazenamento de energia em baterias (BESS) integrado a uma usina solar no Brasil representa um marco para a evolução do setor elétrico nacional. Instalado na usina solar Sol de Brotas 7, da Statkraft, na Bahia, o projeto combina geração fotovoltaica e armazenamento de energia, abrindo caminho para novos modelos de operação, maior flexibilidade da rede e uma gestão mais eficiente dos ativos renováveis. Para a Voltxs Energia, o avanço demonstra que o armazenamento deixa de ser apenas uma tecnologia promissora e passa a integrar as estratégias de desenvolvimento dos empreendimentos renováveis. À medida que a participação das fontes solar e eólica cresce na matriz elétrica brasileira, aumenta também a necessidade de soluções capazes de conferir maior previsibilidade, flexibilidade e eficiência à operação desses ativos. - Primeiro sistema de baterias (BESS) integrado a usina solar no Brasil inicia testes. - Projeto autorizado pela Aneel está localizado na usina Sol de Brotas 7, na Bahia. - Tecnologia permite armazenar energia gerada durante o dia para uso posterior. - A integração busca aumentar a flexibilidade e eficiência da rede elétrica nacional. - A Voltxs Energia destaca que a gestão inteligente dos ativos ganha novo status estratégico. Matheus Ivanoski Teixeira, Diretor de Operações (COO) da Voltxs Energia, afirma que o início do projeto representa um passo importante para a maturidade do mercado brasileiro de armazenamento de energia. Ele destaca que o BESS deixa de ser apenas um tema de planejamento e passa a ser validado na prática como um componente estratégico. A combinação entre geração fotovoltaica e armazenamento amplia as possibilidades de gestão da energia produzida e prepara o setor para uma matriz cada vez mais dinâmica. Armazenamento passa a integrar a estratégia dos ativos Os sistemas BESS permitem armazenar a energia gerada em momentos de maior produção e disponibilizá-la quando houver necessidade operacional ou maior demanda do sistema elétrico. Na avaliação da Voltxs, o principal ganho está na integração entre geração, armazenamento e gestão inteligente dos ativos. Teixeira explica que, ao analisar um projeto híbrido, não se fala apenas da instalação de baterias. O grande diferencial está na capacidade de integrar geração, armazenamento e inteligência operacional para extrair mais eficiência dos ativos. Essa visão tende a se tornar cada vez mais relevante para investidores, operadores e proprietários de usinas. Segundo o executivo, os primeiros projetos em operação terão papel fundamental para fornecer dados reais sobre desempenho, dimensionamento, custos, retorno econômico e aplicações do armazenamento em diferentes cenários. Mercado entra em uma nova fase O avanço também reforça uma tendência observada internacionalmente: a evolução das usinas renováveis para plataformas energéticas mais inteligentes. Essas plataformas são capazes de combinar diferentes tecnologias e responder de forma mais eficiente às necessidades do sistema elétrico. Na avaliação da Voltxs, essa transformação deve impulsionar novos modelos de negócios, ampliar a competitividade dos empreendimentos renováveis e acelerar investimentos em soluções de armazenamento nos próximos anos. Teixeira destaca que os projetos pioneiros serão importantes para definir as melhores estratégias de utilização do armazenamento no Brasil. O aprendizado obtido nessa fase permitirá desenvolver modelos mais eficientes tanto do ponto de vista operacional quanto econômico. A tendência é que a gestão integrada dos ativos passe a ser um diferencial competitivo para o setor. Além dos benefícios operacionais, a integração entre geração fotovoltaica e armazenamento fortalece a discussão sobre a modernização da infraestrutura elétrica brasileira, criando condições para uma matriz energética mais flexível, resiliente e preparada para a expansão das fontes renováveis.

artigo.texto: Desenvolve SP e Möbius criam FIDC de R$ 70 milhões para financiar data centers Fundo terá como foco provedores regionais de internet e operadores de data centers de pequeno porte, especialmente em cidades do interior com menor oferta de conectividade e serviços tecnológicos A Desenvolve SP e a gestora Möbius Capital estão lançando um fundo de investimento em direitos creditórios (FIDC) de R$ 70 milhões para financiar empresas de infraestrutura digital no Estado de São Paulo. O fundo terá como foco provedores regionais de internet e operadores de data centers de pequeno porte, especialmente em cidades do interior com menor oferta de conectividade e serviços tecnológicos. A agência de fomento paulista subscreverá R$ 50 milhões em cotas seniores, equivalentes a 71,4% do patrimônio previsto para o FIDC, enquanto a Möbius ficará com R$ 20 milhões em cotas subordinadas, ou 28,6% do total. Na estrutura, as cotas subordinadas absorvem primeiro eventuais perdas da carteira, funcionando como uma camada de proteção para as cotas seniores, que têm prioridade no recebimento de amortizações e rendimentos, conforme as regras do fundo. Assim, a gestora assume a primeira parcela do risco de crédito das operações, enquanto a Desenvolve SP ocupa a posição prioritária na distribuição dos recursos. O fundo poderá antecipar recebíveis de clientes dos provedores de internet, tanto pessoas físicas quanto jurídicas, além de financiar a aquisição de equipamentos e projetos de expansão da infraestrutura tecnológica. Também estão previstas operações relacionadas à compra e à fusão de empresas, em um mercado que passa por um processo de consolidação. A Möbius foi selecionada em chamada pública da Desenvolve SP voltada a FIDCs e fundos de investimento em participações (FIPs). Segundo Roberto Savaris, sócio e fundador da gestora, a casa já atua no financiamento de aquisições de provedores de internet e na estruturação de operações no mercado de capitais para empresas do setor. A proposta passou por análise de elegibilidade, diligência e aprovação pelo comitê de investimentos da agência de fomento. Para Ricardo Brito, diretor-presidente da Desenvolve SP, a operação busca ampliar o acesso ao crédito para negócios inovadores por meio da combinação de capital público e privado. “Por meio do ‘blended finance’, conseguimos atrair investimento privado, potencializar o impacto do recurso público e alcançar mais empreendedores”, afirmou.

artigo.texto: Flatiron Energy has secured about $850 million in construction and term financing commitments for the Energizar Battery Project in Chelsea, Massachusetts. This project puts Massachusetts at the spotlight as a leader in renewable energy project development in the US. Significance of the Project The standalone energy storage project will be the largest on the East Coast and one of the largest urban battery energy storage systems globally, designed at 1,200 MWh. Timeline Commercial operations for the Energizar project are pegged for the fourth quarter of 2027. This timeline was said by Flatiron Energy. Additionally, once online, the facility will provide critical peaking capacity and reliability resources for the Boston metropolitan area grid, helping to offset local reliance on fossil-fuel-fired generation. What will the Financing Commitments Used for? The financing commitments span construction and bridge loan facilities, term loan facilities, letter of credit facilities, a preferred equity commitment, and a tax credit transfer commitment. The debt facilities were provided by a consortium of financial institutions, with Nord/LB, Santander, and Societe Generale serving as coordinating lead arrangers; Investec and East West Bank acting as joint lead arrangers; and Siemens Financial Services participating as a lender. East West Bank served as depositary, while Santander acted as administrative agent. A premier global credit asset manager with more than $350 billion in assets under management provided the preferred equity commitment, and two Fortune 500 corporations committed to transfer a portion of the project’s investment tax credits (ITCs). Orrick, Herrington & Sutcliffe LLP and Foley Hoag LLP represented Flatiron Energy. Winston & Strawn LLP and Rath, Young and Pignatelli, P.C. represented the lenders. Lastly, CCA Capital LLC advised Flatiron on the preferred equity investment and tax credit transfer. On the other hand, Riverside Risk Advisors acted as hedge advisor to Flatiron for interest rate hedging activities. Lastly, Raymond James Renewable Energy Investments advised the tax credit purchasers. Project Factsheet Project Name:Energizar Developer: Flatiron Energy Location: Chelsea, Massachusetts (Boston Metropolitan Area) Significance: Largest standalone battery storage system on the U.S. East Coast; one of the largest urban installations globally. Commercial Operations (COD): Expected Q4 2027 Technical Specifications - Energy Capacity: 1,200 MWh - Type: Standalone Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) - Primary Function: Grid peaking capacity, regional power reliability, and reducing reliance on local fossil-fuel power generation. Financing Structure - Total Financing: $850 Million - Instruments: Construction & bridge loans, term loans, letters of credit, preferred equity, and tax credit transfers. - Debt Lenders: Consortium led by Nord/LB, Santander, and Societe Generale (Coordinating Lead Arrangers); Investec and East West Bank (Joint Lead Arrangers); Siemens Financial Services (Lender). - Preferred Equity: Provided by a global credit asset manager ($350B+ AUM). - Tax Credit Transfers: Committed by two Fortune 500 corporations. Key Advisors Legal Counsel - Borrower Counsel (Flatiron Energy): Orrick, Herrington & Sutcliffe LLP; Foley Hoag LLP - Lender Counsel: Winston & Strawn LLP; Rath, Young and Pignatelli, P.C. Financial and Risk Advisors: - CCA Capital LLC (Preferred equity & tax credit transfer) - Riverside Risk Advisors (Interest rate hedging)

artigo.texto: Phoenix is stationing inspectors at Menlo Digital’s Ahwatukee data center construction site in the early morning and has secured a series of commitments from the contractor to reduce noise and other disturbances following complaints from nearby residents. The measures include moving construction traffic farther from homes, restricting early-morning deliveries, relocating employee parking and monitoring noise levels around the property. In an Oct. 9 email to residents, Mike Baxley, assistant director of the city's Planning and Development Department, said the city met with the construction management team and a representative of the project's ownership to address neighborhood concerns. “As with all construction projects, there is a certain amount of noise that the activity of construction will create,” he wrote. “The contractor has committed to taking steps to minimize these aspects of those types of issues.” Baxley’s email was the city’s latest reaction to months of complaints by residents about construction noise, bright lighting and work they contend was occurring outside legally permitted hours at the million-square-foot Menlo Digital data center campus near 48th Street and Thistle Landing Drive. "Earlier today we were able to have a meeting with the onsite management team and a representative of ownership for the Thistle Landing project to identify ways to soften the challenges that neighbors are facing with this project," Baxley wrote. His email also came days before two developments are set this week, one involving the Menlo project and the other data centers generally. On Friday, Oct. 16, construction hours return to a wintertime schedule, with crews permitted to work outside only between 7 a.m. and 7 p.m. Monday to Friday unless they secure a special permit from the city Planning and Development Department City Planning Director Joshua Bednarik several weeks ago told residents in an email his department will not give the Menlo Digital data campus company such a permit. From 5-6:30 p.m. today, Oct. 14, Attorney General Kris Mayes will hold a town hall on data centers at The Eagles Community Center, 828 E. Broadway Road, Mesa. “The AG is not investigating the Ahwatukee data center approval,” said Richie Taylor, the attorney general’s communications director. “She is holding a townhall to hear directly from residents about their concerns after receiving multiple complaints from the community.” Mayes subsequently broadened the the town hall's scope to data centers generally. The most significant immediate change outlined by Baxley involves city inspectors. "Starting today, I have asked our Inspections team to have after hours inspectors onsite, in the morning, each work day to ensure that no activity takes place prior to legal start times through the end of the state mandated early construction" period, he wrote. "My hope is that this will ensure compliance and allow the neighbors not to have to worry about having to call in a complaint as we will already have an inspector there to handle any infraction of the mandated start times." The decision represents a more direct approach to monitoring construction activity than relying solely on complaints from neighbors. However, Baxley's email does not indicate that the city has determined any violations occurred. He said his staff is investigating complaints filed Sept. 12, 24, 25, 26 and Oct. 2 to establish what happened and whether enforcement action was warranted. "We use a call service that logs the complaints and notifies the on-call inspector that day," Baxley wrote. "Once I get more information on the complaints for these dates I can respond further as to what the determination of the complaints were and if any action was necessary." The latest development comes as the controversial data center project continues to face opposition from nearby residents, who have raised concerns about its potential effects on their neighborhood. Much of the broader dispute has centered on the facility's anticipated operations, including questions about noise, electricity consumption and other environmental and health impacts. Construction itself quickly evolved as a separate source of friction, particularly for residents living closest to the site. Craig Evans, president of the Ahwatukee Community Alliance, a nonprofit opponents formed to fight the facility, was not impressed by Baxley's message. "It didn’t seem to mean much," he said. "As far as the City of Phoenix seems concerned, the citizens that do most of the living, working and dying in Ahwatukee...aren't all that important to the permitting process. "Disruption to the peace and tranquility of our homes seems an acceptable sacrifice to the City of Phoenix once a permit is issued." "Quite frankly Mr. Baxley should be standing in our neighborhood in the small hours making his own recordings and protecting our interests, rather we suspect his are just the latest effort to discount and dismiss the concerns and suffering the City’s decisions have already inflicted on Ahwatukee." Evans then lashed out at the city process that got the neighbors in the position they're now in. Baxley's email outlines several changes the contractor has agreed to make. Through Oct. 15, when early construction hours are scheduled to end, the contractor has committed not to open the project's gates or turn on construction lighting before the legally permitted start time. Coloque a eixos nas suas fontes preferidas do Google Veja nossas notícias com mais destaque nas suas buscas. Apontada como um dos principais entraves para que projetos de reflorestamento e de Redução das Emissões por Desmatamento e Degradação Florestal (Redd+) consigam acessar linhas de financiamento, a modelagem dos contratos passará a ter um padrão, que está em desenvolvimento pelo Nature Investment Lab (NIL). A minuta desse contrato modelo foi apresentada publicamente durante a Semana do Clima que aconteceu recentemente em Nova York e, para elaborá-la, o NIL conversou com 25 importantes instituições. Entre elas, Itaú BBA, Regia Capital, Systemica, Petrobras e Regreen. No próximo passo, o rascunho do contrato modelo será colocado em audiência pública e deve ganhar destaque durante a COP31, que acontecerá entre os dias 9 e 20 de novembro na Turquia. A meta é concluir o trabalho até o final deste ano. O NIL aposta no processo de amadurecimento desse mercado, que já vem durando mais de 20 anos e que deverá elevar o carbono ao status de commodity, com possibilidade de ser negociado internacionalmente. “A ideia é preparar os desenvolvedores dos projetos de produção de carbono para que consigam lidar com todas as exigências com as quais vão se deparar quando tentarem acessar recursos”, explica Fabiana Philipi, gerente de projetos da Climate Ventures, organização que lidera o NIL. Ela pondera, no entanto, que o documento de referência poderá ajudar os outros players desse mercado, como os compradores e financiadores do mercado de carbono. Segundo Philipi, as propostas de produção de carbono bem elaboradas têm forte demanda e o objetivo é ajudar desenvolvedores de todos os portes, desde empresas já consagradas como Re.Green e Mombak, até aquelas que estão dando os primeiros passos. As maiores compradoras dos créditos de carbono brasileiros, atualmente, são as big techs, principalmente a Microsoft. A minuta apresentada em Nova York refere-se a contratos offtake — compra mínima garantida — que são acordos jurídicos firmados entre comprador e vendedor de uma mercadoria, antes dela entrar em produção. O documento apresenta cláusulas referentes à estrutura comercial, como preço, pagamento e financiamento, garantias, recebíveis e financiadores, ciclo de vida dos créditos, entrega e titularidade, falha de entrega, entre outros. O NIL é um laboratório de investimentos criado a partir de uma iniciativa que reúne o Banco do Brasil, o Instituto Itaúsa, o Instituto Clima e Sociedade (iCS), o Banco Nacional de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Social (BNDES) e a internacional Gfanz. O seu objetivo é atrair e estruturar financiamentos, além de promover inovação financeira, para ampliar a chamada economia de Soluções Baseadas na Natureza (NBS, em inglês). Por Cristina Canas

artigo.texto: Global energy storage targets for 2030 have nearly tripled since the adoption of the COP29 Global Energy Storage and Grids Pledge, reaching 822 GW. However, the combined national commitments remain approximately 45% below the 1,500 GW target established under the international agreement, according to a new analysis by energy think tank Ember. The report highlights a significant increase in global energy storage ambitions, with the combined 2030 targets of 99 countries and the European Union rising by 190%, or approximately 2.9 times, compared with levels assessed during COP29. Despite this progress, national commitments remain below both the global pledge and BloombergNEF’s market forecast, which projects approximately 1,200 GW of battery storage deployment alone by 2030. According to Ember, the increase in storage targets has been driven predominantly by China and the European Union, while most other countries have maintained their existing commitments or have yet to establish dedicated energy storage targets. China has emerged as the largest contributor to the increase in global storage ambitions. Under its 15th Five-Year Plan, the country raised its 2030 energy storage target by 330 GW, from 130 GW to 460 GW. The revised target covers new-type energy storage technologies, primarily batteries, alongside pumped hydro storage. Meanwhile, the European Union established its first bloc-wide energy storage target in June 2026, setting a goal of 200 GW by 2030. Together, China and the EU now account for more than 80% of the combined national storage targets worldwide. Dr Katye Altieri, Global Program Consultant at Ember, noted that the increase in global storage ambition has been concentrated in these two major economies. She emphasised that several leading solar markets have yet to establish storage targets, potentially limiting investment certainty and long-term market development. The analysis also indicates that actual energy storage deployment is advancing considerably faster than national policy commitments. Annual battery storage additions have increased by nearly 80% per year since 2020, significantly exceeding the growth rate required to achieve the COP29 pledge. Global energy storage installations reached a record 118 GW in 2025. Ember estimates that maintaining this annual deployment rate through 2030 would be sufficient to meet the current combined national targets, highlighting the gap between market activity and government policy ambitions. The report further identifies a strong relationship between solar power expansion and energy storage commitments. Countries with ambitious solar capacity targets generally demonstrate stronger energy storage ambitions, although several major solar markets remain exceptions. Among the world’s 20 largest solar markets, eight countries have not established specific energy storage targets for 2030. These include the United States, Germany, and Saudi Arabia, despite their ongoing investments in large-scale battery storage infrastructure. The United States has already installed approximately 52 GW of utility-scale battery storage capacity, while Saudi Arabia has recently connected what Ember describes as the world’s largest single battery storage project. However, other markets, including Poland, Austria, Switzerland, and Brazil, continue to lag in both storage target-setting and deployment. Ember emphasised that rapid market growth does not eliminate the importance of national storage targets. While battery storage projects are progressing in several major economies, deployment remains concentrated in a limited number of markets. Clear national targets can help address regulatory barriers, improve investment confidence, support grid planning, and strengthen coordination between renewable energy development and energy storage infrastructure. The analysis also connects the importance of storage expansion with upcoming international electrification commitments. Ahead of COP31, Türkiye’s presidency is promoting the proposed 35-by-35 Global Electrification Pledge, which aims to increase electricity’s share of final energy demand from approximately 20% to 35% by 2035. According to Ember, achieving these electrification objectives will require substantial investment in renewable electricity generation, modernised transmission and distribution networks, and sufficient energy storage capacity to manage rising electricity demand. The findings underscore the growing importance of battery energy storage systems and other flexibility technologies in supporting global renewable energy integration, improving electricity grid reliability, and accelerating the transition toward low-carbon energy systems. While energy storage deployment continues to accelerate worldwide, Ember’s assessment indicates that stronger and more geographically diversified national commitments will be necessary to align government policies with the COP29 target of 1,500 GW by 2030. Chega ao Brasil teste de urina que pode revelar em 10 minutos sinais ligados ao Alzheimer
Tecnologia disponibilizada pela Biocon Diagnósticos identifica biomarcadores associados à doença a partir de uma amostra de urina e surge como alternativa para auxiliar no rastreamento da saúde cognitiva
Uma amostra de urina e cerca de dez minutos de espera. Uma nova tecnologia disponível no Brasil promete tornar mais simples o rastreamento de alterações associadas à doença de Alzheimer, condição que pode começar a provocar mudanças no organismo muitos anos antes do aparecimento dos primeiros sintomas.
Chamado Demência Rapid Test, o exame é disponibilizado no país pela Biocon Diagnósticos e utiliza imunocromatografia para detectar na urina a proteína precursora amiloide (APP) e fragmentos relacionados à beta-amiloide (Aβ), proteínas associadas aos processos biológicos envolvidos na doença de Alzheimer.
O procedimento é simples. A amostra de urina é aplicada no dispositivo e o resultado pode ser visualizado em aproximadamente dez minutos. O produto é destinado ao uso profissional e possui registro na Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária (Anvisa).
Para Giulia Campanha de Freitas Lino, diretora Internacional da Biocon Diagnósticos, tecnologias mais acessíveis podem ajudar a mudar a maneira como a saúde cerebral é acompanhada.
"A ciência avança para um futuro onde monitorar a saúde do cérebro será tão simples quanto medir a pressão arterial", afirmou a executiva ao abordar a chegada da tecnologia.
Alzheimer pode começar anos antes dos sintomas
Um dos desafios da doença de Alzheimer é justamente o período silencioso. Alterações biológicas podem ocorrer no organismo muitos anos antes de problemas de memória e outras manifestações cognitivas se tornarem perceptíveis.
A beta-amiloide está entre as proteínas mais estudadas nesse processo. Seu acúmulo no cérebro é um dos principais marcadores biológicos relacionados à doença.
Segundo Giulia, o Brasil ainda enfrenta o desafio do diagnóstico tardio. "Em grande parte dos casos, o diagnóstico ocorre apenas quando os sintomas já estão instalados", afirma.
A possibilidade de identificar sinais de alerta antes dessa fase abre espaço para uma investigação médica mais precoce e para o acompanhamento da saúde cognitiva.
Tecnologia foi estudada em mais de 5 mil pessoas
Uma das bases científicas da tecnologia é um estudo publicado em 2025 no Journal of Alzheimer's Disease. Os pesquisadores investigaram fragmentos da proteína precursora beta-amiloide presentes na urina e avaliaram populações da China e da Austrália.
O trabalho reuniu mais de 5 mil participantes em diferentes grupos. Os resultados apontaram potencial dos biomarcadores urinários como ferramenta para auxiliar na identificação de comprometimento cognitivo e demência.
Os próprios pesquisadores, porém, ressaltam a necessidade de novos estudos e acompanhamento de longo prazo para ampliar as evidências sobre a utilização desses biomarcadores.
Resultado positivo não si

A Ucrânia afirmou que seus militares tiveram o acesso à internet via satélite Starlink restringido repentinamente na noite desta terça-feira (13/10), comprometendo operações de combate. A interrupção afetou equipamentos utilizados pelas Forças Armadas ucranianas e ocorreu em meio aos ataques russos com mísseis balísticos.
Segundo Kiev, os serviços de inteligência dos Estados Unidos também não emitiram alertas sobre a ofensiva russa, uma prática que vinha ocorrendo desde o começo do confronto. Os terminais Starlink, administrados pela SpaceX do bilionário Elon Musk, são fundamentais para as comunicações militares ucranianas.
“Nossas Forças Armadas não receberam nenhum aviso sobre essas restrições e isso levou ao fracasso de várias missões”, declarou Serhiy Beskrestnov, assessor de tecnologia militar do presidente ucraniano Volodymyr Zelensky. Segundo ele, a interrupção não foi acidental.
A denúncia ocorre em meio ao acordo firmado entre Washington e Moscou envolvendo a exportação do diesel russo e às pressões do governo Trump para que Kiev interrompa ataques de longo alcance contra a indústria petrolífera da Rússia.
A Comissão Europeia afirmou nesta quarta-feira (14/10) que não dispõe de informações indicando que os Estados Unidos tenham suspendido o compartilhamento de inteligência com a Ucrânia.
Já o secretário-geral da Organização do Tratado do Atlântico Norte (Otan), Mark Rutte, rejeitou as especulações: “esse compartilhamento de inteligência não parou”, declarou em coletiva de imprensa na Estônia.
Nesta quarta-feira (14/10), um novo ataque de drones atingiu um datacenter do banco estatal russo Sberbank, em construção na cidade de Balakovo, região de Saratov, às margens do rio Volga. A instituição informou que seus sistemas bancários continuavam operando normalmente e que nenhum funcionário ficou ferido.
Apesar da declaração, usuários de diferentes regiões da Rússia relataram interrupções nos serviços do Sberbank, incluindo sua plataforma de inteligência artificial GigaChat. A partir das 22h desta terça-feira, a Agência Federal de Transporte Aéreo da Rússia (Rosaviatsia) suspendeu temporariamente pousos e decolagens nos quatro aeroportos de Moscou.
O prefeito da cidade, Sergei Sobyanin, afirmou que a maior parte dos 493 drones detectados sobre a região da capital foi neutralizada, incluindo 180 que se aproximavam diretamente da região.
O datacenter integra um dos maiores projetos de infraestrutura digital da Rússia e foi anunciado como um dos maiores centros de processamento de dados da Europa, com conclusão programada para 2030. A instalação também deverá abrigar o maior supercomputador do país, cuja entrada em operação estava prevista para 2027.
A ofensiva ocorre após três outros ataques contra os datacenters da Yandex, empresa russa responsável por um dos principais mecanismos de busca do país e por diferentes serviços digitais.
Nesta terça-feira (13/10), o porta-voz do Kremlin, Dmitri Peskov, confirmou que o governo discutia as consequênci

artigo.texto: South Korea plans to launch the Global Verified Carbon Market (GVCM) in 2027 to facilitate trading in carbon credits generated by overseas greenhouse gas reduction projects. The system will classify credits according to host-country approval, use blockchain to record key project information and rely on the Korea Exchange (KRX) for trading. The government is also considering digital-asset-based credit issuance and links with its domestic emissions trading scheme. Key Overview - Launch target: 2027. - Market: Global Verified Carbon Market (GVCM). - Trading platform: Korea Exchange (KRX). - Credit categories: GVCM A and GVCM NA. - Technology: Blockchain-based records of key project and emissions-reduction information. - Future options: Digital-asset issuance and possible links with South Korea’s domestic emissions trading scheme. - International cooperation: Participation by other countries and potential conversion of selected World Bank and Green Climate Fund project outcomes into GVCM credits. South Korea Prepares to Launch an International Carbon Market South Korea is preparing to establish an international marketplace for carbon credits generated through overseas greenhouse gas reduction projects, with full operations targeted for 2027. The initiative, called the Global Verified Carbon Market (GVCM), is designed to support the issuance and trading of credits while addressing concerns about the credibility and consistency of carbon markets. The government discussed the detailed implementation plan at a ministerial meeting on international economic affairs on 12 October 2026, chaired by Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Economy and Finance Lee Hyung-il. Under the proposed system, verified emissions-reduction outcomes from overseas projects will be converted into carbon credits that can be traded through the Korea Exchange. Depending on the relevant approvals, the credits could support corporate environmental activities and certain regulatory obligations, including national climate targets. The initiative represents a move beyond a market limited to voluntary corporate offsetting. The government has replaced the earlier name, Global Voluntary Carbon Market, with Global Verified Carbon Market to reflect the broader intended uses of eligible credits. Two Credit Categories Will Determine How Credits Can Be Used A central feature of the framework is the distinction between credits approved for international transfer by the host country and those without that approval. Credits classified as GVCM A will be eligible for specified compliance uses, including contributions towards the investing country’s nationally determined contribution (NDC) and compliance with international aviation requirements under the Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA). They may also support corporate environmental, social and governance activities. Credits classified as GVCM NA will initially be restricted to voluntary corporate environmental activities. Their permitted uses could expand if the host country subsequently grants the required transfer approval. This distinction matters because approval by the country hosting a carbon-reduction project affects whether the resulting credits can be used towards international climate commitments. It also provides a basis for separating credits intended for voluntary claims from those eligible for specified compliance purposes. The two categories of carbon credits are therefore central to the proposed market’s structure and the conditions under which buyers can use the credits they acquire. Blockchain Records to Support Credit Credibility South Korea plans to use blockchain technology to strengthen the traceability of carbon credits. Key information, including project operators and emissions-reduction volumes, will be recorded on the blockchain to help establish a more transparent record of the credits issued. The system is intended to improve confidence in transactions in a market where the credibility of claimed emissions reductions has been a longstanding concern. Better access to project information can help participants track the origins and reported outcomes of credits. The government also plans to use the Korea Exchange as the trading platform. The approach combines blockchain-based information management with an established exchange infrastructure for trading the credits. However, blockchain records alone cannot guarantee that a project has delivered the emissions reductions it claims. The effectiveness of the framework will also depend on project assessment, reliable measurement and verification, and compliance with the applicable approval requirements. Context is everything. Digital-Asset Issuance and Domestic Market Links Under Review Beyond the initial trading framework, South Korea is considering whether carbon credits could eventually be issued in digital-asset form. This remains under review rather than a confirmed feature of the initial launch. The government will need to consider the relevant legal framework, market conditions and the reliability of the proposed infrastructure before deciding how digital-asset issuance might operate. It is also examining whether GVCM credits could be linked to the domestic emissions trading scheme and greenhouse gas target management system, subject to the necessary conditions. Such a link could create additional uses for eligible credits, although the proposal has not yet been confirmed as an operational arrangement.
